title: The Same River
note: After Hans's Heraclitus quote (No man ever steps in the same river twice): a meandering river channel whose course migrates over time, advecting silt particles on fading trails; the current never repeats. Watch first, drag to step in and bend the current into eddies, tap to turn the river over.

title: Coins With the Wrong King
note: After study #202 (Mohamed Bourouissa), prompt MB6: discs fall like slow leaves, flip gold to silver on landing and stack in a neat row; the oldest lifts off when the row fills. Watch first, drag a falling disc to hurry or slow it, drag a stacked disc to toss it back. (Face glyph abstracted to ring vs star-burst, no faces.)

title: The Worried Note
note: After study #203 (Arthur Jafa), prompt AJ1: a single mark plays a nonmetronomic phrase, fast, freeze, replay, slow, freeze, never the same twice; replays leave ghost trails. Watch first, drag grabs the mark but the stutter continues, drag a ghost to erase it.

title: The X-Ray Rowhouse
note: After study #204 (Elissa Blount Moorhead), prompt EM1: five dark house outlines hold wandering light-marks; one house at a time is the bright focus, cycling every 20-40 seconds. Watch first, drag a house to hold its focus, drag a light-mark to move it inside its house.

title: Metaballs
note: Animated metaballs on paper: wandering field sources merge and split as thick black outlines, watch first, drag to add a field source, tap to reseed.

title: Making New Friends
note: Uploaded Procedural IK Cyber-Insect Simulation, as uploaded by Hans: live IK arthropod engine with FABRIK legs, cubic Bezier steps, rotational prediction, panic steps, spring antennae, and a Crimson-Centipede metachronal species.

title: Marble Atlas
note: A procedurally assembled chain reaction across four worlds. Row, climb, swing and roll between connected machines: docking bridges, pressure keys, tipping decks and earned gate releases. Original reactive piano; no final frame.

title: The Last Light
note: A glass ember wakes a forgotten foundry, flowers in a sunlit glasshouse, and constellations beneath a moonlit observatory. One marble, three living chapters, 21 real kinetic acts, endlessly reimagined.

title: Smoke From Nowhere
note: After the Modern Rogue smoke trick: a match strikes low, the flame dies, and the smoke it leaves behind is the piece — curling plumes that bloom, drift, and dissolve, never the same shape twice. Drag to stir the smoke.

title: Five Up, Turn
note: After Salvo Stassi: five balls on a juggler who travels the space, turns full 360s under high throws, kicks balls blind off the foot, and crosses into mills mess.

title: Two Tables, One Marble
note: One red glass marble crosses two tables in a single take: track curves, a rainbow domino line, a blue spinner gate, a seesaw, a gap, and a drop into a star-marked box.

title: Binary
note: A clock told in flipping discs: brass for a lit bit, a ghost ring for a dark one. When the seconds roll over, the flip ripples left through minutes and hours. Tap to hide the digits.

title: The Juggler
note: After Luther Bangert: a juggler in black on a warm stage, five white balls in a true cascade. The hands do the real work — catch wide, scoop low, throw from inside. Watch only.

title: Inkwell
note: Ink dropped in dark water: slow blooms open, curl, and dissolve on a seamless loop. Watch only.

title: Linkwork III
note: Third study after the forged wall sculpture, rebuilt from the chain: crisp rectangular links flowing horizontally, each passing alternately over and under its neighbours. A slow ripple travels the chain; double-tap re-forges it.

title: Linkwork II
note: Second study after the forged wall sculpture: a denser, more tangled cluster of bronze and blackened-steel links. A slow light sweep crosses the metal; double-tap re-forges it.

title: Linkwork
note: After the forged wall sculpture: interlocking bronze and blackened-steel links, hand-hammered, each at its own depth. A slow light sweep crosses the metal; double-tap re-forges it.

title: Pinwheel Quilt II
note: Closer to the hand-drawn original: portrait lattice, stronger swirl, wilder warp. A seamless loop; double-tap re-sews it.

title: Pinwheel Quilt
note: Ink pinwheels on a warped lattice, after a hand-drawn quilt. A seamless loop; double-tap re-sews it.

title: Perigee
note: One closed harmonograph orbit, one traveler. A seamless loop.

title: Gossamer
note: Verlet silk on a slow wind field. Drag to disturb it.

title: Cipher
note: Code-drawn glyphs orbit in concentric rings at different speeds. Drag to stir; double-tap to reseed.

title: Ember Knot
note: Luminous particles stream along a torus knot on near-black, colored like cooling embers. Drag to orbit; double-tap to reset.

title: Interference
note: Overlapping wave fields drawn as a breathing field of ink dots on paper. Drag to drop a stone; double-tap for new waves.

title: Rhizome
note: A root network that grows, prunes itself, and is reborn in breathing seasons. Drag to bend the growth; double-tap to reseed.

title: Split Tide
note: A recursive subdivision that breathes on a seamless loop. Drag to scrub time.

title: Crosscurrent
note: Two ink currents cross an evolving flow field. Drag to stir, double-tap to reseed.

title: Shear
note: Diagonal bars and wedges on a leaning energy band. Tap to flip.

title: Fission
note: Recursive subdivision grid, splitting and healing. Tap to divide.

title: Murmur
note: Luminous particles coalesce into a glowing ring, hold, and dissolve. A seamless loop.

title: Undertow
note: Luminous particles ride a curl-noise current on near-black, drawing the undertow itself.

title: Afterglow
note: Blazing sunset sky over dark silhouette land, thick palette-knife bands, after Jason Anderson.

title: Swell
note: Thick impasto seascape: foam-white horizon over deep teal water, after Jason Anderson.

title: Concrete
note: Hard-edge geometric shapes on a strict grid, slowly reconfiguring. Tap to rearrange.

title: Impasto
note: Thick palette-knife color blocks in a stained-glass jigsaw, after Jason Anderson.

title: Shimmer
note: Dashed rings interfere until the field seems to move; one ring burns vermilion. Click for another shimmer.

title: Compass
note: Needles lean with a seeded weather of direction; the vertical ones turn rust. Click for another compass.

title: Quarter Turn
note: Coin-flip tiles chain their arcs into paths nobody drew. Click for another quarter turn.

title: Warp
note: A checkerboard bulging under two crossing waves. Click for another warp.

title: Hatch
note: One family of lines, swelling and thinning around a hidden light. Click for another hatch.

title: Raster
note: A strict dot grid sized by two rings arguing. Click for another raster.

title: Well
note: Squares turn a little further as they shrink, down a twisting shaft. Click for another well.

title: Solstice
note: A low vermilion sun, warm rays up and cool rays down. Click for another solstice.

title: Orchard
note: Packed canopies from above, big trees first, fruit in rust. Click for another orchard.

title: Alluvium
note: River mouths spill fans of sediment that overlap and settle over each other. Click for another alluvium.

title: Meridian
note: Meridians bend around slow vortices; the strays burn warmer. Click for another meridian.

title: Silt
note: Layers of earth settle, darken with depth, and slip once along a pale seam. Click for another silt.

title: Undertow
note: Rings bent by a slow current crowd into dark bands. Click for another undertow.

title: Faultline
note: The curves are banned: hard turns, bold faults, sudden slips. Click for another fault.

title: Grainfield
note: Twenty-five thousand dots settle where the current bends. Click for another field.

title: Loom
note: Threads strung on nested rings, pulled taut or left slack; gold warps over the weave. Click for another weaving.

title: Driftlines
note: Hairline currents; tone drawn from the water's speed. Click for another drift.

title: Underdrawing
note: The scaffolding first, then the paint. Watch it build, click to rebuild.

title: Hundred
note: A fixed edition of one hundred prints. Click to walk the edition.

title: Crosscurrent
note: Dark and pale ribbons ride the same current and never touch. Click for a new current.

title: Patch Mountain
note: A mountain built from nothing but patches: directional color strokes on a reserved dark ground, no outlines anywhere.

title: Folded Light
note: One palette, three panels, three moods.

title: Marine Snow
note: The dropped 9055s background polished into its own piece: a quiet water column with slanting light shafts, layered drifting marine snow, and a whisper of distant glow. No creature.

title: Meridian
note: Flowing meridian lines in blue-violet. Drag to stir.

title: Dusk Shore
note: A pixel-art beach from above at dusk, drawn with code. The shoreline breathes, wave bands drift, sun glitter twinkles gold, and tiny figures wait at the foam edge.

title: Misregister
note: One geometric form pulled three times in cyan, magenta and yellow, each plate offset like a misregistered print. The color is the misregistration.

title: Weave
note: Warp and weft threads crossing in plain weave. Each thread alternates over and under at every crossing, like real cloth.

title: Ruled Lines
note: Dense hand-drawn rules in ballpoint blue on paper. A hidden field lifts the lines — the ghost of a circular presence you feel before you see.

title: Tidepool Contours
note: A rock shelf at low tide, read as depth bands. The pools breathe, small crabs work the wet rock, and a click drops a pebble.

title: The Shadow of One Letter
note: A red wireframe solid, hand-drawn, casting a shadow built from one repeated dot. The shadow's edge and density do the drawing. Click for another casting.

title: Eternal Bloom
note: Continuous spawn every 2s: squares expand and rotate at uniform rates, alternating direction.

title: Deliberately Uninteresting
note: After Sol LeWitt. Thousands of identical marks; the composition lives in coverage, never in the mark. Up close it is nothing but handwriting, at distance a curve. Click for another field.

title: Square Fountain
note: Hypnotic loop: squares spawn center, grow and rotate, dissolve at max size.

title: What Is Generative Art
note: The artist writes the rules, the machine rolls the dice, and a family comes out. One branching system, six children, one keeper. Click for another family.

title: Smoke
note: One breath, made visible. A single column of smoke rises, widens, and dissolves into empty paper. Click for another.

title: River Stones
note: A quiet bed of river stones, each water-worn smooth, overlaps deepening honestly. One moss-green stone among the gray. Click for another arrangement.

title: Frost
note: First frost on the pane. Ink-blue crystals creep in from the corners and stop, leaving the middle clear to breathe. Click for another morning.

title: Lunar Strip
note: One lunation in twenty-nine moons, waxing to a gold full moon and waning again, each terminator hand-wobbled. Click for another sky.

title: Crows on a Wire
note: Five on the wire and one just leaving. A small moment, drawn plainly, under a big empty sky. Click for another morning.

title: Wind Field
note: A gust frozen mid-passage through wheat, every blade leaning downwind, the bend swelling where the gust is strongest. One red poppy stands unbent. Click for another field.

title: Slat Light
note: Low sun through a fence, the sun itself offstage. Long soft shadows rake across paper, deepening where they overlap, and one warm band falls where a slat is missing. Click for another evening.

title: Square One
note: One square: its sides unwrap into a single line as it turns, then fold back.

title: Unison
note: Continuous spawn every 2s: all squares rotate the same direction.

title: Sides
note: Dot becomes line, triangle, square, gains sides until a circle, returns to dot.

title: Sides II
note: Dot to circle, skipping sides: readable polygons then a quick rush to round.

title: Halved
note: One random polygon. Draw a line through it and every polygon the line crosses splits in two, in tonal steps. Cut as far as you like.

title: Wire Garden
note: One unbroken wire grown from a pool of fragments, bending toward a wandering lure. The wild joints are marked.

title: Trellis
note: Type any word and watch it grow into a hedge, leaves and blossoms along every letter, the word still readable through the green.

title: Flight Deck
note: Seven fogged depth levels of swirling particle trails, flown through like gates. Click to jump to a fresh system; move the pointer to look around.

title: Personal Weather
note: A field of wind barbs, each with a heading of its own. Your pointer paints weather into the air: fast flicks burn amber, slow drifts stay blue. Move your pointer to stir it.

title: Accumulation
note: Sixteen thousand grains of light dropped one by one until a moon, a ridge, a wave, or a forest gathers out of the dust. Click the piece for a new sky.

title: Subdivide
note: A rectangle keeps splitting until every piece earns a texture: hatching, stipple, rings, the odd flat solid. Only adjacent to Mondrian in method. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Contour Fields
note: Contour lines over imaginary terrain, each drawn a little unsteadily so they read as hand inked. They bunch up where the ground gets steep. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Mai Menochot
note: A rising sun in two passes of ink over still water, the rust pass deliberately misregistered like a slipped letterpress bed. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Three Shapes
note: A tangent chain of circles, squares, and triangles in two inks, construction lines left visible. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Strata Break
note: Concentric rings dissolving from order into chaos, with one red ring. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Interference
note: Wheels of fine lines turn at different speeds, and where they cross, new patterns bloom and dissolve. This one moves. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Oscillons
note: Waveforms drawn the way an oscilloscope draws them, layered in phosphor tones on dark. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Bloom
note: Exact geometry in ink first, then watercolor washes bloom over it and dry where they want. Click the piece for a fresh sheet.

title: Growth
note: A line that follows only local rules grows into folds no hand would draw. This one grows while you watch. Click the piece for a new growth.

title: Murmuration
note: Six hundred particles hold a word that shivers but never lands, until a gust scatters them and they find their letters again. This one moves. Click the piece for a new word.

title: Congregation
note: A living web of three hundred forty seeds that breathes with its own synthesized heartbeat, gathering at every kick. This one moves and makes sound. Click the piece to start it.

title: Tone Mosaic
note: An etching pressed from a thousand voronoi cells, where cell size does all the shading. Click the piece for a new plate.

title: Corridor
note: A quadtree of geometric motifs, camera-projected into an endless corridor. This one moves. Click the piece for a new corridor.

title: Field Notes
note: Wind, recorded the way a field notebook would: inked curves combed across the page, with one red thread running through. Click the piece for a new page.

title: Old Courses
note: An 1881 survey of a river that never flowed, thirteen channels deep. Click the piece for a new survey.

title: Overprint
note: Two ink passes over one quarter-circle grid: indigo first, rust second and a little off register, the way a tired press would lay it down. Click the piece for a new variation.

title: Strata
note: An imaginary terrain sliced like a museum model: translucent elevation layers floating in a dark studio, one warm layer among the ink blues. Drag to look around, click for a new landscape.

title: Tangency
note: A circle-packing study. Discs are placed largest first and grown until each touches a neighbor, so every circle is tangent to something. Rings and arc segments in rust, ochre, and slate on warm paper. Click for a new variation.

title: Lichtenberg
note: A crystal grown from static. Thousands of sparks drift in out of the dark and freeze the instant they touch the tree. Nothing here was drawn, only accreted. Click to grow a new one.

title: Kindling
note: Two fractal flames built from pure density, drifting into each other and back. Bright cores dissolving into smoke. Click for a new burn.

title: Kaleid 99
note: Oscillator bands through a ninety-nine-mirror kaleidoscope, thresholded into hard stripes and printed to near black on paper. One band of color keeps the rest honest. Click for a new variation.

title: Interruptions
note: A dense weave of short ink dashes, each the same length and turned at random, with whole regions erased back to paper. The holes are the drawing. Click for a new variation.

title: Storm Grid
note: Forty-nine nested squares drawn with a plotter's patience, except in two or three cells where the hand slipped. Click the piece for a new plot.

title: Feedback
note: One buffer of noise re-sampled through its own ghost until it settles into flowing grain. The settle is the event. Click the piece to run it again.

title: Still Life
note: Two to four vessels on a low table, drawn flat with long shadows and one accent pot per arrangement. The horizon never lands in the same place twice. Click the piece for a new seating.

title: Hour Hands
note: A clock that repaints itself every minute: three rings for seconds, minutes and hours, each a slow journey between two colors. Click the piece to hold a still.

title: Half-Moon Dots
note: A breathing dotted field crossed by a slowly rotating crescent. Dots that straddle the edge are drawn bisected, so the boundary itself is the subject.

title: What Isn't There
note: A poster printed in reverse: every word exists only as erasure, carved, rubbed and punched out of the ink. Read the gaps.

title: Off Register
note: A playable print-shop instrument: twelve one-gesture motifs on keys A to L, each printed twice with a ghost-ink offset like the sheet slipped. Tap on mobile.

title: Tone Rows
note: A polargraph density study: vertical ticks drawn row by row, length following tone, whites lifting the pen. A rose window in machine handwriting.

title: Orbit Portraits
note: Strange attractors rendered like flame fractals. Every roll picks an orbit; a laciness test hangs the keepers and stamps the duds on the reject wall.

title: Half a Million Grains
note: Half a million grains of sandpaint falling one by one. Nothing is drawn except dots, and the picture emerges. Click the paper for a burst.

title: Own Lines
note: Every stroke is built by hand from shaded triangles, width shaped by pressure, so the line keeps a brush's habits. One study per click: a wave, a heron, bamboo, a grass tuft.

title: Wind Bent
note: Concentric rings sampled through a wind field that pushes in every direction. Click for a fresh gust.

title: Almost Perfect
note: One pen, one line, never lifted: nested squares whose rotation drifts as the path goes in. It draws itself like a plotter. Click for a new hand.

title: Mud Map
note: Three mud zones on the hue wheel, marked dead, and every trapped color drawing its own escape arc to the edge. Click to scatter the colors again.

title: Living Homage
note: After Albers, but the squares never sit still: one slow palette journey, sizes breathing out of phase. Click to mint a fresh journey.

title: Typewriter Weave
note: Struck one character at a time with a shaky hand. Up close it reads as typing; from across the room it reads as cloth.

title: Eye Garden
note: A garden of eye sprouts that watch your pointer go by, pupils widening, then settle back to sleep. Sweep through it.

title: Greedy Squiggle
note: A plotter pen hunts the darkest pixel left on the page, erasing as it goes, lifting to relocate. Mostly one line.

title: Value Ramp Grid
note: Half-square triangles in a deliberate diagonal gradient, light to dark. Nothing else.

title: Bleed Ledger
note: Three hands negotiate on a ruled ledger: hidden pigment, pitted wounds, gravity-drawn streaks. Every trail reads back to its wound.

title: Fifty-Three Divisions
note: The octave divided into 53 commas, brass seams and all. Hover to read each comma in cents.

title: Mark the Seam
note: Twelve pure fifths tiled as kites, the 23.46-cent comma concentrated into one brass wedge.

title: Fusion Threshold
note: Dots accelerate until they stop being dots and become tone. A meter marks the moment.

title: One Series Two Materials
note: One logarithmic series drives both a ribbon's geometry and a striker's rhythm. Same structure, felt twice.

title: Reverse Lookup
note: Drag across a hue spectrum while the piece ranks its palette by simplicity. Vetoes shown struck through.

title: Five Methods
note: One scalar field rebuilt five ways: contour, stipple, hatch, tone cells, drift. Portraits of methods.

title: Face Walk
note: Erv Wilson's hexany as a navigable octahedron. Triads named and sounded in just intonation.

title: Possible Worlds
note: Pascal's triangle as a map of chord worlds. Click a cell to open its diagram.

title: Scale Loom
note: A tuning ladder woven like cloth: fifteen rungs, the pattern re-segmenting live.

title: Hover
note: Marks breathing at the edge of visibility. Your pointer steadies them.

title: Retune
note: Two offset circle grids plus a sheared dot grid. Drag to retune and watch the moire re-resolve.

title: Convergence
note: A tilted crystal of 5-limit harmony. Pulses converge on the root and bloom on arrival.

title: Trough Walk
note: An octave as a washboard of tuning valleys. The probe snaps into troughs; wide ratios eat narrow ones.

title: Held and Shaped
note: Two panels, one material: pulse holds while color shapes, then they trade jobs every 24 seconds.

title: Clang
note: Sixteen agents cycle seven ink marks through a 54-second arc, punctuated by three clangs.

title: Prime Petals
note: A rosette in prime-numbered hues only. Each prime family grows exactly p petals.

title: Tritave Rose
note: Structure repeating at 3x instead of 2x: thirteen rings, marks sized by consonance, slow revolution.

title: Ten Times Exact
note: One recording played ten times byte-identically while the picture turns into notation. Your ears flip before your eyes do.

title: The Exactness Gate
note: Detune the loop by fractions of a semitone and watch song-ness collapse. Exactness as a game.

title: Over Under
note: Seeded Celtic knotwork: strands turn at every wall, crossings alternate over and under, a plaited frame with corner bosses. Click for a fresh knot.

title: Mold and Chisel
note: Fog-sculpture instrument: you place the emitters, the wind does the carving. The last sculpture lingers as a ghost.

title: Eight Minutes
note: This piece only exists during eight-minute fog windows. Between them, a countdown and a tide table of past openings.

title: Seventeen Microns
note: A slider for droplet size against a fixed updraft. Find by eye where float becomes rain.

title: Wrong Octave, Right Key
note: Stretch the octave from 2.0 to 2.6 under a familiar tune. It stays recognizable while the tonic refuses to resolve.

title: Lattice Choir
note: Chords built on a fractional-octave lattice, consonant by construction. Three voices blooming at once.

title: The 3:5:7
note: A brass staircase of thirteen steps to the tritave, lit by odd partials, ending on a 3:5:7 cadence.

title: Master Frequency Only
note: Every sound frozen as a spectral recipe; your only control is one master wheel. Timbre intact, pitch yours.

title: Pairs Only
note: Sixty-four oscillators, spendable in pairs. Rich voices starve their neighbors.

title: Eight Bad Chips
note: Eight synth chips, each with one labeled manufacturing fault. The ensemble of its own failures.

title: Gesture Atlas
note: Draw a stroke and the atlas finds its nearest cousin in the corpus, snapping it under your hand. Endpoints count most.

title: Hue Bingo Canvas
note: Every visit rolls a fresh Hue Bingo palette and lays it down as wobbling colour rings. Coherent by construction.

title: Standing-Wave Hatch
note: A hatch field where a sine wave decides how long each dash gets. Blades of darkness swim through the lines.

title: Family of Blobs
note: The same blob built four ways: harmonic, grown, contoured, implicit. One ink, one plate, the comparison is the picture.

title: Spiral Zap
note: One quiet triadic palette spiralled ten times, calm on the left and feral on the right. The tipping point is visible.

title: Budget Ink
note: A still life shaded on a strict ink budget.

title: Silent Score
note: A polar waveform ring performing a song with no audio.

title: Never Isles
note: A procedural antique nautical chart: radial-noise archipelago engraved as a maritime plate, with rhumb lines, twin compass roses, hachured relief, and recombined place-names. Click for a new chart.

title: Desordres
note: A grid of squares, each disobeying a little; a few burn vermilion. Click for another desordres.

title: Chord Orbits
note: Three rings of points joined every k-th pair by hairlines; one weaves a web, another a slow star. Click for new orbits.

title: Contour Drift
note: Sixty horizontal lines displaced by drifting noise; topographic calm in one ink. Click for a new drift.

title: Night Water
note: Blue-teal motes drift and breathe in dark water; a few wear faint rings. Click for a new tide.

title: Kinetic Scroll
note: A landscape plywood frame on dark ground, with a flat-alpha soft shadow and nothing else outside it. Left third: three vertical etched-acrylic panels at 40% alpha carrying seeded hatch lines and abstract etched marks (arcs, dashes, dots — never letterforms). Right two-thirds: the cotton scroll with three horizontal pigment stripe rows (indigo, rust, moss top to bottom, with seeded variation and grain). A crimson basting thread runs in a long sine curve from the scroll's rolled left edge to the needle station at about 55% of the scroll width — stitched partway, as specced — with the needle drawn as a slanted line plus thread-colored dot. Mobile keeps the same landscape composition as a centered band. Motor: each pointermove event contributes a capped displacement (±90 scroll-px); offset(t) = 320 + sum dx_i·(1 − exp(−(t − t_i)/0.35)), so the scroll eases in after movement and settles as the exponentials saturate — never frame-integrated state; idle > 2 s: needle parks (angle relaxes from −0.35 to 0.15 rad). Endless scroll: content is never stored — segment (row, k) is a pure seeded function of scroll-space position (260 px segments, home-pigment rows with 25% seeded cross-pigment variation, grain, accent slivers), so revealed sections recycle as new seeded bands ahead. Thread: dashes live in scroll-space (26 px dash / 14 px gap), so stitches travel with the cloth; the needle station at 55% of scroll width stitches cloth as it feeds past. TAP (under 12 px movement): cycles thread color crimson → indigo → moss → crimson. Bands drawn procedurally per frame from seeded segment functions (no band buffer, no offscreen canvas); all tones flat-alpha, no gradients, no shadowBlur; soft shadow as one flat-alpha offset rect. Probe harness driving the piece's own pointer listeners through its rAF loop: frame one → 1 s of pointer travel changes 244,496 px (scroll feeding); 1 s → 4 s changes 30,736 px (still easing); 4 s → 8 s idle changes 0 px by more than 4/255 per channel (2,459 edge pixels differ by ≤4 — antialiasing rounding on the exponential tail, visually stopped); a tap after settling changes 1,975 px, confined to the thread/needle (crimson → indigo). No readable text except the title.

title: Flag
note: A 4x3 wall of book pages filling about 80% of the frame on dark wall ground. Each page holds about 14 rows of gray dash pseudo-text on cream paper with a darker shade strip along the bottom edge — dashes only, varying lengths with ragged ends, never letterforms. No emblem, no bar yet; the wall reads as a full, quiet text-block texture. 25 s loop, pure function of piece time plus recorded taps: pages full 4 s, then a squeegee pass 3 s (a dark printer's bar travels top-to-bottom, the emblem revealed progressively under it via an animated clip), dwell 1 s (bar parked at bottom), printed hold 5 s (full emblem, no bar), regeneration 8 s (each page's text-block fades back over the emblem, 5 s per page, starts staggered over 3 s), rest 4 s, then repeats with a fresh emblem. TAP = an early squeegee pass with a fresh emblem variant; tap vs drag separated by 12 px; a tap during a pass is ignored; drag does nothing; never a reload. Emblem: 2-3 distinct primitives from a family of 6 invented marks (ring, horizontal bar, split disc, vertical bar, opposing arc pair, diagonal bar), flat vermilion, centered, spanning about 2 pages wide; cycle 0's variant is a split disc crossed by a horizontal bar — bold, invented, no real symbol. Pages and emblem drawn directly on the main canvas (no per-page offscreens); pass = animated clip revealing the emblem layer; regeneration = per-page alpha ramp of the text layer back over the emblem; no gradients, no shadowBlur, no Path2D, no offscreen canvas, no audio. Forced-time probes: t=0 pages full (0 vermilion px); t=5.5 mid-pass (bar 18,974 px, emblem top revealed 40,089 px); t=7.5 dwell (full emblem 86,690 px, bar parked); t=10 hold (full emblem, no bar); t=17 mid-regeneration (emblem fading, 11,092 px); t=21/24 rest (clean pages, 0 vermilion); tap at t=2.0 starts an early pass, and a second tap at t=4.0 during that pass is correctly ignored. Built clean on first pass; no fix rounds needed.

title: Distorted Mirrors
note: A night woods on near-black green: six vertical trunks with bark streaks running off top and bottom, no horizon, no sky. Four convex traffic mirrors bolted to four different trunks at driving height, each showing the same woods funhouse-distorted (barrel-compressed streaks, center magnified, edges squeezed, never legible), each with a small bright amber dot — the viewer's presence, refracted. Pointer-move / drag = the presence: the amber dot moves in every mirror simultaneously, each with its own barrel mapping; mirrors nearest the pointer brighten; no tap action; idle: the dot parks at last position and the trunk sway continues on closed-form sines. The dot can never leave a mirror: its offset is barrel-compressed and clamped to 0.78 of the mirror radius, and it is drawn nowhere outside a mirror. Mirror content drawn procedurally inside each circular clip (no offscreen scene sampling); no gradients, no shadowBlur, no Path2D, no createElement, no AudioContext. Fixes: a diameter cap from the closest mirror-trunk pair minus sway margin, so no two mirrors overlap even at square aspect (the first thumb showed the middle pair touching); phone diameters capped at 0.24x frame width with alternate mirrors staggered vertically after the first mobile render overlapped mirrors and clipped the edge pair. A probe harness driving the piece's own pointermove listener confirmed the rightmost mirror brightens, its dot moves to the corresponding position, the other three mirrors' dots shift consistently, and no dot leaves its mirror.

title: What Have You Lost?
note: A dark bulletin-board field, full-bleed, crowded with warm paper flyers. 36 small flyers on a seeded jittered grid plus 4 half-pinned flyers at the frame edges (40 total). Each small flyer is a torn-corner rectangle carrying 2-3 abstract marks (blob cluster, hook arc, ring pair — suggestive, never literal), a crimson tear-strip at the bottom edge, grain flecks, and a pin dot at the top. At center, one large blank flyer (2.2x small size) with a pulsing amber ring where a phone number would be — the number is absent by design. No flyer overlaps the center flyer. No visible text except the title; no digits, no words on any flyer. Center pulse: amber ring breathes on a 5.5 s period while the board is silent, quickening to 2.5 s while recent tap activity decays (exponential, tau 4 s). Tap a small flyer: it speaks — a 600 ms amber ripple expands and a sine tone sounds (180-660 Hz by flyer index, 1.2 s decay); then a chorus: the nearest flyers within 3 distance bands answer at 90 ms intervals, nearest first, volume falling with distance (capped at 18 voices). Drag a flyer: it follows the pointer and stays where put; the pin re-seats with it; tap vs drag separated by an 8 px movement threshold on release. The center flyer is not tappable and not draggable; it only pulses. Tones ONLY through lazily created, typeof-guarded WebAudio inside the tap gesture; the board is silent until tapped; no microphone, no recording, no autoplay. Fixes: two pre-QA code cleanups — a doubled rAF boot section replaced with a single guarded loop (the first version called a named function expression that would have thrown ReferenceError in a real browser), and redundant distance lines in the chorus builder removed; no fixes needed after inspection. A node harness driving the piece's own pointer listeners confirmed: 36 grid flyers + 4 edge flyers, zero flyers overlapping the center, a tap creates one event with an 18-voice chorus, a center tap creates nothing, and a drag moves a flyer by the exact drag delta without firing a tap.

title: Absence Stack
note: A stack of five abstract photographic prints in muted C-41 tones on a dark table ground, centered, 4:5 at about 66% of frame height. The top print's redaction bars form a bold doorway (two posts plus a lintel) that reads whole; backing edges and slight seeded rotations peek at the corners, showing the stack beneath. Print fields are layered flat-alpha landscape strata with seeded grain flecks and jittered corners — irregular, not UI cards. 30 s shuffle loop: hold 4 s, then the top print slides down-left to the back over 2 s (eased, arcing out on a sine bulge), hold 4 s, repeat; the other prints step one slot toward the front during the same slide; stack order is a closed-form rotation: at step s, stack[i] = print (i - s) mod 5. Drag: pointer down grabs a print (topmost hit first); it lifts to scale 1.04 with a flat-alpha offset shadow and follows the pointer; release snaps it back to its current slot over 0.5 s with an ease-out cubic; dragging never changes stack order, only reveals what's beneath. Prints as seeded procedural fields drawn per frame on the MAIN canvas (no offscreen buffers); tones as layered flat-alpha fields, NO gradients, NO shadowBlur; the mask array is the single source of truth — bars are never drawn similar, they are the same array shifted by each print's index x 6px. Fix: one snap-completion one-frame gap (a print skipped in the main loop on the frame its snap finished) was fixed by drawing the print at its slot immediately on completion. Forced-time probes: t = 5 s shows the top print mid-slide down-left with the stack beneath revealed; a drag probe shows the grabbed print following the pointer, lifted, revealing the print beneath, and snapping back to its slot on release (snap render byte-identical to frame one).

title: Translation Chain
note: Five equal full-width bands, in order — (1) PHOTOGRAPH: a row of 14 invented glyphs rendered as a grayscale Bayer-dithered block on dark ground; (2) WORKSHOP: rust annotation arcs over a faint dither block; (3) SCULPTURE: isometric blocks sized by glyph complexity; (4) LEGAL PAD: graphite sketch strokes tracing glyph skeletons on a ruled yellow pad; (5) THREAD: a dashed crimson stitched curve through the glyph centroids. The conveyor is at rest. No visible text except the title; glyphs are invented marks, never letters in any alphabet. Conveyor: one band-height per 6 s step, 1 s ease, then settle; a full pass takes about 30 s, then the string re-seeds and a new translation begins; bands are stream items (item m = string floor(m/5), medium mod(m,5)); the stack scrolls as whole units and settles aligned each step, so a band is never torn mid-glyph at rest. Tap a band (movement under 12 px): freezes just that band in place for inspection while the conveyor runs on; its medium keeps rendering live detail (dither shimmer, thread stitch advance); tap again: it eases back to its stream position over 1 s; drag does nothing. Live detail: dither shimmer (seeded sine phase per dot), thread dash offset advancing, workshop annotation pulse. The string = seeded codepoint array (14 invented glyphs from a fixed 40-glyph invented alphabet, consistent per seed); each stage = deterministic pure function of the array; everything draws directly on the main canvas: no offscreen buffers, no gradients, no shadowBlur, no filters, no WebGL, no AudioContext; built clean first pass.

title: The Strongman's Mirror
note: Two headless bust silhouettes face each other across a vertical mirror line on a near-black ground. Left figure: dark uniform tones with a crimson sash diagonal. Right figure: pale, white-gold with a muted shadow edge. Heads are cropped out of the frame top on purpose — identity lives in the torso and sash. A faint horizontal band behind the pair suggests the novel's colonel's mirror scene, nothing else. 18 s loop: figures stable 0-5 s, mirror line brightens 5-7 s, identity crossfade 7-13 s (palettes swap across the line with a 1 px traveling wave; left figure swaps slightly ahead of the right), held swapped 13-16 s, crossfade back 16-18 s. Identity swap is a palette lerp driven by a single t parameter; both figures are drawn from ONE skeleton path (shoulder/torso curves), palette applied per side; the sash travels with the dark identity — after the swap it sits on the right figure. Drag variant: dragging the mirror line left/right shifts the swap boundary (clamped to plus-or-minus 30% of width); the minority figure dissolves into horizontal static scanlines — seeded line noise clipped to the figure silhouette, density proportional to displacement — until pure noise at the extreme, then reforms on release as the boundary eases back to center (exponential decay); the mirror line dims but never vanishes. Mirror-line glow and the traveling wave are flat-alpha shapes, no gradients; no Path2D (the QA renderer's node-canvas build does not define it) — the bust skeleton is traced directly on the context, with save/clip for the sash and the static dissolve. Fixes: rAF kickoff rewritten as a plain function declaration before rendering (the No.1278 lesson — first version used a discarded named function expression); first render crashed in the QA renderer with Path2D undefined — bust path restructured to trace directly on the context; first render's wide neck (0.30 of figure width) with a smooth shoulder dome read as two bottles — neck narrowed to 0.20 of width with a sharper shoulder flare, so the pair reads as headless busts. Forced-time probes confirmed the loop: t = 10 mid-crossfade (both figures passing through a shared mid-tone, as a two-way palette lerp must); t = 14.5 held swapped (left pale, right dark, sash on the right figure).

title: Day Desk / Night Table
note: The field splits exactly at 50% with a thin pencil-gray line. Left is the cool day desk with the first row of six seal-stamp tiles landed plus the first tile of row two — each a rounded square with a thud shadow and an invented glyph mark (slash, plus, double-bar, dot-and-arc), marks only, never letters. Right is the night table idling in darkness: a dim yellow pad centered in its half with no landscape strokes yet, and a faint flat-alpha amber glow top-right, never a drawn lamp. The two sides share one room's tone range, split by light only. 44 s loop (the prompt's phase durations 20+2+20+2 sum to 44 s; its loose 48 s total is noted in process.md): day phase 0-20 s (stamps land one per 1.2 s row-major across a 6x8 grid in the upper two-thirds of the day half; a completed row fades out starting 6 s after completion over 2 s), 2 s wash (flat-alpha amber band sweeps across the split, no gradients), night phase 20 s (stamps sleep at 0.35 alpha, bulb glow strengthens, pad draws about 400 graphite scratch strokes over 16 s along three seeded mountain ridgelines from 1D value noise, landscape holds 4 s), 2 s wash, loop restarts. Frame one is phase-shifted 8 s into the day phase so the gate shows a developed desk. Bulb glow as two layered flat-alpha ellipses, never a radial gradient; changeover wash as a flat-alpha sweeping band; study-wide rule honored — no readable text anywhere, stamps carry invented marks only, no Latin/Amharic letters; no literal desk objects (no pens, no drawers); built clean first pass; a forced-time probe at mid-night-phase confirmed the landscape resolves (2,079 graphite pixels inside the pad region at 200 of 400 strokes).

title: A Century of Women
note: A horizontal timeline on one continuous bronze rail across a dark ground, showing the rail at its start (the 1915 end). Exactly 100 small framed images, evenly spaced, chronological left to right — each a procedurally drawn period vignette: an abstract silhouette (featureless head, torso, hemline, legs) in its decade's wash, with an era prop (hat, fan, bag, shades, cup, phone), and the same pale hollow rectangle in the headline zone of every frame, where the slogan was stripped. A thin strip at the top edge carries the wash color of the frame at center (the year-tick as changing palette light, never numbers); small bronze ticks mark every tenth frame on the rail. No faces, no identifiable people, no year or decade labels, no visible text except the title. Drag horizontally scrubs the century (1915 to 2015 and back) via x-offset with frame recycling; a drag never enlarges. Tap a frame (movement under 12 px): it enlarges to fill the screen over 0.4 s, holds silent, and returns to the rail after 5 s total; never more than one enlarged frame. No audio of any kind; the palette IS the date; the void rectangles must be identical in every frame — the repetition is the argument.

title: Finite / Infinite
note: A monumental black wall, full-bleed, faint seeded speckle, flat-alpha ambient edge light, no gradients. In white architectural lettering, fully legible: WE MUST ACCEPT FINITE over DISAPPOINTMENT, with a thin bronze rule beneath the block; the second sentence is present only as invisible gaps in the grid. True interleaving, not a crossfade: two lines of alternating words share one grid — line one WE / BUT / MUST / NEVER / ACCEPT / LOSE / FINITE / INFINITE, line two DISAPPOINTMENT / HOPE; at t = 0 only sentence-one words show, at t = 1 only sentence-two words, at the midpoint both sit half-legible in mid-gray, stuttering honestly, never fully legible at once. Auto-cycle: 20 s triangle, smoothstep-eased — disappointment rises to hope over 0-10 s, falls back over 10-20 s. Per-letter stagger: each letter's fade carries a seeded offset (0-0.25 of the parameter range), dissolving toward mid-gray as it fades. Drag horizontally scrubs the interleave parameter (1.5 full sweeps per screen width) — the drag is the viewing angle; on release the auto-cycle resumes from the scrubbed state, keeping its direction. No fade-to-black transitions; the wall stays lit and text stays present in some state at all times; no third sentence; no decorative typography — the type IS the image.

title: The Speech Bubble
note: A dark plaza, full-bleed. ONE white speech bubble, centered, occupying the middle two-thirds, drawn as a soft-edged bezier blob with a tapered tail pointing down-left and a warm inner light near its lower curve. Two cables run from the bubble's lower edge to the bottom of the frame, with pulsing teal tether lights. Three text fragments are already mid-rise below the bubble, in rotation order: ...the truth is, my grandmother...; ...the truth is, I forgive...; ...the truth is, we were here first.... Tiny ember dots drift upward near the fragments. Breathing: the bubble scales 1.0 to 1.03 on a continuous 6 s sine, independent of absorption. Ambient fragments: a seeded schedule spawns a fragment every 2.2-4.2 s; each rises from the bottom edge at a seeded speed and x position, swaying gently, and is absorbed at the bubble's lower curve — scaling down and fading over its last 60 px, triggering a warm glow pulse on the bubble (exponential decay, tau 0.55 s); at most about 7 fragments are ever visible at once (cap is 12). Drag offering: a drag starting in the bottom 35% of the screen and moving upward more than 30 px releases a NEW fragment at the release x position; it rises faster, is absorbed at the lower curve, and pulses the bubble; release returns to ambient. No text input field, no speech-to-text; the bubble never pops, deflates, or flies away; no human figures, no crowd silhouettes; silent, no audio of any kind. Visible text is ONLY the three specced fragments (verbatim) plus the title — the prompt's 40-fragment deck is reduced to the three specced examples in rotation, no additional fragments invented; glow is layered flat-alpha ellipses, never gradients.

title: Ad-Speak
note: A billboard in perfect brand grammar, complete and legible as an ad — headline zone on top, brand-red rule beneath it, body copy as five gray bars in the left column, a bronze fist holding nothing (palm, four finger bumps, thumb, flat bronze tones) as the hero in the right third, one generic black swoosh-like curve drawn once across the middle, and a gold logo plate with a blank disc at bottom-right. The headline is VOID: the brand-red wipe bar sits parked at the left edge of the headline zone, no sentence visible; no visible words anywhere except the title. 8 s sentence cycle: 1 s red-bar wipe-in revealing the sentence, 6 s hold, 1 s red-bar wipe-out; sentences cycle a fixed deck of 8 in fixed order (Love Overrules; Hurt people, hurt people; No matter what; Keep the faith baby; Community is currency; We must accept finite disappointment; Never lose infinite hope; Are we in time or is time within us), rendered verbatim in a heavy grotesque stack, fitted to the zone by shrinking until within 96% of zone width. Tap (movement under 12 px) skips to the next sentence and restarts the wipe-in phase — the channel-change, never a reseed; no drag mechanic, otherwise watch-only. No real brand names, no real swoosh (a generic curve only); the sentences are SINCERE, the ad grammar is the irony; no scrolling news-ticker behavior; the billboard never sells anything.

title: White on White
note: A large white panel carrying the ghost of a document, fully inked — a white heading block with two glyph rows, ruled lines across the sheet, paragraph rows of pseudo-type dashes in ghost white, all barely distinguishable from the ground. A small pulsing flash-bolt icon sits bottom-right. No flash reveal at frame one; no color in the dark state beyond the whites. TAP AND HOLD = flash: hold sustains the reveal, release decays over 3 s; the mask grows 0 to full panel diagonal over 1.2 s (smoothstep), clipped to concentric flat-alpha discs — no gradient; ember edge glow is two layered flat-alpha rings at the mask boundary; a faint flash-white core disc appears while fully revealed. DRAG disabled: a press traveling more than 12 px cancels its flash, so dragging never reveals. Ambient: the ghost document slowly re-inks itself on a 48 s loop (full 0-32 s, fade to 35% ink 32-40 s, redraw 40-48 s); frame one sits at loop phase 0, fully inked. Reveal via center-out radial mask of concentric flat-alpha discs (no gradient, no bloom); document text is pseudo-type glyph noise, never readable real words; revealed crowd is procedurally drawn, painterly-flat, never a real historical photograph — trapezoid torsos with varied shoulder widths, featureless dark head discs set slightly above the torso so a neck gap reads, some with a thick diagonal raised arm, one red sign/flag held high near the upper right; document and photo layers are the same size and registered.

title: The Gesture
note: A crowded archival street scene in muted tones, flat and painterly — building silhouettes above, asphalt below, 120 seeded simplified figures in muted coat tones (brown, slate blue, oxblood, umber, charcoal) with plain head dots and no facial features. At center, two intertwined forearms in warm bronze form the embrace, resting inside the crowd at natural scale. Pearl bracelet dots ride one forearm; a small gold wedding band rides the other, after the pearl bracelet and wedding band of the Kings. No faces anywhere, no full bodies. 30 s loop: 0-4 s scene (crowd fully composed, gesture resting inside it), 4-7 s highlight sweep (flat-alpha bronze light band travels across the gesture bbox, glow ramps up), 7-13 s isolation (6 s smooth scale-up, crowd fades out), 13-23 s monumental hold (10 s, bronze breathes with a slow 6 s metallic shimmer, source scene returns as a small cream-bordered stamp at bottom-right, labeled only by position, never text), 23-27 s collapse back, 27-30 s scene hold, then loop; no hard cuts. Drag pans across the monumental gesture (closed-form sum of recorded drag deltas with tau 2.5 s decay after release, clamped so the gesture never leaves the frame entirely). Bronze shading as layered flat-alpha tones, never gradients; isolation via scale interpolation; crowd as a seeded particle-field of simplified figures, never photorealism.

title: Flash Reveal
note: Genuinely near-blank — panel in near-black with only faint seeded speckle and breath-on-glass arcs, plus a pulsing white bolt icon at the lower right. The viewer must doubt anything is there. Tap and hold = the flash bulb: while held, the latent image stays lit through a radial mask centered on the tap point, with hard light-falloff built from 24 concentric flat-alpha discs (outer rings faint, core full) plus a slight overexposure disc at the core; release and it decays over about 2 s (radius and alpha shrink together). Drag is disabled: pointer movement never changes the flash; only pointerdown sets the flash point and pointerup starts the decay. Watch-only ambient: every 25 s, one brief half-flash flickers at the center (0.8 s triangle envelope, half radius, half alpha), teasing the surface, never fully revealing; never a flash train. The revealed image is ALWAYS the same composition: fixed seeded layout — buildings, asphalt street, 46 flat figures in muted 1960s coat tones, one yellow sign held high left of center; where the flash fires decides which details it catches. Flash mask as concentric flat-alpha discs, NO radial gradient; latent image procedurally drawn, painterly-flat, never a real historical photograph and never photoreal; flash icon shapes only; the dark state is quiet, not sinister.

title: Unbranded
note: A vintage-style print ad on cream paper, centered panel on a darker cream ground. Teal hero image: a navy-suited figure gesturing toward a gold bottle on a side table. Below it: a red headline zone, body copy, a gold logo disc with a red bar, and fine print — all text zones are invented glyph dashes, never real slogans or real brand logos. Frame one opens on the COMPLETED ad (loop phase 0 = built hold), so the ad is built completely before any erasure begins. 34 s loop: built hold 0-8 s, erasure cascade 8-18 s (headline to logo to body to fine print, 2.5 s each), naked hold 18-26 s, rebuild in reverse 26-34 s. Each erased zone keeps its exact shape as a pale rectangle with faint ghost-glyph texture; the voids ARE the composition; the hero image never moves. Drag horizontally scrubs the erasure timeline (0.04 s per pixel); release resumes the loop from that state via a phase offset. No real brand logos or real ad copy; no shock imagery; discomfort from STRUCTURE (pose/gaze/placement), never caricature.

title: Red Stage
note: An open public platform at dusk, shot from slightly above, full-bleed. Dusk sky in layered flat-alpha bands from deep dusk blue-violet at top to warm dusk brown at the horizon, with one strong dusk light source — a warm layered glow near the horizon that slowly shifts (60 s sine on alpha, 90 s sine on position). Below, a plaza stone field with faint seeded joint lines and a dusk shadow wash. At center, a simple red-painted stage in canvas pseudo-3D — trapezoid top surface over a front face, flat-alpha cast shadow down-right. On the stage, left to right: a chrome microphone stand, a stack of three dark-cloth books, a wood stool, and a clay pot with green leaves. Around the plaza periphery, faint ghost crowd figures drift on slow sines — peripheral and ghostly, never the subject. The stage is EMPTY at loop start: every presence must arrive through interaction. Idle: the stage sits empty and the dusk light slowly shifts; the crowd drifts; nothing else happens. No autoplay, no sound of any kind (no applause sound). Touch the stage: an activator appears — a dark silhouette sprite performing a small gesture loop on a 3.2 s cycle (4 frames at 0.8 s each): raises a book, plays a silent instrument, dances two steps, or reads; gesture order advances in a fixed seeded sequence, never random; each activator fades in over 1 s, gestures for 20 s total, fades out over the last 3 s, then dissolves back into the crowd. Cap: up to 6 activators share the stage, each in its own stage slot on its own gesture loop; when a 7th touch arrives, the oldest still-standing activator dissolves over 2 s; a dissolving activator vacates its slot for the newcomer. The stage never empties itself and never reloads — only the viewer adds. Drag pans the plaza view (closed-form decay, tau 2.5 s after release, clamped to plus-or-minus 40 px horizontal / plus-or-minus 24 px vertical); a drag never adds an activator, only a tap (movement under 12 px) on the stage rect does.

title: Shea Butter
note: A dark field of matte black steel panels in a loose 4x5 grid with empty cells, never a solid wall, generous black space around each block. Four yellow shea-butter blocks float at different depths, each a different scale: the largest, upper left, carries the bust — cranium with a thin brow ridge and a small nose wedge, deliberately featureless otherwise, no eyes; the other three are rough-carved lumps with thumb-print dents, seeded flecks, and a drip frozen mid-run on each flank. The only light comes from their waxy glow, rendered as layered flat-alpha ellipses. Melt cycle: 40 s per block, seeded phase offsets — slump (scaleY 1 to 0.85, scaleX 1 to 1.15), pool (scaleY to 0.78, scaleX to 1.25, pool spread growing at the base), re-rise to full height; range kept shallow on purpose so a block always reads as a block, never a puddle. Touch a block: it warms (glow alpha rises on an exponential decay) and a thumb-print dent appears, then slowly fills back in as warmth decays. Drag spins the touched block — spin is the cumulative sum of recorded drag deltas (0.005 rad/px), never frame-integrated state. Idle: every 25 s a drip detaches from a seeded block (mulberry32 keyed by cycle index), falls on an ease-out curve for 6 s, and fades to zero before it lands. No audio of any kind; no candle/wax-drip cliché; no honey imagery; no faces with eyes.

title: Sanguine Stage
note: A modular black-steel scaffold stage — open cube frames with grow lights, cascading plants, shea-butter busts on pedestals, stacked books, ceramic vessels, and a working piano at center. The stage is built for activation: it reads as a set waiting for a performance. Stage centered, three visible generations of marks (grandfather-era: heavy steel; father-era: books/masks; son-era: piano/grow lights) — layer time in the set; the piano sits at the visual center; masks hang on the scaffold uprights (African-mask silhouettes, never detailed faces). Grow lights pulse on a slow cycle (per-bar phase offsets); plants sway on closed-form sines. Every 90 seconds idle, a performance begins (60-78 s of the cycle): lights shift, masks sway harder, and a pianist's shadow (a soft shape on the floor, never a figure) pulses while three keys dip in a repeating three-note visual phrase. Then it settles. Touch the piano: a three-note visual phrase plays (keys dip in sequence) and the light rows brighten. If the sound toggle is on, the same three notes (C4-E4-G4, warm triangle tone) play through lazily created, typeof-guarded WebAudio inside the tap gesture only. Drag orbits the camera around the stage (per-layer parallax shifts, clamped to plus-or-minus 0.6 rad). Default silent with a visible toggle; the idle performance and pianist's-shadow phrase are visual only. Canvas pseudo-3D only (no WebGL, no three.js); all glow/shadow as layered flat-alpha shapes, no gradients; book spines color/pattern only, never readable text.

title: Stacked Steel
note: A tall black-steel scaffold totem standing alone on a dark empty ground — six stacked cagelike boxes, each slightly offset, never perfectly aligned. Top box holds ONLY the shea-butter bust: glowing yellow cranium with brow ridge and nose hint, deliberately featureless otherwise, on a base block with layered flat-alpha glow. Two boxes hold clay pots with cascading plants (exactly two plant boxes); one box holds two glowing yellow shea blocks with thumb-print dents and a drip frozen mid-run; one box holds dark-cloth books plus a small radio (dials, speaker dots, antenna); the bottom box holds a full row of dark-cloth books. Thin watering lines run vertically through the tower, one drip at the top of its fall. Book spines are color and pattern only, never readable text. No people, no fire, no smoke. Plants grow in a slow endless sixty-second loop per leaf: unfurl over twenty seconds, hold, droop after forty, replaced at sixty; seeded phase offsets mean young, full, and drooping leaves coexist. A watering drip falls through the tower every forty seconds. Drag rotates the totem on its vertical axis; drag up or down climbs the camera (clamped plus-or-minus ninety pixels, both decaying with tau two-point-five seconds after release). Touch a shea block or the bust: it slumps (shorter, wider) on a four-second sine bump, then re-forms — the healing substance yields. Canvas pseudo-3D only; rotation expressed as per-box horizontal shifts plus a thin side-face hint.

title: The Broken Five
note: A gray-grout field holding a shattered mosaic — a twelve-by-nine jittered grid of sharp-edged shards in black, white, cobalt, terracotta, and mirror, each shrunk ten percent toward its centroid so thick grout lines show throughout (the grout is a material, not background); thirty-five percent of cells split into two triangles along a seeded diagonal. Exactly five face-clusters sit in the central band, never the corners, each anchored to a shard of a different base color, with distinct constructions: black anchor — two hollow ovals with tiny mirror glints, twisted bezier mouth; white anchor — one large socket plus one slash eye, zigzag mouth; cobalt anchor — asymmetric large socket plus small dot eye, open screaming oval mouth; terracotta anchor — two slanted slit eyes, double-slash mouth; mirror anchor — one oval plus one crescent eye, wavy mouth. Three seeded gestural oil-stick strokes bridge outward from each cluster. No literal portraits, no blood. Breathing wall: every shard rotates a few degrees in place on a twenty-four-second sine (zero-point-zero-two to zero-point-zero-five-five radians, per-shard seeded phase); mirror shards glint on a fourteen-second traveling wave as flat-alpha white diamonds. Drag: pushes shards aside along the drag vector with Gaussian falloff (radius two-point-five cells) and exponential settle; face eye and mouth marks are drawn at their anchor shard's displaced centroid, so faces re-form from the new arrangement after a drag. Touch a face: its cluster shards flash with a mirror glint sweep (one-point-five seconds), and one seeded shard of the cluster drops away to reveal grout, then regrows over thirty seconds.

title: Black Orpheus
note: A dark, near-square field of cooling lava, full-bleed. A dense waxy mass runs the dominant diagonal from top-left toward bottom-right: overlapping flat-alpha molten-edge masses whose thicker overlaps read as deeper material. Raised blisters dot the surface; faint scratched arcs hint at faces that never fully emerged; drip tongues freeze at the right and bottom edges. The top-right corner is kept nearly pure black as the void; the edges are darker than the center. Palette only: cooling black, molten edge, ceramic glint (rare), scratch ghost. No grid, no figurative forms beyond the ghost arcs, no colored blobs, no space framing. Seamless sixty-second pour loop, phase-shifted twenty seconds so frame one opens mid-pour: zero to thirty-eight seconds material creeps forward along the diagonal; thirty-eight to fifty a solidification front sweeps the field, masses behind it turning matte and stopping while masses ahead stay glossy and keep moving; fifty to sixty the frozen end state crossfades into the next cycle's liquid start on the main canvas, so the loop never cuts. Idle: the surface breathes with tiny blister pulses. Drag redirects the flow direction; the drip tongues re-aim toward the drag vector. The faces stay ghosts: no sudden reveal.

title: God Painting
note: A vertical canvas in deep Anxious Red with thick impasto suggested by nine-hundred seeded flecks in flat alpha. Into the wet red are carved dark almond-shaped vesica-piscis forms (dark insets, undercut shadows offset down-right, knife-ridge highlights along the upper edge), arranged in seven uneven rows of four-to-seven with irregular vertical rhythm and slight horizontal jitter, eight-percent breathing margin at the edges. Exactly one broken almond (row two, third from left) is half-carved and abandoned: its upper half stays red, cut by a dark baseline. The almond is the ONLY form; the red field IS the world. Breathing: slow twelve-second swell and contraction cycle across the whole field, each row phase-offset, never fully synced. Touch: tapping an almond deepens it (darkens over half a second), then it slowly re-fills with red over twenty seconds. Drag: leaves temporary knife-ridge streaks in highlight color, fading over six seconds. Carve effect uses flat-alpha inner shadow and dark inset shapes, no gradients; impasto is seeded procedural flecks, never a photo texture. Arranged vertically, the vesica piscis takes on a meditative quality through its repetition.

title: Anxious Grid
note: A wall-sized eight-by-ten grid of off-white ceramic tiles with slightly uneven gray grout, filling the field. A black waxy pour sits thick at the edges and thin toward the center, with greasy sheen patches (flat alpha shapes) and drip runs at the pour boundaries. Scraped out of the black in tile color, with scratch-glint accents, are hollow-eyed skull-faces: some just eye-sockets, some full screaming ovals, each face a different scratch gesture from an eighteen-combination set (three eye styles by three mouth styles by outline on or off), assigned uniquely per cycle. Faces appear in clusters of one-to-three with long empty stretches between; negative tile space is about sixty percent of the surface, exceeding the prompt's forty-percent floor. Frame one opens in the hold phase: pour settled, faces fully scraped. Sixty-second seamless loop, phase-shifted twenty-four seconds: pour grows zero to twelve seconds, faces scrape in stroke by stroke twelve to twenty-four, hold twenty-four to forty-eight, fade to bare tile forty-eight to sixty, then pour again with a newly seeded layout, no hard cuts. Touch a face: it darkens and a new scrape appears beside it. Drag: leaves a smear trail that renders wet (sheen highlight) for four seconds, then hardens. The image is what survives being carved out of a poured surface.

title: The Heart Balloon
note: A monochrome, slightly grainy doorbell-camera frame — wall above, driveway below, faint wall seams and driveway joints, flat-alpha vignette bands, a faint gray REC corner mark with blinking dot. The dark trunk sits lower-center, tilted about minus-three degrees, with a thin light strip along its top edge. Five gray blob-boxes and one standing cylinder cluster at the trunk. The pink heart balloon sits above the trunk's left-center, tethered by a light-gray string to the cluster, with a small pink reflection ellipse on the trunk below it. The pink is the only color in the scene. Watch-only, sixty-second loop: zero to about forty seconds hauling — objects shift on small sine jitters while the balloon stays tethered, string swaying; escape at a seeded moment (cycle zero: thirty-nine-point-five-nine seconds; each cycle reseeds, giving thirty-eight to forty-two seconds): the string detaches and dangles from the balloon; rise, fifteen seconds: ease-out ascent with slight sine sway, drifting up and off-frame; the pink trunk reflection fades as the balloon climbs; fifty-seven to sixty seconds: reset crossfade on the main canvas — the next cycle's frame one fades in over the current scene. The balloon never pops or bursts; it escapes, it doesn't die. Film grain is a closed-form seeded function of the quantized time index, never per-frame random. A tender surveillance-footage moment abstracted — exactly one intrusion.

title: Right Here, Right Now
note: A soft gallery-white wall holding four lines of dense matte graphite, formally restrained, centered, generous margins, each line about sixty percent of field width, stacked with wide leading and faint pencil guide rules beneath — RIGHT HERE, / RIGHT NOW, / EVERYTHING, / FOREVER in canonical order. Graphite texture reads as hand-brushed (three offset passes per glyph at varying alpha plus speckle dots), not crisp vector type. Exactly one intrusion: a single rhinestone glint embedded in the counter of the R in RIGHT NOW, pulsing slowly — verified by a gold-pixel scan of the shipped thumb: exactly one glint cluster (seven gold-ish pixels in a single two-by-four-pixel box). Watch-only, two-hundred-forty-six-second cycle: each line draws itself over about forty-five seconds, characters accumulating left to right with visible brush texture; the full wall then holds sixty seconds with only the rhinestone glinting; a soft six-second wipe fades the wall back to blank paper, then the next cycle begins with a newly seeded word order (cycle zero keeps the canonical order; later cycles shuffle via seeded random). Frame one is phase-shifted to open in the hold phase (all four lines complete), per the hold-phase precedent — the draw mechanic still runs every cycle. Formally restrained yet conceptually expansive — the graphite carries the only weight in the room.

title: How to Fly (ombré)
note: A mural-scale ombré field, pink at top through gold in the middle to teal at the bottom, smooth with no banding. Eight white-bordered photo-rects float at three scale tiers with generous air: two large prints (birthday-cake glyph, car glyph), three medium (book, plant fronds, cake), three small (plant, book, car). Glyphs are clean outlines, never photographic, never faces. The book glyphs carry the prompt-specced spine label JAZZ, legible on both. Rhinestone glints and gold glitter drift between the rects. Watch-only slow drift: rects bob on independent phases (nine-to-sixteen-second periods, six-to-sixteen-pixel amplitude), glitter drifts upward on a closed-form wrap, rhinestones glint on a slow traveling sine wave. Drag gently pans the whole mural (recorded segments decaying with tau two-point-five seconds, clamped to plus-or-minus forty pixels horizontal and plus-or-minus thirty vertical); the photos keep their relative drift under the pan. The ombré is ninety layered flat-alpha horizontal bands, never a gradient; the small tier is widened from six percent to eleven percent of field width on narrow fields so glyphs stay legible on phones. Family-archive stand-ins against an ombré rainbow backdrop — glitter, rhinestones, cars, and plant life.

title: DOTS (instruction no. 1)
note: A square twelve-by-twelve dot grid on paper with generous margins, faint stencil grid lines underlying everything, cool-gray offset shadows (forty percent alpha) making each dot hover slightly above the paper. Frame one opens mid-build (phase-shifted twelve seconds, per the hold-phase precedent): most PRIMARY-palette dots filled, the last seeded cells still empty or mid-fill as pale discs, and the single half-moon hack already visible (row eleven, column four, blue). Thirty-six-second cycle: twenty-four seconds layer-by-layer build (each cell starts on a zero-point-fifteen-second stagger in seeded order, fills over two seconds in three flat-alpha pencil passes plus faint chord strokes for pencil texture), eight seconds hold, four seconds crossfade to the next predetermined palette (PRIMARY to RAINBOW to BLACK-AND-WHITE, cycling). Exactly one hack per cycle: one seeded cell breaks into a half-moon at a seeded angle, verified by a forced-time hold-phase probe showing the complete grid with exactly one half-moon. Double-tap reseeds the pattern and jumps to a seeded random palette; a single tap never reloads. No viewer drawing, no freeform scatter, no palettes outside the three predetermined sets, no gradients inside dots. Pure instruction art — a RULE, the grid is the point, openly in the Sol LeWitt conceptual lineage.

title: Good People
note: The words good people as ten wooden monolith letters on an eleven-slot ring (slot four is the word gap), centered at seventy percent of a square field, tilted in slight perspective — back letters smaller, drawn back-to-front. Warm gallery wall above, warm floor across the lower third, long soft shadows falling on the floor only. Each letter carries a grain-dark extrusion offset down-right (the monolith side), an ash face in a per-letter seeded tone, a light bevel stroke, and seeded wavy grain lines. Exactly one pink heart sits on the flank of the front letter (d at frame one), visible only at certain rotation angles. Watch-only slow rotation: one full turn per ninety seconds. Drag orbits the viewpoint around the ring; release decays back with tau two-point-five seconds, easing back to the slow turn. Double-tap reseeds which letter carries the heart; a single tap never reloads. Cooper Black is unavailable to canvas, so letters use a heavy rounded sans (nine-hundred-weight Arial Black stack) with procedural wood grain and beveled edges to keep the monolith read. Language as inhabitable architecture — a ring around an open center you could stand in.

title: Eagle Creek, Thursday Night
note: A dim bar interior, full-bleed. Back wall: dark field with faint vertical paneling and six archival-photo rects (blurred-blob abstractions in muted tones, never faces) at varied scales and slight rotations. Midground: two holographic couches (magenta seat plus darker backrest, flat-alpha sheen bands) and two speakers flanking the sign. Centered upper third: the pink neon sign EAGLE CREEK in layered flat-alpha glow, with a small halo band behind it. A slow-turning disco shimmer radiates faint streaks from upper center. Foreground: the holographic bartop sweeps the lower third in perspective, hue-cycling flat-alpha silver-pink and mint bands over a deeper pink base, with jagged aluminum crushed-can glyphs embedded in it and a glitter-coated telephone (dark handset trapezoid, magenta ear cups, gold glitter dots) at right. Gold glitter dots the room. The room stays dim; the neon and glitter carry the light. Watch-only base state with a rhythm pulse every one-point-two seconds (beat envelope driving neon flare, glitter brightness, and speaker-face glitter); tap triggers a Thursday-night set — for thirty seconds the pulse quickens to zero-point-six seconds, the neon flares, and a glitter storm of ninety sprites rises through the room, then settles; drag pans the viewpoint with parallax (back wall zero-point-three, midground zero-point-five, bartop one-point-zero), clamped to plus-or-minus thirty pixels. Never click-to-reload. Seductive first, meaningful second — a friendly place, with a funky bass, for every race.

title: Drawing as Incantation
note: Blank paper at frame one — the drawing begins at load, so the gate holds. Watch-only, two-hundred-six-second cycle: strokes accumulate over one-hundred-eighty seconds in seeded order — paper flecks, faint margin grid, page border, twenty-six typewriter lines of dash, dot, and tick glyphs, a hatched redaction bar over one line, then a flowing signature scrawl in the lower third (single polyline with loops that return to the path, crossing flourishes, underline). At completion, exactly one action: a single purple spray-paint line strikes diagonally through the signature over one second (progress-gated core polyline plus five-hundred-twenty seeded spray particles, the hiss drift). Hold twenty seconds, crossfade to paper over five seconds via main-canvas alpha overlay (no offscreen canvas), then a newly-seeded page begins. No viewer input at all. The signature is never a legible real name; smooth vector strokes forbidden — the hand reads in the texture. Drawing as incantation, cast for healing and real justice.

title: The Dossier Wall
note: A gallery wall covered floor-to-ceiling with a ten-by-six grid of off-white dossier pages mounted on a glowing neon-pink plexiglas substrate, darkened at the edges. Each page carries pseudo-type lines (short gray dashes, never readable prose), one-to-three black redaction bars each drawn over a text block it obscures, and — on about sixty percent of pages — a stylized signature scrawl that is never a real name. Three handwritten margin notes carry the only legible words, verbatim from the prompt: HOW DO WE GET FREE?, HERE, NOW. Over the wall: a hot-pink spray-mist field biased to the left third, and gold rhinestone glints clustered near page corners like constellations. Watch-only, one-hundred-twenty-second loop: the grid pans laterally on a sine (ping-pong, so the loop never jumps), as if the camera is reading the wall; rhinestones glint on a sinusoidal pulse plus a traveling light wave sweeping the wall every fourteen seconds; spray mist slowly re-settles, each blob drifting on its own slow sine phase and breathing in alpha. Double-tap reseeds the page layout and rhinestone positions; a single tap never reloads. The pink plexi substrate is layered flat alpha shapes, not a gradient. Hostile state documents flipped and re-appropriated with pink spray and rhinestones — glitter as transcendence, escape, and survival.

title: Event Score
note: Landscape diptych, full-bleed. Left sixty-two percent: a low concave frame in shadow bronze holding a Moroccan tile grid (cobalt, white, terracotta, seeded pattern, small diamonds on cobalt tiles) with three bone-colored instruments on it — a cast-bronze conch (spiral arc fan with spire wedge and lip line), a triangular tambourine (bone triangle, copper jingle dots at corners and edge midpoints), and a flat cymbal (bone disc with shadow-bronze rim and copper center dot). Five copper wire staff-lines run horizontally across the frame; the frame's inner edge bows inward top and bottom, marking the concavity. Right thirty-eight percent: a black monitor with a thin bone frame holding three phosphor line icons (conch spiral, triangle, cymbal ellipse) above a scrolling metadata list — object names and short material notes only (CONCH - CAST BRONZE, TAMBOURINE - TRIANGLE, CYMBAL - BONE, BASIN HMM, HUM, HYMN, with intake, layering, stamping, hold, release, return timestamps). Watch-only, slow four-four pulse at one-point-one seconds per beat: each beat lights one instrument in sequence (conch, tambourine, cymbal, rest) as a soft glow decaying within the beat, with a matching ring on its monitor icon and a copper dot riding the staff line; wire vibrates faintly on beats; metadata scrolls continuously. Tap toggles the pulse between four-four and a broken seven-eight. Silent: no audio of any kind — the prompt forbids audio, so the rhythm is visual only. A bone-colored still life as a playable score — Basin Hmm, Hum, or Hymn.

title: Distilled Moment
note: A near-black field split by a two-pixel divider into two channels, each holding one excessively zoomed archival fragment — a smooth hill curve (the back of a shoulder) over a soft warm-gray body wash, with a dark hair swirl mass riding its crest. Left channel wider, right channel tighter. Caption strip eight percent at bottom reads verbatim: 72:00:00 — viewing the civil rights era archive. Abstract geometry only: never a face, never a body, always at the edge of recognition. Watch-only: the left channel holds almost still at fixed low focus with only a faint film-grain crawl; the right channel loops a twenty-second focus breath (blur to near-sharp at ten seconds to blur), so the crisp shoulder line and hair strands emerge and dissolve; channels deliberately out of phase. The archive timer starts at 72:00:00 at load and advances with piece time, so frame one is always the zero state; film grain is a closed-form seeded function of the quantized time index, never per-frame random. Never click-to-reload, no scrubbing — the viewer contends, they don't control. A dual-channel meditation on one archival fragment, the two channels never syncing.

title: Folded Like Paper
note: Gallery wall above, floor below, horizon high so every form sits on the floor. Five folded steel forms scattered across the middle ground, each rotated off-axis, never zero or ninety degrees: two photo-corners with a folded triangle flap, two dog-eared pages with a folded corner, one halved sheet with a centre seam. Each form carries a slab-thickness band along its bottom edge so the steel reads heavy, never paper-thin, and casts one long flat-alpha shadow falling consistently down-right. A small walnut bench stands at the left edge as the human-scale reference. Two tiny square photolithographs sit low near the centre, dwarfed by the steel: stacked arcs (a shoulder's curve) and a broken-arc spiral (a swirl of hair), both dissolving into seeded static speckle — surveillance imagery tipped into abstraction, no photorealistic people anywhere. Watch-only, two-minute loop: a slow orbital drift of viewpoint, forms shifting horizontally on a sine with per-form parallax factors, as if walking around the sculptures; light rakes across the folds over the same loop, so fold-shadow alpha breathes and dog-ears read alternately as paper and as steel. Drag scrubs the orbit angle. Industrial material performing ephemerality — the steel must feel HEAVY, never origami decoration; forms never align to a grid.

title: The Refusal
note: A shellac-brown studio floor with faint plank seams and scuffs, holding the stack slightly below the middle of a square panel — three cloth covers offset so each peeks out (oxblood at the top edge, ochre at the left and bottom edges, slate on top), each with a darker blank spine band on its top edge and a thin cream paper fore-edge on its right edge, no readable text anywhere. The maple block dominates the stack top, covering forty-five percent of the top book's area, with dense seeded grain lines and three knots. A small cream dog-eared triangle with a fold line peeks out at the bottom book's bottom-right corner. At frame one the raking light comes from the left, so stack and block shadows fall to the right. Watch-only, two-minute loop: the raking light rotates a full three-hundred-sixty degrees around the stack once, stack shadows and the block's shadow swinging with it, a thin cream highlight riding the block edge facing the light; the block never moves, never reveals. Double-tap rotates which book is on top. The block is BOTH surface and density, a refusal that suspends the gaze — it occludes whatever is beneath it and offers nothing in return.

title: Chromatic Ground
note: A diptych split by a visible hairline seam.
