Left panel: black ground holding a centered grayscale Riffs stack at sixty percent of panel width — shellac-dark wood floor with grain streaks and knots, a document rotated four degrees with fold line, ink scrawl doodles, and a jagged torn edge, and a snapshot rotated minus-seven degrees from the document with white border, soft gray blobs, and flat-alpha drop shadows. Right panel: deep amber field with layered gold and cream washes, flat-alpha light-leak bands at the edges, near-black vignette bands, and a thin cream paper-edge frame; the checked pattern sits at zero opacity at frame one. Two objects, not one image. Watch-only, seventy-five second loop on the right: gold washes drift on slow sines, cream washes breathe, the checked pattern fades in, holds, and fades out; the black-and-white panel is still except for a slow grain shimmer. Drag horizontally shifts the seam, clamped to thirty-two to sixty-eight percent of width; release decays it back to center. The pairing asks the viewer to think about the colors that are NOT visibly present in the black-and-white photograph — not a photograph, nor digitally produced, but darkroom exposure with paper edges.

title: Forty-Two
note: A dark monitor field with an amber timestamp top-right and a blinking white cursor block beneath it; the center holds a concrete-poetry assembly in phosphor green-white — INK AVENUE WINDOW LAMP / STOOP KITCHEN MARKET DUST / READING — staggered, no sentences, no slogans; three lanes of small gray dataset type flow along the bottom third, every seventh word in phosphor. Watch-only, sixteen-second cycle: staggered assemble, hold, reverse-stagger dissolve, empty field, then the next seeded assembly. A forty-two-second cursor cycle idles blinking, then types a seeded vocabulary word character by character, holds, deletes it, and returns to blinking — the quotidian gesture, left visible. The timestamp reads real local time quantized to whole minutes, so the frame is reproducible within the minute; only the timestamp digits change across a minute boundary. Double-tap reseeds the vocabulary pool; a single tap never reloads. The words are DATA, not message — a visualization of metadata from a dataset built by reading and free-associating images of the National Memorial African Bookstore.

title: The Lean
note: Wall plaster upper fifty-five percent, floor lower forty-five percent in perspective. A maple frame with a thin aluminum inner edge leans at eight degrees off vertical, pivoted on its bottom center, casting a long soft shadow to the right. Inside the print: a document field with a fold line, torn top-right corner, ink scrawl doodles, a pictured leaning square of wood — the form rhyming with its content — and a faded coral-and-sage snapshot with a white border, slightly rotated. At the frame's left base: three stacked clothbound books (oxblood, ochre, slate) with blank cloth backs — one spine flipped away, rebuffing the gaze — and a small leaning maple block standing on the books against the frame's edge. No glass anywhere; the panel leans, unsecured, never flat, never touching the wall. Watch-only: an almost-imperceptible sway, the panel settling one-to-two pixels over a sixty-second loop as if gravity is still deciding, then holding; a viewer-presence shimmer passes across the glassless print once per loop. Drag slightly shifts the viewpoint in parallax; release returns. The artwork is a three-dimensional object, not a flat image.

title: Three Windows
note: A square staged stack on a shellac floor filling the field — floorboards with grain lines, knots, and plank seams. The worn document page sits central at seventy percent, rotated four degrees, with a folded top-left corner, jagged torn right edge, abstract ink scrawl doodles, and a headline band of dash marks half-obscured by an ink blotch — no readable words. The snapshot sits on it at twenty-eight percent of field area, rotated minus-seven degrees from the document, white border, faded image of coral and denim blobs on sage, a pearl-dot arc, and an abstract grill grid — no faces, no real photo. The single hack reads clearly: the snapshot's top-right corner lifts and curls with its own cast shadow and highlight streak. Shadows are layered flat-alpha shapes, so the stack reads as physical staging, not a flat collage. Watch-only, ninety-second loop: a soft raking light band sweeps across the stack once, shadows shifting direction as it moves; the curled corner flutters once mid-loop and settles. Nothing else moves — a slow read. One hack only, every layer a window repeated in succession.

title: The Monster Factory
note: A dark charcoal factory floor with a horizontal conveyor line at sixty percent height and roller ticks along it. Three station zones marked by faint dashed rectangles with ground glyphs below the belt — circle, triangle, square. Three monsters visible at three production stages: a single paper disc blank at intake, a half-accreted dark stack with one toxic eye in the layering zone, and a finished beast at stamping — paper-and-ink distorted stack with spikes, toxic-green eyes, a rust patch, and a small abstract punch-card stamp glyph beside it. Watch-only: four monsters ride a seamless belt loop at fixed spacing, stage from belt position — blank, then accretion mapped linearly, then full monster plus stamp glyph; each monster's anatomy is per-monster seeded — three-to-six distorted layers, two-to-five spikes, one-to-three eyes, rust patch on about sixty percent. Stamp glyphs are abstract tick marks, never readable text or real dates. Toxic green is the single accent. Beasts produced by mechanism, not design — abstract, beastly, print-like, never cute — work presented as arriving, not finished.

title: Broadcast Slices
note: The locked portrait — kitchen-white field, an abstract seated figure with chrome headphones at a chrome counter (head ellipse, headphone band and ear cups, trapezoid torso, one arm reaching, amber cup on the counter), seeded bottle rows in green, amber, and chrome at both edges, and nine abstract stamp glyphs — diamond, ring, star, cross, bar — floating in the upper third, no readable words, no likeness. The forty strips show as thin gaps even when locked, so the slice structure reads from the first frame. Watch-only, forty-second loop: six seconds locked, eighteen seconds drifting out of sync on per-strip seeded amplitude, phase, and speed, eight seconds re-locking, eight seconds holding; three seeded strips per loop flip mirrored and stay flipped until the loop boundary. Drag scrubs the slice-offset field, decaying back after release — a system to explore the collage's permutations. The portrait is readable only when the strips lock; most of the time they drift out of sync.

title: Catching Hole
note: A square panel on a dark matte ground, white frame with a thin dark matte inner line holding a paper field inset by the twelve-percent frame margin. Seven black-and-white prints fan from a pivot at the bottom-center of the field, rotated minus-forty-five to plus-forty-five degrees, each paper white with a thin ink border, faint gray wash, and a procedurally drawn hand gesture — palm ellipse with crease arcs, wrist stub, four-to-five finger arcs, thumb arc, line art only, never photorealistic. The stack reads as one object from a distance, seven prints up close. Watch-only slow breathing: the fan gently oscillates its spread on a fourteen-second sine; one three-second diagonal glass sheen sweep crosses the field per eighteen-second cycle, clipped to the inner field. Double-tap reseeds the fan arrangement and the hand gestures; a single tap never reloads.

title: Potato-Bag Automatism
note: Kraft ground fills the frame; a single black ink line wanders the full width, starting at the left edge and ending in a pen dot near the right edge — the drawing already in progress, not a blank page. Faint blue crease polylines cross the field, rice-glue sheen tabs sit at the top and bottom margins, dashed suture seams mark the panel boundaries, and one pipe ring sits mid-field with the line passing around it, not through it. Watch-only continuous scroll: the view drifts left, the pen dot rides near the right edge, so new line always emerges at the right and drifts left, with blank kraft ahead of the pen; each candidate step is checked against the line's own history, and coming near closure visibly bends the heading away — the line never closes into anything recognizable. Drag scrubs back along the drawing's accumulated timeline; releasing resumes the forward drift. The drawing never ends, no loop-closure seams.

title: Zero State
note: A cold empty dark field holding a single cold portrait at sixty percent height — a tall head ellipse in ice outline over a faint steel wash, bone eye ellipses with ice dots, brow arcs, one long nose arc, one shallow mouth arc. No real face anywhere: the abstraction is ellipses and arcs only. Faint ice dots speckle the field and flat-alpha light-bleed streaks radiate inward from the edges. Watch-only, twenty-eight second loop: one distorted copy fades in every two seconds, up to eight — the same ellipse-and-arc portrait rotated, stretched, and offset by amounts growing with copy index, later copies more translucent like layered exposures, the last copies carrying one small blood-red streak each — the form warps toward the beast, holds and breathes, then the stack collapses back to the single cold portrait and the loop reseeds. Nothing starting to produce something.

title: Orbit Composite
note: A slate field holding a centered, densely layered mound of translucent detritus in crimson, burnt orange, ochre, bone, and teal shadow — record discs with grooves, plates, tool bars, doorknobs, plain paper slips, shard polygons, all flat alpha shapes, capped at nine layers. A large dark record with bone groove rings sits hazily at the bottom center of the pile, partially overlapped by mound items — the trapdoor that yanks the abstraction back to reality. Twelve small perspective thumbnails arc down the left edge; the first is highlighted with a bone border. Watch-only, seventy-two second loop: the composite crossfades through twelve circled perspectives, five seconds each; for six seconds one seeded view resolves crisp — zero jitter, higher alpha, the record more visible, its thumbnail highlighted — then dissolves back into layered abstraction, and the loop reseeds. No branded objects, no photorealism, no gradients.

title: Detritus Diptych
note: A centered two-to-one diptych on black ground — left panel paper white, right panel black, panels at slightly different heights to break symmetry. Left panel shows the scene crude: rough jittered detritus objects — forks, can, spool, box, glue sticks — with heavy offset shadows, hatch marks, and set-flat backdrops. Right panel shows the same scene clean: precise white-outlined shapes on black. One amber band on a single spool appears in both panels, the only warm accent. The bright seam between them is mid-glitch at frame one, drawn in deterministic offset slices. Watch-only, twenty-second build cycle: each cycle the detritus panel reassembles into a new miniature scene from a seeded generator, and the clean panel renders the same scene faithfully; the seam shimmers slowly and glitches in short slices, never a strobe; from cycle one on, a seeded flag swaps which panel is crude in about a third of cycles. Double-tap reseeds the scene pairing; a single tap never reloads. The seam is the artwork.

title: Disc Nine
note: A square kraft-paper field carrying a full center-out spiral of glyph rings — innermost crosses tight and clean at the center, then flags, medals, abstract gun silhouettes, portrait ovals, and rubble hatching cycling outward band by band in black ink, sepia, and rust, with a faint sepia spiral guide line beneath and static kraft flecks, a margin of blank kraft around the disc. Watch-only, ninety-second loop: frame one opens on the finished disc, still coherent; the outer bands then scatter, rotate, and overlap into a pile while the inner bands stay clean; the field fades to bare kraft; the spiral draws itself outward over seventy seconds, center first; then the loop reseeds. No readable text, no gore, no glorification — a long history compressed into a disc, coherence as a function of radius, until the ninth disc collapses into a pile.

title: Bloemenlust
note: A dark soil bed with a long unwinding spiral ribbon of ninety-six small pink buds across the middle band — growth just beginning, no unfurled petals yet. Watch-only, seventy-five second cycle: growth (petals unfurl in spiral order, inner turns first, into living pink), downpour (grey vertical rain streaks across the full frame, petals bow downward), rot (petals brown from the spiral's tail inward, living to rot brown to compost, center last to rot), drought (amber heat-shimmer lines, petals fully still), white bloom event (a fullscreen white flower drawn in horizontal bands with per-band jitter over a faint scan-green grid, reading like a scan image, then dissolving — neurological, not decorative), then reseed. Drag stirs petals locally as wind without breaking the cycle. No pretty-flower wallpaper — rot is half the palette; the long unwinding spiral of rot and fertility.

title: Le Chiffonnier
note: A soft-lit sorting room with calm negative space in the upper half and four open-top bins in a row across the lower half, receding slightly left to right — each a thin steel line cage holding a translucent cotton membrane, with a seeded pile of small scraps peeking above its rim in its category color: indigo, madder, undyed, black, and eight loose scraps resting on the piles. Drag-to-sort: dragging a scrap lifts it; releasing over a bin arcs it in, the pile grows and the cotton bulges slightly; releasing elsewhere arcs it back. If left alone, the system performs its own slow resorting — every sixteen seconds a scrap lifts, arcs to another bin, and settles; the ragpicker's care continues without you. Bins breathe slowly with cotton bulging; stitch lines shimmer faintly on hover. No gamification, no scores, no timers, no overflowing mess — the bins stay tidy, the care is the point, the refuse treated as treasure: now homed, protected, and sheltered in these carriers.

title: Code of Points
note: Riso paper with static grain flecks and generous margins, carrying three horizontal score bands, each with its own beam line and a trace dot parked at the left margin — top band dense black dot-dash runs, middle airier teal loops with a faint two-pixel misregistration second pass, bottom sharp coral angular bursts with a faint three-pixel offset second pass. All marks ahead of the heads render faint; the field is legible but unplayed. Watch-only: each band's trace dot runs its routine left to right at its own fixed tempo, then the band reseeds to a different routine fragment, the three running independently and phase-drifting. Drag slows or speeds the nearest band's tempo, like holding the paper. No gymnast figures, no beam apparatus, no Olympic marks — only the score, scored as rhythmic mark sequences: dense dot-dash runs for Comaneci 1976, airier loops for Miller 1996, sharp angular bursts for Biles 2016.

title: 37 Fouettes
note: Paper-white ground with a very faint cellulose-weave grid; two staff lines in the upper third carrying fourteen abstract Labanotation-style glyphs — diamond, hook, ring, triangle, chevron, double bar — at seeded irregular spacing, no metronome regularity; the reading head, a vertical ink line with a dot, parked at the staff start; the pirouette field below empty, awaiting triggers. The score plays left to right automatically over a forty-second loop; each glyph triggers its fouette when the head passes — a particle spinning outward in tightening spirals, thirty-two turns, leaving faint circular trails that fade aggressively so they never clutter. Dragging the head scrubs the score; dragging backward rewinds and re-triggers. Each fouette carries a one-in-thirty-two chance of being the one vermillion failed fouette, rolled from a seeded sequence, so the chance is real and reproducible. Glyphs are abstract marks, dancers absent — language, movement, pattern and material embodiment.

title: Tarp & Tempo
note: Storm-sky ground, two long panels hanging in the left and right thirds with a visible gap of sky between them, never touching — the left weathered tarp olive with flat fold shading, five stitched patch squares with dashed stitch borders, and a zigzag frayed bottom hem; the right new tarp pale blue-grey, clean, with fold shading and a subtle light hem band — distinguishable from the weathered panel at all times. A single rope line with a slight sag runs across the bottom third behind the panels, and faint moire shimmer lines cross the gap. Watch-only: a shared wind field of slow sine gusts drives both panels; over a forty-five second loop the new panel's billow, period, and lag converge toward the weathered panel's — it learns the memory — without ever fully synchronizing; the half-beat lag is the point. Drag is a gust both panels answer, the new one slightly later. Tarps are work covers, no flag or sailboat reading.

title: Interrupted Factory
note: A dim room with a floor line and empty negative space above, holding four bare-steel sewing apparatuses in a loose receding row: a thread stand with the single warning-red spool and a glowing taut gold thread; a sewing machine on a table with a sagging idle thread; a second stand under a slipped dust cover, its narrow drape slanting with the rod visible below; a halted machine with its thread hanging slack to a small coil. The giant needle stands foreground right, eye slot near its top end, shaft exiting the frame bottom edge — a tool first, a weapon only by scale. A faint silver web fan sits top-left. Watch-only, ninety-second cycle: each apparatus moves through WORK (thread taut, faint vibration) to IDLE (thread sags) to COVERED (a cover descends and swallows it) to HALTED, never all covered at once; the web adds one thread per cycle and never resets; at a fixed point each cycle one apparatus swerves — its thread snaps taut and quivers, then relaxes. Interrupted work — or possibly closed, or possibly liquidation had begun — but the mood is grief, not threat.

title: Umi
note: Three long fabric tubes hang from the top edge across the central span — deep eggplant purple, sand linen, purple again — with flat fold-shading bands, raw edge lines, and irregular barnacle-like offcut flaps stitched along both edges, clustered denser toward the bottoms, gravity-sorted. A faint horizontal tide line sits behind at mid-height on near-black ground. Watch-only with drag: each tube sways as a pendulum on its own slow period, flaps fluttering slightly out of phase; a horizontal drag is a wind gust that sets the tubes swinging and the flaps fluttering, decaying back to the tide rhythm. The tubes read as shrouds, not flags — no gloss, no bright purple, no people, no hands: costume becomes shroud becomes ceremonial remnant.

title: The Tailor
note: A charcoal-black field with an EMPTY center in roughly human-torso proportions, ringed by ten translucent offcut polygons at the periphery — pattern-piece negatives with concave armhole curves, notched necklines, and long selvedge edges, drawn in warm linen fill with aged-brass contour thread and dashed inner seams, two overlapping like pinned pattern layers, one the single deep-red tailor's-chalk interrupt at the bottom. Watch-only: the offcuts drift in slow elliptical orbits, rotating a few degrees per loop; over each sixty-second cycle one offcut slides slightly toward the center, then retreats — it refuses its confines. Drag gently perturbs the drift; the offcuts yield, then settle back, and the center stays empty even under drag. No body rendered anywhere; nothing looks like clothing, only its leftovers — the contours and transparency index an absent body, a body that refuses its confines, and a body remembered.

title: Tent for Close Readings
note: The viewer inside a shamiana: six block-printed cotton panels in madder red, indigo, and cream radiating from an implied apex above the top edge, filling the whole frame with no outside visible — each panel its own print-and-dye combination of diamonds, triangles, dots, and rings, the two center panels carrying the strongest motif, side panels fading toward the edges, dashed stitch lines along the panel edges with gold beading dots on beaded panels. Slow watch-only drift: the panels breathe on long sines and the light through the cloth strengthens and dims in long cycles; a gentle pointer drag pans the view slightly inside the tent with depth-scaled parallax between panel layers. No tent poles, no structure, no people, no sky — the cloth is the architecture, panels lifted off the block printer's table and simply hung in the sky.

title: Rabari Embroidery
note: A deep indigo achadiya field, full-bleed, with soft pale ghost washes and faint ghost block motifs beneath — and bright Dhebariya Rabari embroidery creeping across it in bands on gentle diagonals: chain stitches in orange, pink, and green forming mirror-centered rosettes and zigzag bands, plus buttonhole-edged patches, each band visibly detouring around the palest ghost areas rather than crossing them, forcing a more careful reading of the cloth beneath. Five seeded mirror rosettes sit along the bands, each a small mirror center with ten radiating chain stitches. Embroidery covers well under forty percent; the indigo shows. Drag to embroider: a needle-following stitch line extends from the last rosette toward the pointer, laying chain stitches, the thread color cycling per rosette; double-tap places a mirror rosette; mirrors glint on pointer pass. Watch-only otherwise — nothing happens without the drag. No symmetrical mandalas, no neon threads: motifs cluster and wander like hand embroidery.

title: Kabir's Cloth
note: A square khadi-paper panel centered on a darker warm-brown ground, deckled edge visible on all sides with a soft offset shadow, faint wash blobs and fibre flecks on the paper — bare paper at first frame, no weave, no scrawls, no glint yet. Watch-only, twenty-eight second loop: a shuttle line weaves left to right laying fourteen horizontal lines with slight sag, then three hands draw scrawls in sequence — ink, tighter and slower; indigo, faster and looser; madder, fastest and loosest — with a small recycled-plastic glint fading in at the top-left corner, well under five percent of the frame; the cloth holds full, then the loop sheds back to bare paper and reseeds. The scrawls suggest script without forming any real words or letterforms of any script. Drawing as marks by many hands: the weaver-saint whose songs accrued authorship over centuries.

title: The Block Carver's Table
note: A woodblock seen face-on at left in warm teak with wavy stylized grain, bevel highlights, and a depth side — its ajrakh rosette carved in reverse, recessed dark outlines with cut-highlight ticks — beside a thin vertical rule and the print it produced at right in black on cream, showing the same motif correct-reading with three mis-registered impressions fading down-right and registration crosshairs at the corners, a faint blue grid behind everything. Watch-only: the block rests, a roller pass inks its face, it stamps with a small lift, the ink starves a little with each stamp, and mid-loop one petal groove deepens as the carver re-carves it. The motif is seeded once for the whole piece, so block and print always agree — the print shows the same motif, as the process demands. Stylized drawn wood, no literal hand: the hand is implied through the stamp action.

title: Suspended Canopy
note: Four long indigo cloths hang from a single suspension line, thin black cables running from each cloth top edge to the frame top — one cloth double-width — their ends pooling and folding on the floor line with shallow fold shadows and raw cotton hems on two cloths. Pale ghost-resist marks ride the fabric — diamond outlines, crosses, dash clusters, rings — with two to four flat-diamond mirror dots per cloth. Drag horizontally to stir a gentle air current: the cloths sway, hems lift slightly, then settle with damped oscillation, a slow idle sway continuing. The whole piece is a drawing made of hanging fabric, cloth lifted off the printer's table and never stretched or framed. Matte and deep throughout — no plastic look, no bunting feel.

title: Mill Owners, Repeating
note: A full-bleed madder-red field covered edge to edge with a strict block-printed repeat of near-black architectural triangles — each a right triangle plus a separate diagonal fin floating parallel to its hypotenuse, the diagonal brises-soleil of Le Corbusier's Mill Owners' Association Building abstracted into geometry — with occasional gray offset double-stamps every fifth motif showing the hand. Three brighter-red applique rectangles interrupt the most regular areas, each with a complete dashed stitch border. Watch-only: the blocks stamp on one at a time in back-and-forth order with tiny rotation errors, then the patches stitch on, then the repeat holds and breathes slightly, then the loop reseeds its mis-registration map. The repeat reads as block-printed, not digital — and turning the building into an ornament pokes at modernism's no-repetition rule while venerating the building itself.

title: Mirror-Drawing
note: A centered square field of deep cloth on night-indigo ground, crossed by a faint weave, holding a loose spiral of sixteen small irregular mirror shards — five-to-seven-vertex polygons, generous gaps — and a warm light pinpoint parked at the top of the field, clear of every shard. No glint at frame one: the field feels empty until the light comes. Drag anywhere to carry the light and a shard glints — brief white flash plus an expanding ring — only when the carried light crosses it; on release the light slows and parks. Mirrors never glint on their own. The spiral reads as a drawn line that only exists where light hits: drawing with mirrors on cloth, after the Kutch lippankam mud-mirror craft.

title: Ghost Prints
note: A long horizontal cloth band, middle two-thirds, raw cotton edges top and bottom: at first frame it is un-dyed pale ground, no ghosts, no mirrors — the reveal is the piece. Over a twenty-four second loop a slow indigo wash develops from the edges inward, and five staggered rows of worn-down ajrakh-style ghost impressions fade UP out of the wash row by row in stamping order — diamond, diamond rosette with dot quartet, square-with-dot, all slightly doubled and mis-registered, one row carrying a clear double-stamp near the left third — then exactly four irregular-pentagon mirror shards near the center glint once, and the loop sheds back to pale. Everything looks developed, not drawn; loop reseeds run on a seeded sequence, so repeated loads produce the same pattern order. The printer's drop cloth, salvaged and dyed indigo, developing like a photograph: every block ever stamped on it, revealed as ghosts.

title: Grandmother's Garden
note: A low intimate viewpoint: the viewer kneels in a green Canadian garden looking slightly up at a Punjabi grandmother in a bright magenta sari with gold trim, seen from behind with no face detail, dominating the upper two-thirds, her arms reaching down-forward to two hands kneading a brown earth mound at center. Nine rows of leaf-cluster plants converge to a high vanishing point, tiny at the horizon and larger toward the foreground, over soft green washes, framed by a thin dashed red phulkari border with diamond corners. The leaves sway in slow waves; the hands work the earth in a small repetitive kneading loop. Drag upward to stand slightly — the viewpoint rises a few degrees and the garden tilts — release to kneel again. Seen as a family member might, kneeling low, hands in the earth: work carried out by women's hands, documented, not sentimentalized.

title: Madhur's Phulkari
note: A dark 16:9 film frame kept whole: a glowing ember phulkari cell field — diamond outlines, X dashes, plus dashes, squares with dots — covers it, while six small chalk figures stand off-center in the rudimentary hand-drawn register: a couple weeping black tears left of center, three small marchers right, one lone bowed figure far right. Over a seamless forty-eight second loop the cells dim from the edges inward, then four diagonal black scrawls sweep through and swallow the figures, and finally the scrawls fade, the cells restore, and the figures draw themselves back in stroke by stroke, returning exactly to the start. Drag stirs the scrawls briefly; watch-only by default. Slow and mournful, no jump scares: a requiem for a craft industry extinguished following Partition, and for the displacement the phulkari pattern haunts.

title: The Great Divide
note: A tall narrow vertical scroll in the original's 27:76 proportion: an embroidered river in deep blue runs its full length, slightly off-center with a gentle meander, widening toward the bottom, light flow streaks running down it. Muslin banks carry flat wash texture and red phulkari dash bands along both river banks; tiny ink marchers walk both banks, small at top and larger at bottom, one crosser visible on the river. Top and bottom bands hold prayer-verse fields as sewn-dash stitch rows — deliberately no legible wording and no fabricated Gurmukhi, since the prompt specs verse fields but gives no verse text. The river flows downward continuously in a seamless loop; drag upstream to slow the flow and the figures lean harder against it; release and the flow resumes. No literal map lines, no national borders — the divide is the river, not a cartographic statement. Borders that both frame and divide.

title: Mango Choga
note: A draped robe form — a mango-shaped choga, full-length, standing centered on plain dark ground with no horizon line. Fifty-eight Kashmiri Ambi motifs tile it exactly, denser at the hem: mango teardrop outlines with inner spirals, every curve drawn in cotton-thread dashes with seeded jitter, in crimson, teal, saffron, and rose infill. The paisleys slowly unfurl in a traveling wave, each spiral rotating open a few degrees and closing; drag across the robe and the paisleys near the touch bloom open fully, then relax. No symmetrical mandala, no glossy vector paisleys — every motif is a hand-stitched dash construction. The Ambi motif as cultural DNA, carried in cloth.

title: Never Say Goodbye
note: A grid of portrait frames like sticker-book collectables — twelve shoulders-up singer portraits in slightly rotated cream frames, arranged 3x4 against a chalky pink washed background, with hand-drawn love-hearts and decorative bubble-word balloons scattered between them, the whole like a childhood poster. Every portrait is procedural and generic — five headwear variants, dot eyes, dash mouths — no real names, no real likenesses. The portraits sway gently out of sync; drag horizontally to stir the wash and the frames lean while the hearts bob; tap a portrait and it glows warm for a few seconds, like a stage light catching it. A hall of fame for the voices of a culture whose club scene became a place where external markers could be exceeded.

title: Quilt Sandwich
note: Four physical strata stacked as one object, hanging slightly askew on ink ground: a drawn paper layer (sepia vignette of hands holding a photograph), a batting layer (soft white puff with scalloped edges), a bordered fabric layer (deep-red cloth with a gold phulkari dash border), and a dark binding rim, bound into a small quilt. It breathes gently — the batting swells and the strata separate by fractions of a pixel. Drag a corner to lift it and the layers peel slightly apart, paper lagging most, then settle with a spring. Tap the binding edge to trace a fresh baste stitch along the rim. It reads as physical textile, not a flat card: mixed media on paper, sewn with bordered fabric, batted, basted, binded into a quilt.

title: The Red Ghost
note: A black-and-white archival drawing of farmworkers laboring in a field — grayscale figures bent over crop rows, loose graphite washes, agitated mark edges, the whole scene slightly askew like an old photograph. Crossing it diagonally from lower-left to upper-right, one fiery-red ghost figure strides, semi-transparent and glowing against the monochrome, larger than the workers. The scene advances at eight frames a second with a visible 1-2 pixel step, hand-held animation feel; the ghost's red intensity breathes slowly. Drag the ghost and it resists, trailing ember streaks, before snapping back to its path. No blood, no literal violence — the ghost is color-as-data: violence, exploitation, trauma, and loss as the one chromatic intruder in a monochrome archive.

title: Beautiful Zameen
note: A hand-stitched textile on muslin: a central drawn vignette of farmers' hands holding crops and a photograph, rendered in loose washes over a sepia ground, framed by a thick indigo phulkari border of dense darn-stitch diamond cells in mustard, red, and cotton white, the stitching jittered so it reads hand-sewn. Two draped figures — one in handspun-silk red, one in field green — meet at center where two hands hold a small askew cream photograph, cotton plants with white bolls in the foreground, field rows converging behind at a kneeling viewpoint. Along the bottom band, Raina's own sewn verse stitches itself in word by word over thirty seconds: please strip them of these / chemical cotton flowers / let them cling to peace. Drag across the border and the darn-stitch rows ripple outward, compressing, then relaxing. Stillness lets a slow breeze pass through the cotton flowers. No fabricated Gurmukhi anywhere — the verse is his actual English line only.

title: Wonder Women
note: A field of vintage-sari fragments, dark and dense in six deep indigo shades, across which female figures repeat in a loose procession — flat sari-print silhouettes in magenta, marigold, peacock, and rose at varying scales, walking left to right, never marching in step. Forty-two small warm LED dots glow and pulse across the field, scattered, never on a grid. The procession drifts and loops around; drag downward and the field dims, the figures sinking into the dark while only the LEDs stay lit; release and it restores. Not a neon sign — small warm dots, her first light worked into the sari surface.

title: A Mended Heart
note: A torn heart-shaped form hangs at center on ink ground, suspended from two thread lines, its wound a jagged vertical tear. Seven oversized stitches bridge it — crochet-thread X-stitches and running-stitch dashes alternating in cream, rose, and gold floss. Over a forty-four second loop the stitches pull the tear closed, hold, then ease it open again — and the gap never reaches zero: eighteen percent of the open width remains at full heal. Drag across the wound and a new stitch animates in and joins the loop. No cartoon heart, no medical imagery. The repair stitch is the compositional line, and the point is the ongoing mending: it never fully heals.

title: Nomads, Dreamers
note: Six mirror-polished steel pods stand in a circle on dark ground, each draped with a monumental sari tapestry — magenta, emerald, and cobalt fields with gold trim and seeded gold diamonds, the cloth spilling from the pod tops to the earth. Five braided-sari phala globes hang on thin lines between them, low garden tufts run the ground line, and one small walker silhouette crosses between the pods. The tapestries sway on their own phases; drag horizontally to stir a breeze and the sway rises, then settles. Tap a pod and it catches the light in a bright sweep across its face. Exactly six pods. No literal park, no skyline — this is the monument, not the place. A monument to the state of becoming.

title: She Arose
note: A circular pool fills the frame edge to edge on deep plum ground — concentric rings of braided worn-sari ropes in cobalt, magenta, marigold, and ivory, crossing and interweaving, trailing off beyond the frame, no floor line. At its center the dancer exists only as braid density: nine interweaving near-vertical braids, two fanning bundles raised like arms, a small tangle of partial loops where a head would be. Remove the density and there is no figure at all. The braid field breathes on a slow sine; drag upward and she rises, braids streaming downward like hair in water; drag downward and she sinks, braids gathering. No literal body, no face. A state of becoming.

title: Kala Pani
note: A square panel of aged paper: an invented colonial engraving in crosshatch lines and ornamental borders, faded ink on tea-stained ground — a three-arch colonnade, a domed pavilion, diamond motifs, corner rosettes, no real print copied anywhere. Over it, embroidery: floral vines and a female face stitched in marigold, deep green, and crimson floss, denser where the architecture sits, the thread curves partially obscuring the print beneath. On load the engraving fades in first, then the embroidery stitches over it; drag over a stitched region and the stitches lift slightly, then settle. Stand still and the engraving dims, leaving the thread as the lasting image. Brown reclamation: the stitch outlasts the print.

title: Wedded Bliss
note: Two large facing forms built from layered sari textiles — bridal red with sari-gold bands at left, shadow indigo with red bands at right — stand across a center gap, neither touching the other. Between them, twenty-eight pink floss stitches in seven rows bridge the gap like sutures, pulsing faintly. Drag a figure to lean it toward or away and the stitches stretch, tighten, or slacken; release and both return slowly. No hearts, no romance iconography. The union here is about suturing, not sweetness — a family's history as indentured laborers, and the trauma that moves through generations, held together by thread.

title: Self-Portrait in Thread
note: An antique tapestry hangs in ruins — sixteen irregular fragments of faded damask and umber, visibly torn at the edges, pieced together with charcoal seams. On it, a female figure draws herself entirely in thread: short chain-stitch dashes in magenta and rust tracing her silhouette and face, dash by dash over twenty seconds, then holding. At first frame only the top arc of the head is down. Tap and hold a region and it re-stitches itself, dashes fading and redrawing. Drag a fragment edge and the tapestry nudges and settles. No smooth vector lines anywhere — every line reads as thread.

title: The Sea Wall
note: A tall textile wall hangs across the frame, floor to top, pieced from vintage-sari fragments in jewel tones — magenta, turmeric, peacock, aged ivory — dense with bindi and bead dot fields, embroidery-floss contours, tassels and trim along the seams. One unbroken horizontal opening runs through it slightly above middle, gold-trimmed on both edges, and beyond it layered sea and sky: horizon pale above, sea deep below with slow shimmer lines. The wall sways faintly. Drag across the opening and it widens — more sea revealed, the fragments pulling apart at the edges — then stillness lets it narrow again. The wall in Guyana prevents a clear view of the horizon; here the opening is the freedom.

title: Mamabot Assembly
note: A tender, awkward robot assembled from picture frames, standing in a soft spotlight pool on dark ground. Its head frame holds a crayon panel — sun, house, wobbly ground line; its torso a sepia interior — window, table, rug; its arms folded letters, tea-stained, stamped. The whole body is wrapped in breathing paper skin. It works on loop, automatic, a little weary: thirty-six seconds of reach, tidy, rock. Drag a limb and it adopts your dragged path as its new task. Double-tap and a new memory-frame stacks along its torso. Every panel is a procedural abstraction — no real photographs anywhere. Handmade, framed, awkward, tender.

title: Nagging Ribbons
note: Korean commemorative ribbons cascade from gold rosettes across the top of a dark ground — white, red, blue — each lettered in gold with a loving nag in English and romanized Korean: call your mother, wear a jacket, did you eat?, your metro card is empty, text me when you arrive. Twelve phrases, no more, specific over volume. Along the bottom, a ticker scrolls Seoul LED bus-board etiquette: please yield your seat to the elderly, let passengers off first, mind the gap. Tap a ribbon and it folds itself into a name-tag bearing a retranslated name variant, gathering in the corner cluster, while a fresh ribbon respawns in its slot. Overbearing and wry, never cruel.

title: Mismatched Karaoke
note: A noraebang screen split into two scrolling lanes: above, a stylized Colorado drive — red-rock mesas under a flat yellow sun; below, a Seoul drive at night — palace blocks with upturned blue roofs and magenta and cyan neon. The subtitle ball bounces across the lower third, and the subtitles are original nonsense verses in English and romanized Korean that slowly desync and mistranslate each other: the moon rides a yellow bus to Denver. Tap a line to 'correct' it and it mistranslates harder. Drag to scrub both lanes together. The song never ends, and it is entirely silent — the ball, the lanes, and the drifting subtitles carry it. Melancholy and funny, never mocking.

title: Complex Silence
note: A nine-foot microphone looms in a dark room, and it only whispers. Sixteen seeded text fragments — half-translated memories, self-reflection shards — rise from the grille on slow cycles, bone-italic: I left my name at the airport; the rain in Seoul smells like home. The response is inverted and never explained: tap near the mic and it hushes, fragments thinning and scattering; stand still five seconds and the soundscape swells, fragments multiplying, the mic swaying. No volume control, no meter, no loud payoff. The instrument of amplification, nine feet tall, that refuses to amplify.

title: Vacuum Topography
note: A landscape of lumpy, plastic-sheathed forms: the ghosts of packed memory objects pressed flat — a photo frame, a shoe, a book — rendered in matte cast aluminum with a graphite wash, personal ephemera read as geological strata. The packing cycle runs twenty-four seconds: relaxed, compressed to less than half its relief, sealed, then sprung back with a small overshoot. Drag anywhere and the terrain dimples and seals under your hand; release and it breathes back over four seconds. Four graphite strata bands follow the profile, and a red dashed stitch runs the crest.

title: Knot Seen
note: Cords hang from the top edge like an exhibition wall, and one by one the knots tie themselves: maedeup braids, butterfly knots, chrysanthemum knots, each from its own seed, drawn as a stroke along the curve over eight seconds, then swaying on its cord. The field stays asymmetric and hand-tied, crimson and hemp on ink-dark ground. Drag a knot down to stretch it and it rebounds, re-tying itself over two and a half seconds. Double-tap and a new seeded knot ties at a free anchor. No perfect symmetry, no clip-art knots.

title: Proper Table Setting
note: A round table seen from above, turning one slow revolution every five minutes like a lazy susan. It opens with a single hanji-white cast: a Korean bowl in celadon with spoon and chopsticks. Tap a setting and it lifts and turns while its story shows — plain, specific, never sentimental: set for the sister who never visits. Tap the guest book at the center and a new seeded setting casts itself in over ten seconds, capped at nine. Drag empty space to turn the table yourself. No setting ever sits at exact center.

title: Second Skin Suitcase
note: A battered suitcase at 3/4 view on a dark ground, being wrapped in real time. The paper skin cycles the Joomchi phases, twelve seconds each: soak, when the sheet goes translucent and slack; beat, when violent ripples cross it; crumple, when sharp folds bite in; wring, when it twists; felt, when it smooths into a tight hide-like second skin with stippled texture. The latches and seams press through like a frottage. Drag the amber corner handle and the skin pulls tighter — it resists, then yields. Hold to mist the paper and restart the phase. The violence of the beating reads as craft, not damage.

title: Tooth or Dare
note: Two flat collage figures across a small table with a shared plate of four morsels between them. Tap one and it feeds the other: the morsel arcs across with a wobble, and your drag during the flight steadies it. Steady enough and the receiver's paper mouth opens, the steel cheek-retractors stretching its corners, and the two lean a little closer. Fumble it and the morsel drops, splats on the table, and they lean a little apart. The distance between them is the whole record — no hearts, no scores, no win state. Awkward and tender, never crude.

title: Ghillie Suit Parade
note: A white gallery, a runway at the lower third, and a parade of ghillie suits walking it one at a time — burlap figures covered in procedural leaves in three greens, rustling, drifting off, regrowing as they go. Tap a figure and the audience completes it: twenty fresh leaves grow in. Drag one and it slows into a pose, arms raised, shedding leaves at two a second while you hold it. Strip one bare and all that is left is a naked outline, still walking. Absurd and joyful, a gallery prank, not a uniform.

title: Workmare Lamp
note: A night desk, lit only by a lamp built from office junk: a mug for a base, a binder-clip arm, a sticky-note shade. Around the dial at the corner, a strobe you set yourself from 1 to 12 Hz — but the flicker never leaves the lamp's glow and never tops about 8 Hz, so the room itself stays dark. In the flicker, crude stop-motion anxiety creatures scurry: a mop with legs, a door with a face, a jittery coffee ring. Too fast and they freeze mid-pose; too slow and the dark swallows them. Tap one and it stops, pinned as a specimen with its label: desk anxiety no.1, no.2, no.3. Double-tap and the desk repopulates.

title: Oracle Walk
note: A dim gallery wall holds sixteen faint framed pieces, and two gold lines: hold your question in mind; when you are ready, press and hold to be blindfolded. The walk is near-black, led by a guide hand that catches up to your drags at a capped pace — you are led, not driving. Pieces breathe brighter as the hand passes. Tap within reach exactly once and the blindfold lifts on one piece, large and framed, with its commentary and a question back for you. Then the walk ends. Reach the wall's end uncalled and that, too, is an answer.

title: Making Time (Boredom Engine)
note: A surveillance corner in an empty gallery: a clock contraption with correctly meshed brass gears, a desk of blank forms, an empty tray, an empty frame on the wall, REC running at 00:00:00. Nobody is here, and nobody comes until you do the one ritual the piece demands: drag your phone into the dashed PHONES box. Only then do the three Boredom Engagement Specialists enter and begin their patrols — adjusting the clock, staring at the empty frame, carrying forms to the tray. Tap to file a form yourself; drag to nudge a specialist off script. Boredom, professionally engaged.

title: Genesis (Living Portrait)
note: A serene plaster profile on black, eyes closed, while a mycelium colony grows slowly across its face. Cream filaments fan from the ear, the jaw, the hairline — 820 segments of seeded growth, revealed by a front that advances one compressed day at a time. Hold to mist and the growth triples its pace; the counter reads day 2 at first frame, day 7 at full coverage. The colony skirts the eye and the mouth while it is young. Double-tap to reseed a new colony. Serene, not horror: a portrait becoming a garden.

title: Soil/Soul Zoetrope
note: A paper zoetrope drum on a plinth in a dark, star-speckled room. Twelve frames tell one ritual: a cow-horn is buried, and roots reach down to a star reflected in the soil below. Nothing moves on its own — you crank it. Drag the crank in circles, or push the drum, and it coasts to a stop on its own friction. Tap to lift the slit mask and watch the frames blur into motion. The horn's burial is the same act whether you spin fast or slow; the speed only changes how often you see it.

title: Acausal Portal Field
note: A dark field of ten ink objects, each inside its own pulsing gold ring: an eclipse portrait, a brass fork, a coin, a key, a marble, a leaf, a record, a postcard, a button, a bus ticket. Linger two seconds inside a ring and the object opens into a portal — it grows large, the field dims to ghosts behind it, and its story tells itself one phrase at a time. Drag an object and it stays where you put it, permanently. Tap empty field and you contribute a new object of your own, with a story the piece invents for it. Nothing here is a picture of a portal; the field itself is the registry, and it only ever grows.

title: Irretrievable Replies
note: A letter being read aloud, one word at a time. When a word has an image — lake, door, house — a faint sepia picture blooms above the line and fades. But nearly half the words bloom nothing: her replies were never printed, so the gap just stays empty, typeset as a row of underscores in the text. "I have a million things to tell you" — and no way to retrieve them. Drag to scrub the reading back and forth.

title: Traverse
note: A small figure tries to walk through a mountain. It leans in with both hands flat on the rock, trembling, then slides back, brushes itself off, looks up, and tries again further along the slope. Every minute, another attempt. The mountain — huge, calm, snow-capped — does not react, ever. Tap and the figure sits down facing it for a while. Defeat as rest. It will not get through.

title: Theater of the Mind
note: Two eyes in the dark, cropped tight, and nothing else. They look left, and behind them a doorway you can barely see brightens; they look up, and a hand-shaped ghost stirs. The story plays out in the theater of the mind, synced to the gaze — fixation, saccade, blink. Drag, and the piece looks where you pull. Tap, and it blinks for two full seconds of pure black.

title: Grey Areas
note: Forms that never resolve: something almost a hand, something almost a cloud, drifting in a field while a threshold slides back and forth beneath them. Edges sharpen for a moment — a palm, fingers — then dissolve back into fog, rust flecks at the dissolving edge. A classification bar at the bottom tracks the threshold, helpfully, while nothing ever gets classified. What is the exact moment it is not OK? Drag to push the threshold yourself.

title: It's Just the TV
note: A dark living room at dusk, a boxy television glowing, and on its screen the family ritual: video feedback — the camera pointed at its own picture, spiraling inward in warm amber and magenta, soft as phosphor. A sepia family photograph keeps dissolving into the recursion. The room barely moves; the feedback does all the work. Drag to deepen the spiral, tap to drop the photo in again.

title: Greeting Algorithm
note: A small soft-bodied someone crosses a pale desert to greet a saguaro: it leans its whole body against the cactus and holds the hug for half a minute. Then it goes to the boulder and lies along its slope, mirroring the angle. Then back to the cactus. Greeting, not conquering — it never climbs, never plants anything, and it has no face. Each greeting lasts as long as it lasts.

title: Held Empty Frame
note: The camera holds an empty golden-hour field — low sun, one tree, long shadows — for forty seconds of almost nothing: a heat shimmer, a single blade of grass twitching. Then a small figure crosses the whole frame, leans against the tree for a while, and leaves. The field returns to stillness, and holds again. What happens when nothing happens is the piece. Tap to skip ahead to the entrance.

title: Archive of Things
note: A lumen print, developing in real time: a lemon, grapes, beans and leaves lie on dark paper as near-black silhouettes while a pale sun crosses on a slow arc. Where the light lingers, the emulsion blooms — the lemon opens into orange and acid-green wedges, the grapes go magenta on the sun side, the beans stay silver a while longer. Nothing here is fast. The print only accumulates; drag to change the sun's speed, tap to hold it still over one specimen.

title: Key Phrase
note: A very cheerful language app. The owl says: IT IS NOT YOUR LAND. The owl says: YOU HAVE NO CULTURE. The owl says: WE DO NOT THINK. After every card, a big green checkmark slams in — "Correct!" — and holds for two full seconds, a little too long. The streak flame climbs and never falls. The app notices nothing wrong, ever. Tap to keep studying.

title: A Space for Reflection
note: A dark room, three tall mirrors, and a speaker on a rotating mount sweeping a visible amber beam — LRAD sound made spatial, and harmless. Where the beam strikes a mirror it bounces, thinner and brighter, and each bounce spawns expanding teal rings: the sound filling the space, disorienting or pleasing. The sweep takes a full minute. Drag to re-aim the speaker yourself; it will resume its slow rotation when you let go.

title: Button Pusher
note: A year's worth of nervous-habit photographs, tiled: 360 tiny procedural snapshots — doorways, pigeons, cup shadows, cracked windshields, empty chairs — filling a calendar grid over two minutes, each landing crooked with a soft xerox thump. No captions anywhere; the photos explain nothing, because they were never taken for you. They are the residue of moving through space with a camera as a buffer. Tap a tile to look closer. Drag to flip through finished years.

title: Lurkin' Hard
note: Someone else's abandoned camera roll, zine-flipped: a blurry dog, a party with the flash too bright, a motel pool at dusk, a birthday cake mid-collapse, a thumb over the lens, and every eighth frame blank leader. Sprocket holes, light leaks, red-eye, crooked horizons — rescued, never curated. In the corner, a counter reads "garbage bag: 214 rolls unprocessed". It never decreases. Swipe to browse the roll.

title: Scream but Not Cry
note: A white flag burning on the Racetrack Playa. The burn line crawls up the cloth; press and hold to scream, and the flame grows, the embers lift, the flag whips harder — and nothing else changes. The rocks keep their faint trails until the rain comes and erases them, on schedule, whether you screamed or not. Screaming only consumes the flag faster. That is the whole piece, and it has no text in it at all.

title: Five States of Freedom
note: Five abandoned military sites at night — a bunker, a silo, a radar post, a fenced compound, a watchtower — each with a small placard: "FBI raid, 1987", "wildlife refuge, 2005", "subdivisions at the fence line". Tap a site and its flasher fires: hard white bursts strobe the concrete for four seconds, and the ground stays scorched where the light landed. The scorch accumulates all session. Evidence, not decoration. Drag to pan the strip.

title: Uncontrollable Misinterpretation
note: An artist's talk about censorship that censors itself as it scrolls: proper nouns first, then verbs, then everything, black bars slamming down mid-sentence until no complete sentence survives anywhere on the page. "They used the word uncontrollable in the memo" — parts of it, anyway. A gasp strip along the bottom notches with each deletion and a tally counts the words removed. Tap any surviving word to censor it yourself. It will not be restored.

title: Noise Karaoke
note: A karaoke machine that sings nonsense: Dada syllables bounce across a red-framed screen — "blEEshheeeff mmpeepmmpeess gruh kroTRANG" — each one lit yellow as the beat lands, a ball hopping word to word, while a green crowd waveform below pulses like a whole room yelling. Every thirty seconds the screen glitches down to a whisper: tiny grey syllables crawling, the crowd nearly flat. Drag to change the tempo; the room yells faster or slower, but never stops embracing the nonsense.

title: Nothing To See Here
note: A dark room, a projector, and a curated program that never channel-surfs: found sepia snapshots rescued from abandoned cameras ("found, not taken"), a sound-first piece where waveforms bloom into geometry, a lo-fi band melting into VHS, a one-minute protest-etiquette flash — with an academy leader countdown between reels and a chalk placard beside the screen: "pay what you can", "sound first", "underrepresented mediums welcome". Swipe to help the projectionist change reels.

title: The Air We Breathe
note: Shared air, made visible and unequal: five horizontal bands of sky, the clear blue thinnest at the top, the chemical amber murk thickest at the bottom. Smell ribbons drift through, labeled — sweetgrass and cut grass ride high; diesel, exhaust, smoke and wildfire sink. At the center, lungs drawn as branching trees breathe on a twelve-second cycle that never changes tempo; on each inhale the ribbons bend toward them. Press and hold to slow the weather. The breathing does not slow.

title: Seeds Are Meant to Disperse
note: A garden bed from above, and the slowest piece in the set: dandelion parachutes, milkweed silk and tumbling grass awns release on the wind across four ninety-second seasons. Most land on the pavement and do nothing. A few land on soil and sprout next season. A small ledger in the corner keeps the tally — germinated 4, dispersed 96 — with no celebration at all. One slow drag is one gust, and only one per half minute. Care, at the speed of gardening.

title: Wandering Through Secret Storms
note: A triptych of redactions. Left: a weather field report almost entirely blacked out — "funnel", "11:47", "not confirmed" survive, one underlined in red pencil. Center: women filing records in a steel archive aisle, drawers sliding. Right: a satellite storm under black bars that breathe and occasionally slip, showing handwriting: "the dog knew first". Drag to shift the bars and redact it yourself.

title: Emulsion Lifts
note: Film, physically unmade: a faded prairie street with a tornado on the horizon, sprocket holes down both sides — and pieces of the emulsion lift. A water tower's tank curls away on a translucent sheet, blank leader beneath; a roof re-adheres in the wrong place, windows near the ground. The collage keeps un-collaging itself, one peel every quarter minute or so. Drag a shard to help it peel. You cannot repair it.

title: Mapping the Prairies
note: Sunny ruins inside a metal room: bleached farmhouses, a grain elevator, a collapsing barn under wide prairie skies, framed top and bottom by riveted steel sheeting with a specular light sliding across it on a sixty-second orbit. Survivor quotes scroll through the lower steel, never over the building: "the wind took the roof before we heard it", "we waited in the cellar three hours". Drag down to move the light; sideways to scrub the quotes.

title: Bad Stars
note: After BAD STARS: genuinely calm nature scenes — starfish, clouds over water, a narwhal, blooming cacti — inside a floral wallpaper border, the room as frame. Over the calm, hand-set omen phrases: "we heard people trying to dig through the rubble", "it was a clear day, like this one". Every so often, exactly four seconds of intrusion — a burning bush, a smoking grate, a volcano — never announced. Then calm again.

title: The People in This Picture
note: Battle's datamosh ethic: a prairie town under a funnel, crashed — macroblocks displaced, colors bleeding magenta and green, rain lattice over everything — while plain typewriter captions state the facts: "the funnel stayed on the ground eleven minutes", "the grain elevator held". Once a cycle the frame repairs into a clean photograph for three seconds. The repair is the lie. Drag sideways to scrub the corruption depth like a forensic tool.

title: Just One Peek (Aftermath)
note: The aftermath, not the feed: a dark ink room where phantom notification shapes — rounded rectangles, heart outlines, bell curves, no logos, no counts — drift in from the upper right like weather, some with red cores, multiplying and emptying in ninety-second waves. A lone figure sits in the corner. Touch a phantom and it dissolves. That is the only verb the piece offers, and it unlocks nothing.

title: gains + losses (A Letter)
note: After Supnet's letter film: a small ink figure with a single red scarf walks an empty paper landscape — walks, pauses, sits, walks on — while fragments of an unfinished letter drift past at different depths: "respect their need for privacy", "i kept the blue cup", "yours, still". Day and night alternate; little vignettes (a cup, a train, a chair) surface at the edges like memories. Drag to unscroll the letter. The walker keeps its own pace regardless.

title: Closed Circle of Worship
note: Supnet's mathematical ritual: three chalk rings on aged black paper turning in stepped polyrhythm — pyramids and crescents outside on a 12-step cycle, blue eyes in the middle on 8, angular horn-and-jaw motifs inside on 5 — with hand-inked sigils redrawing themselves in the band between, and a still empty void at the center that nothing ever enters. Drag the outer ring and it resists, snapping back to the count on release.

title: Ways + Means (Pedal-Powered City)
note: Her pedal-powered city: a hand-drawn Toronto of ink blocks, cranes and one red streetcar on trembling 16mm, sprocket holes along the top. The projection speed is your hand — drag to pedal it, and the city streaks into multiple exposures and pixellation bursts; let go and it eases back to a trembling standstill, single frames holding. At rest it just trembles, the way film does.

title: Smoke (Four-Colour Catastrophe)
note: After Supnet's Smoke: an ink volcanic plume on paper that you zoom into until the image dissolves into its own printing — CMYK rosettes blooming at the edges, registration drifting apart, until at forty times there is no catastrophe left, only misregistered dots. Closeness dissolves it. Drag vertically to dive; double-tap to come back to the whole picture.

title: Finding the Truth in the World Among Us
note: An EVP summoning after Supnet's 2013 piece: a dark field of AM static, tuned like a radio band, and pale chalk forms — waves, rings, eyes — flickering half-heard out of the noise. Every so often one locks, flares dark red, and shatters into twelve fragments. Drag to retune the band and change what can come through. It ships silent: a closed-form signal model does the listening, which the process notes explain.

title: Heavy Metal Parking Lot (Paper Cutout)
note: Supnet's Animated Heavy Metal Parking Lot rebuilt as paper: a tilted diorama of torn-edge cutout cars in tailgate reds and denim, ink-faced figures bobbing between the rows at six frames a second, glue tabs and paper backing showing on every shape, a big low sun over the asphalt. Drag to slide the lightbox. Coming near the figures scatters them a little. Disturbance, not control.

title: Sun Moon Stars Rain, Choreographed
note: Supnet's second-by-second choreography made visible: a ritual mandala of sulfur sun, crescent moon, pyramid and starburst on black, where every second of the 24-second loop performs a different transparency — the sun steps, the moon swaps phase, the stars scatter and regather, red rain falls in cuts. A glyph timeline along the bottom is her shooting plan. Drag sideways to wind the film, drag vertically to pedal the projection speed, even backwards.

title: [pink noise]
note: A film with no image and no sound: a black screen, an amber card — PUT ON 3D GLASSES NOW - INSERT EARPLUGS — then subtitles for sounds that are not there. [pink noise]. [a door closes upstairs]. [silence, but the wrong kind]. Twenty-two captions over three minutes, with pure black between them. Drag and a faint waveform appears: the noise that isn't playing, deliberately unrelated to the words.

title: One Year Project
note: A photo a day for the leap year 2004, all 366 of them in one grid: tiny generated snapshots — walls, rooflines, fields, street corners — with flash blowouts, thumbs over lenses, crooked horizons, and the camera's green timestamp burned into every frame. One day is highlighted, advancing every ten seconds. Press and hold a day to see it full-frame. Drag to scrub the year.

title: A Knight's Walk
note: A knight tours a near-black chessboard, one move a second, and every square it leaves changes medium: film grain first, then green pixel blocks, then ASCII glyphs — the board fills with three kinds of noise in visiting order, a neon trail behind the pale knight. Drag the knight yourself if you like: legal moves only, and the tour replans from wherever you put it.

title: Rotterdam Tower
note: An Empire for the video-game generation: a flat-shaded tower in a seamed skybox, the camera never moving, one compressed night running 8:06 PM to 2:42 AM in 14 minutes 28 seconds. Windows light one by one in sodium orange, a tiny car crosses now and then, and the corner clock runs Liberty City time. Drag sideways to scrub the night. Nothing bigger happens. That is the piece.

title: All My Life (After the Stitcher)
note: A landscape panorama stitched in real time — fence, trees, road — until the stitcher overflows and tears it: a tree stands three times with magenta fringes, a seam ghosts the fence double, a band smears orange. The failure is kept, and every new pass stitches over the wound. Drag hard right-to-left to feed it frames and cause the next overflow yourself.

title: Splice Lines
note: After Kurt Kren, a film made only of cuts: black leader, then a white flash frame, a frame-counter number, an orange tape mark — and back to black. The cuts are the content; between them, only drifting scratches. Drag anywhere to splice your own cut into the rhythm. It stays.

title: Windshield Baby
note: A street corner through a Gameboy Camera: 160 by 144 pixels, four greens, nothing else — not even the frame counter. Cars are blocks, faces are four-pixel smears, the camera re-exposes with a hard snap every few seconds and drops frames as it goes. Nothing happens, and the ordinariness is the dehumanization. Drag to pan in hard 8-pixel chunks.

title: Ten Skies, One Cloud
note: Ten skies condensed into one frame, the way Clint Enns remade Benning: ten cloud systems drifting through a single flat sky at ten speeds, and wherever two skies cross, the chroma key fails — hard green matte edges, magenta fringes, cyan flecks shimmering along the seams. The seams are the picture. Hold a cloud to solo its sky; release and the ten collapse back together.

title: Keep It Away From Everything
note: The archival paradox: a band print in a dark vault, and a seal of steel rings closing over it for two minutes — the only way to preserve it is to lock it away forever. When the seal completes, ten seconds of black and one small word: "saved." Then it reopens, brighter. Drag outward to hold the seal open a little longer; inward to seal it early. You can negotiate, not stop it.

title: Something Containing Nothing
note: The null set, staged. A faint empty-set outline hangs in a black void, and one by one computed color bands arrive inside it — 4, then 12, then 24, then the full 48-band print — as the outline fades, gone at the exact moment the print completes. It holds, empties, begins again. Drag to gather elements in faster, or push them back out.

title: The Instrument Room
note: A dark room, a wall of 24 Null_Sets prints — constitutions, genomes, insurance policies, novels, source code, a phone book — each computed from its text's bytes, each sized by its byte length: the genome towers, the phone book sprawls, a chess game is a postage stamp. Phosphor readouts give bytes, bands, dominant hue. The camera dollies slowly past. Drag up on a print to zoom the instrument in.

title: The JPEG Decides
note: One text, three file formats. The US Constitution rendered as 48 flat bands whose colors are computed through a quantization table — and every 30 seconds the table changes: JPEG luminance gives blues and teals, chrominance gives magentas, DCT rounding gives warm reds. The plaque names the table. The hand is nowhere in it. Drag sideways to scrub between tables.

title: Hex Subtraction
note: Her method, live: a quiet blue scene above a hex panel. Every few seconds a run of bytes is deleted — greyed out, struck through in red — and the band above shears within a second, magenta blooming. Nothing is ever added, nothing heals. Drag across the hex to aim the next deletion; the session ends heavily wounded.

title: Interface Absences
note: A desktop that empties itself. A cursor opens windows on decaying newsreel fragments that close too soon; footage windows fill with checkerboard absence; folders delete themselves; the trash fills. In three minutes only the cursor and the wallpaper remain — then the desktop restores and loses everything again. Drag a window to rescue it for twenty seconds.

title: The Gap Between Data and Information
note: The same passage, two readings. Left: Romeo and Juliet on warm paper, legible, the read lines dimming as you go. Right: the identical characters as saturated Null_Sets bands, unreadable. Amber bits cross the divider one character at a time, and the two sides never fall out of lockstep. Drag left to pause and read; drag right and the machine reads faster.

title: Null_Sets
note: A gallery wall of data prints: famous texts — the US Constitution, a car insurance policy, the human genome — rendered as horizontal color bands by a fixed byte-to-color rule the artists did not choose. A new framed print joins the wall every 45 seconds. Drag on a print to re-render it from a different passage of the same text; the bands re-flow, the text is the same.

title: Why Make a Broken Thing
note: A pristine corporate grid and one line of chalk: "why make a broken thing." Nothing breaks on its own here — the lesson is yours. Each drag breaks exactly one thing: a square shears, a border fringes magenta, a corner frays, a cell rots. The chalk tally keeps count. Twelve breaks and the board answers: "good. again?"

title: Float / Sink
note: A first-person drift through a ghost town at the blue hour, from the Ghosttown Spirit Simulator's grammar: press and hold to float weightless, two fingers to sink, release to hang in the air. No controls but buoyancy. Shear-bands wipe the rooftops, and after a minute idle the town dissolves and re-lays itself — never the same town twice.

title: Sympathy for the Blue Screen
note: The most honest sentence a machine ever wrote, on BSOD blue: "I have been running for 214 days. I am tired." Every thirty seconds a new crash report types itself out — a hard drive, a GPU, a phone battery, a backup drive nobody checked — plain log entries from dying systems, shear-bands dreaming behind the text. Drag to smear the words like wet ink; they settle back.

title: Null Sets
note: Whitman, mistranslated. A stanza types itself at the top; each finished line flashes, shatters into its own bytes, and rains green binary into an image building below — a blue ghost-field with a half-erased figure. Four stanzas complete the picture, and the poem is gone. Drag in the falling bits to corrupt the compilation.

title: Hand-Processed Binary
note: A fresh strip of hand-processed film: a figure against Meaney blue, waiting for your hand. Drag across it to scratch the binary — slices displace, magenta fringes bloom, emulsion darkens — and the scratch stays. Twenty scratches and the strip is a palimpsest; a new one begins. The chalk counter keeps the darkroom log.

title: A Better Ghost
note: A home movie on a failing drive: a figure walks a blue field, and each stutter shears the slices and costs it opacity, until the walk is a procession of ghost-bands trailing behind the lead. The place persists; the person fades, but never fully. Hold a finger down to summon the ghosts back toward solid — a seance, not a save.

title: The Deconstructive Linguist
note: A split-screen thesis: on the left a hex dump scrolls and an invisible hand edits bytes in amber; on the right, the blue home-movie image those bytes become shears in the matching band a second later. Every glitch is traceable to an edit. Drag the hex side to choose where the next corruption lands; drag the image side to smear it yourself.

title: Digital Alzheimer's
note: A home-movie still — a figure against a saturated blue sky, a small house — stays clear for ten seconds. Then the forgetting begins: horizontal bands shear sideways, one discrete event at a time, skin tones gray, a magenta band chews down the frame. It never heals. After three minutes only smear-ghosts remain on blue. Drag to hasten the forgetting where you touch.

title: Glitch School Lesson
note: Glitch school is in session. Each 45-second lesson pairs a technique with an aphorism in chalk: pixel-sort waves under "Glitch Art is the Art of Surprise", a circle that refuses to close, a moth whose wingbeats spawn artifacts. Drag chalk on the board and the lesson corrupts your notes.

title: Blue Moon Burning
note: Three movements, hard cuts only: color-shift glitch blocks; a flat blue planet turning with its landmasses and clouds; an extreme close-up of the cratered moon, half in shadow. Then a white flash and it begins again. Hold a finger down to bend the starfield like a gravity lens.

title: Dirty New Media
note: A perfect corporate-minimal grid — white field, gray rounded squares — and then the dirt starts: bit-rot spreads from a corner with a visible front, cells fray into magenta and green static, a chromatic ghost of the clean design slides sideways and stays. Drag a squeegee of cleanliness through it; the rot returns in five seconds.

title: Copy-It-Right
note: An appropriation machine: a cream cactus sits center, and every thirty seconds the machine presses it — slices streak, channels split — stamps it COPY-IT-RIGHT × N / Edition 25 in red, and files the bent copy in a scrolling archive. The original never changes. Drag across it to pre-bend the next edition.

title: GlitcHorses
note: Two black horse glyphs gallop across an explosion field, red-pink neural networks pulsing inside their silhouettes, nose to tail. Every twenty seconds a glitch burst freezes them mid-stride — RGB ghosts, scanline rake — then they resume. Drag to fire a shockwave that lights the nerves it crosses.

title: Ghosttown, Never Twice
note: A procedural ghost town at night — water towers, a church, saloons around an empty main street, spirit wisps rising from lit windows, a count of spirits ticking up. Every three minutes it dissolves into static and regenerates as a different town. You can never step into the same town twice. Hold the moon to summon the dissolve.

title: Yawl
note: One line of glitch dialect types itself in phosphor amber, corrupts into leet and cyan-magenta substitutions, holds, and re-forms: "goodMorn'NN Out West yawl." Text is the whole artwork. Drag to smear it like a bad tracking head; it snaps back.

title: Snowrainbow Television
note: A dead TV channel: coarse analog static resolving into slow rainbow bands, with a rider, fence posts and a water tower ghosting half-buried in the bottom third. Every nine to fourteen seconds a tear-line splits the picture. Drag to tune an antenna ghost — a trailing patch where the horizon briefly resolves.

title: Useful Radio (Duo)
note: Two radio voices trade phrases across a split screen: VOICE-K answers in sharp cyan bursts, VOICE-F splits magenta blobs into five droplets, a broadcast tower pulsing over the divider. Twice a loop a ghost static crackles through and both stutter. Drag the divider to tune it. Radio voices, citizen listening.

title: Ice Cream Truck at Channel 19
note: A tiny striped ice-cream truck drives a figure-eight over a city grid, broadcasting its 8-note jingle. Three CB receivers replay it by distance: the near one clean, the middle one dropping every other note, the far one smeared into blue ribbons. Drag to raise buildings that block a receiver's line of sight.

title: The Correct Time
note: An astronomical clock with one dramatic beat: a sun dot travels a thin ecliptic ring over pale rising particles, and at the loop's 60% mark it reaches the equator line and everything inverts — white field, black ring — held for three seconds while the readout says EQUINOX. Then the descent into darker months. Drag to tilt the ring.

title: Wind Chimes, Prepared Copper
note: Nine prepared copper chimes hang from tree limbs on S. Laflin St and the wind performs them: calm, a twenty-second front, calm. Tubes swing on closed-form pendulums and collide — 30 collisions a cycle, each struck tube flashing under an expanding ring. Drag to add a gust. The artist never touches them.

title: Rock Speaker Garden (4 Hours)
note: A plan view of the four-hour, ten-track speaker garden: ten monoliths on a dashed walking path, each broadcasting colored rings on its own cadence, white bleed flares where rings cross. A ghost visitor walks the path while the track clock runs 0:00 to 4:00:00 in three minutes. Drag to pan the plan.

title: No-Media Trio, Again
note: NO-MEDIA again, as a trio: nine radio modules ring a black stage, three are pulled into the circle each round to cross-modulate for a compressed ten minutes — amplitude bends paths, rhythm gates flashes, speed warps scale. At zero the stage wipes black. No history, no replay.

title: Smoke Detector Choir
note: Twenty-four smoke detectors on a dark ceiling beep on their own misaligned cycles, LEDs flashing, amber rings expanding, neighbors blinking in sympathy. Once a loop, two of them accidentally phase-lock into unison for twelve seconds. Drag a hand over one to mute its next beep.

title: Signal Territory
note: One orange transmitter divides the field into coverage territories: bright sharp dots with trails in LOCAL, stuttering amber dots in DISTANT, blue fragments that barely exist in FRINGE. A pulse every four seconds upgrades whoever it passes. Drag to drag an interference shadow across the dial.

title: Asemic Score
note: A page of asemic writing: six staves of flowing, meaningless glyphs. A scan line descends and performs them — each glyph fires its shape as an expanding arc, pulse, falling line or ring and stays lit red. At the bottom the page wipes and a new score generates. Tap a glyph to read ahead.

title: Rubber Chicken Orchestra
note: Six absurd instruments on a shelf — rubber chicken, toy accordion, squealing wheel, rubber duck, fried circuit board, degreased gear — take aleatoric turns, one at a time, each filling the air with its drawn sound: rings, zigzags, sparks, bubbles, pixels, saws. Tap one to steal its turn.

title: Everything Wrong the Right Way
note: The I LOVE PRESETS trio again, but choreographed: eight bars at their presets, then the WRONG light flashes, the sliders slam to 400% and negative, and everything runs feral until RESET slams it home with a white flash. You cannot drag anything. Tap RESET to cut it short.

title: Windows into the Continuum
note: One jagged screech line, endlessly reprocessed: sped up, slowed, chopped, looped, fed back through itself, each process labeled as it lands. A scrubber marks "you are here" on a timeline with no start and no end. A window, not the work. Watch only.

title: The Subtraction
note: A score written as a module inventory (oscillator, filter, filter, sloth, sloth...) types itself out, and each line adds a lane that re-renders the same signal through its process — smoothed, hazed, pulsed, band-colored. Every minute the inventory shuffles and the path changes.

title: neural goldberg (chatter)
