note: Two semi-autonomous systems chatter across a split screen: the cyan one draws line constellations, the magenta one splits blobs into exactly as many droplets as the other side just spoke. They stall, drop out, and free-run. Tap to interfere — it perturbs, never commands.

title: Wild at Heart, as a Control Voltage
note: An abstract film of drifting red, teal and bone rectangles runs a synth rack through light sensors: brightness drives the oscillator, hue the filter, contrast the tremolo — always half a second late, which is the point. Drag across the film to interfere with a flashlight wipe.

title: No-Media Pairing
note: Twelve voices ring a dark stage. Every minute a random pair is spotlighted to improvise together, cross-modulating each other through green tendrils, while a 10:00 countdown runs. At zero the pair vanishes with no trace and no history. It never repeats. Watch only.

title: Net Art Battle
note: Two algorithmic players duel on a split screen, firing corruption volleys (row-tears, channel splits, pixel-sorts) at each other's landscape every four seconds while a fake chat crowd reacts. Coach your side with a tap between bouts. It always ends in a draw.

title: Wrong Ways Prevail
note: Error dialogs with absurd messages ("the file is too honest", "it was Tuesday") spawn in a fixed musical score and stack up on a dark stage. Tapping one to dismiss it splits it into two smaller ones. There is no way to win. The score strip at the bottom conducts.

title: MicroMonotaur
note: A failure bench for storage media: a floppy, a hard drive and a USB stick are read in turn — clean signal first, then dropouts, bit-flips and wobble creep in until the readout names the failure (SECTOR NOT FOUND, BIT ROT, HEAD CRASH (SIMULATED)). Tap a card to read it now.

title: Radio Buttons
note: A demoscene of old-OS interface glyphs — radio buttons, checkboxes, scrollbars, close boxes — pulsing through four patterns in fixed order: SWEEP, FUGUE, CANON, SELECT_ALL. Drag to scrub the timeline.

title: Beachball Metronome
note: A spinning beachball conducts six tiny vignettes: they play, freeze when it "thinks", and resume when it releases, on a strict rhythmic schedule. The progress bar stalls at 99% forever. Tap the beachball for an extra freeze.

title: Satromizer
note: A wrong tool for a calm landscape: five sliders (SMEAR, TEAR, CHANNEL, STUTTER, DECAY) each genuinely corrupt the picture in real time. Drag them; tap BYPASS to A/B clean against corrupted; double-tap a slider to zero it.

title: I Love Resets
note: A trio console (VOX / VID / DRUM) whose preset knobs really work: drag them toward wrongness, up to 400% and into negative. Every eight bars the panels slam to absurd extremes on their own, then the big RESET slams them back. Tap to start the jam.

title: Prepared Desktop
note: The piece is a fake desktop running a performance: windows cascade open with little glitch animations inside, the cursor drags the top window around leaving smear trails, a beachball freezes everything for a beat, then it all closes. You just watch — the cursor is the performer's. Watch only.

title: Glitch-Alike Lab
note: Four ways to fake a glitch, judged honestly: a smooth prompted filter and a blocky upscaler are labeled GLITCH-ALIKE; a real databend and a palette token swap earn REAL BREAK. Tap a panel to isolate it.

title: How They Watch
note: This page fingerprints your browser (canvas hash, fonts, screen, timezone) and draws the portrait as labeled red bars. Drag to rotate it into a radar view. Everything on this page stayed in your browser.

title: Mavuel
note: A generative music box that never loops: a tender plucked arpeggio improvises further from itself the longer it plays, its score drifting from gold to cyan as deviation grows. Tap to begin; tap the score to reseed the deviation.

title: Sneakers Decryptor
note: A working encryptor in 1992 hacker-movie chrome: type plaintext, get cipher blocks, decrypt with the key matrix to get it back. It genuinely round-trips, and nothing leaves the page. Drag the signal slider to change key length.

title: Tactical Misuse Kit
note: Five browser-hack toys against dark patterns: a feed that poisons its recommendations, a cookie banner that grows when declined, a like button that deducts from your score, a search that answers with metadata, a progress bar that fills only while you do nothing.

title: Dear Apple
note: An open letter types itself live — "dear apple, we need to talk about us" — while the geometric field behind it degrades into codec artifacts as the letter complicates. Drag to scrub through the letter.

title: New Aesthetic Compositions
note: The generator is the artwork: six New Aesthetic compositions (pixel sorts, satellite mosaics, wireframes, bar fields) beside the commented source that makes them. Tap a preset to regenerate; drag the obfuscate slider to corrupt.

title: Codec Tutorial
note: A calm dusk scene (banded sky, orange sun, dark dunes) is destroyed the way a codec destroys it: macroblock bands drift, colors trail, then a keyframe snaps it clean. The caption strip teaches as it goes. Watch only.

title: Kopimashin
note: A machine that copies itself into futility: flat shapes spawn at the center and copy outward in a spiral, each generation grayer, until a hard wipe sweeps the mush away and the machine sits thinking. Watch only.

title: Basic Waveforms
note: Three neon waveforms march in their lanes over a dim burst field: the square wave's edges tear the field, the sine smears its channels, the sawtooth drops flat blocks — all stepped to a 120bpm beat. Watch only.

title: Hyperobject Acts
note: Climate grief in four acts over one dark scanline field — denial barely glitches, despair detonates into databend chaos, acceptance settles into rhythmic green bands, defiant hope locks into a rising yellow diagonal. Hard cuts only. Watch only.

title: Sticker Shuffle
note: Five sticker creatures, cut into outlined fragments, shuffle like a deck twice per loop: pieces land in the wrong creature, brief hybrids form, then everything flies home. Watch only.

title: Vernacular Triptych
note: Diagonal bars and concentric rings read through three forgotten file formats — run-length smears, shuffled scanlines, strided channels — the same seeded error showing three different faces. Drag to scrub corruption depth; double-tap reseeds.

title: Room Tone
note: Twelve invented glyphs rot left to right across a twelve-second loop, stems splitting into red fragments, while the small cyan reference row beneath stays perfectly legible — the computer still understands it. Watch only.

title: Favourite Songs
note: Sixteen imaginary songs, each drawn as its own binary data reinterpreted into pixels — noise fields, byte-run stripes, flat loud blocks, nothing like a waveform. One panel remixes itself at a new bit depth each cycle. Watch only.

title: Raw Import
note: A picture of flat tiles is imported as raw audio and run through an echo effect: the top rows stay clean as a header while every row below tears into ghost copies and channel splits — Roberts's 2009 Audacity databending tutorial. Watch only.

title: Monglot Machine
note: A green arc-and-spoke mandala runs down a visible pipeline — datamosh smear, block shift, channel swap — each stage feeding the next, after Menkman's monglot machine. Drag vertically to scrub corruption depth; double-tap reseeds.

title: De/Calibration Grid
note: A wall of calibration cards, every one miscalibrated in its own way. Drag across the grid and the wrongness spreads to neighboring cards like an infection; leave it alone and the wall re-calibrates itself over about thirty seconds.

title: Axes of Affordance
note: Two hundred tiny pictures float in a dark volume, split by a translucent plane: crisp neon on the possible side, gray mirrored residue on the impossible side — Menkman's BLOB. Drag to rotate the view and move the plane; double-tap reseeds the tiles.

title: Impossible Rainbow
note: Six flat bands make the rainbow everyone draws, then the artifact intrudes: bands drop out, swap colors, jitter — one glitch at a time on a 16-second loop. Watch only.

title: Vernacular Triptych
note: One stacked motif rendered three ways — blocky and smeared, flat and posterized, Bayer-dithered — the same image in three file-format tongues. Drag to pull the shared corruption band through all three at once.

title: Collapse of Signal
note: An analog signal hunt: a white diamond tries to sync over a rolling phosphor field, locks for one held second, then decays into tear and noise — Menkman's analog piece. Watch only.

title: Databend Canvas
note: A databent picture file corrupts on an 8-second loop, its first rows holding as a protected header while the bent rows smear and never quite recover — Menkman's Compression Study 2. Watch only.

title: Block Lattice
note: A field of tiny color blocks on black, a ghost image of rings and a diagonal bar quantized to oblivion — Menkman's Compression Study 1. Watch only.

title: Reworld
note: Kimchi and Chips' reworld: a wall of four hundred tiny prisms, each sampling the same procedural city at its own angle and zoom, sky, sun, rooftops, traffic, fractured into a glittering mosaic that re-tunes every forty seconds. Drag to stir the prisms.

title: Unread Characters
note: Kimchi and Chips' unread characters: three hundred frosted lenses over a field of warm bokeh, and hidden in the light, one hand-written line, the crow's eye counts the unlit windows. Head-on there is nothing to read. Drag to tilt the panel and find the one angle where the dots become handwriting.

title: Optical Rail
note: Kimchi and Chips' optical rail: a warm back-lit print, hatching, halftone, three bold circles, one red band, that never moves at all. What moves is a train of glass lenses crossing it, bending the pattern only where they pass. The image is still; the seeing travels. Drag a lens; double-tap to reverse the rail.

title: Another Moon
note: Kimchi and Chips' another moon: the real moon hangs small and warm, and beside it a second, colder moon built from laser beams, shining on yesterday's sunlight. A hairline of charge along the bottom fills by day and drains by night, and the moon's phase is its battery. Double-tap to burn it all in one flare.

title: Halo
note: Kimchi and Chips' halo: a ring of light in mist, held up by twenty-four small mirrors along the floor, each tracking a sun that is never drawn. Low sun, the ring burns; noon, it fades to a ghost; sunset, it breaks into glints. Drag to move the sun.

title: Light Barrier
note: Kimchi and Chips' light barrier: forty mirror shards you can barely see throw pale beams across black space, and where the beams cross, small bright phantoms condense, hang, and dissolve as the array re-tunes. Drag to tear the crossings; double-tap to re-tune now.

title: 483 Lines
note: Kimchi and Chips' 483 lines: all 483 NTSC scanlines standing in a dark field like threads, bending in slow waves, brightening where they gather into folds. Every forty-five seconds a warm field sweeps down and the whole field re-tunes. Drag to pull a fold; tap to hold it.

title: Line Segments Space
note: Kimchi and Chips' line segments space: a wireframe phantom hangs in black haze, drawn in pale blue beams that bloom brighter wherever they cross, slowly becoming other solids, tetrahedron, octahedron, icosahedron, knot. Drag to bend the beams; double-tap and the piece re-tunes itself, beam by beam.

title: Drawing Robot
note: Jussi Aengesleva's drawing robot, after Royal Jelling: a small carriage on rails crosses a dark wall forever, drawing vessels, runes and spirals in chalk, each new find bright, the old ones fading to ghosts behind it. Drag on the wall to feed it a find; double-tap for a fresh wall.

title: Samaras
note: Jussi Aengesleva's samaras: thirty flying seeds hang in a dark tower on invisible winches, each spinning slowly like a maple seed, sinking, and being drawn back up, brass spines, pale wooden wings catching the warm light once a turn. Drag to stir the air.

title: Body Mnemonics
note: Jussi Aengesleva's body mnemonics: ten glowing orbs drift in a dark field, and five faint rings wait where a body would keep its things, head, hands, chest, feet. Drag an orb into a ring and it is remembered there; double-tap and everything returns to its place.

title: Pinnannousu
note: Jussi Aengesleva's pinnannousu: a robot arm carves a block of ice into a lens, the lens throws a +2 of light on the wall, and then, over ninety slow seconds, the lens melts and the number melts with it. Drag the light while it lasts; double-tap for a fresh block.

title: Delta Phi
note: Jussi Aengesleva's delta phi: a milled chrome wall, apparently abstract, and one slow spotlight. Where the light meets the facets at the right angle, a Greek letter resolves in the reflected caustics on the dark around it, then dissolves back to shimmer. Drag the light and read.

title: Petalclouds
note: Jussi Aengesleva's petalclouds at Changi Terminal 4: six clouds of aluminium leaves breathing overhead in a blue dusk, forever re-forming, forever crossing the sky, their warm shadows drifting the other way below. Drag to pan; nudge a leaf and its cloud re-balances.

title: Kinetic Rain
note: Jussi Aengesleva's kinetic rain at Changi: two fields of copper droplets that think in shapes, a balloon, a paper plane, a kite, a flock, a dragon, each form held for a breath in rising and falling copper, with every droplet's shadow pooled on the floor below. Drag to scatter the rain.

title: Last Clock
note: Jussi Aengesleva's last clock, with Ross Cooper: no hands, no numbers, three rings of one-pixel slices from a small procedural sky, the last minute, the last hour, the last twelve hours, new slices bright, old ones fading to ghosts, until the face is a mandala of archived time. Drag to scrub the archive.

title: Timescope
note: Joachim Sauter's timescope: a quiet gray city, and one brass-ringed lens that reveals the same streets in the augmented present, teal towers, amber routes, a river of light. Drag the lens slowly; it lags like real glass.

title: Symphonie Cinetique
note: Joachim Sauter's symphonie cinetique, with Olafur Arnalds: eleven brass pendulums play a three-minute movement, chaos, waves, canon, unison, and a finale where all hang still for one beat. Tap the piece and a felt-piano score joins in, one note at each swing's edge.

title: Floating Numbers
note: Joachim Sauter's floating numbers: hundreds of glowing numbers drift on a dark table like plankton, cyan values, amber dates, gray operators, gathered into loose neighborhoods that breathe, with one large hero number slowly counting. Drag to scatter them; double-tap for the data tide.

title: Petalclouds
note: Joachim Sauter's petalclouds: six clouds of aluminum petals drift over a vast dim terminal, slowly opening, closing and stretching, their warm shadows pooling on the floor below. Everything here is patient. Drag to pan through the space.

title: Reflective Kinematronic
note: Joachim Sauter's reflective kinematronic: a hundred small mirrors turn at their own speeds in the dark, throwing warm spots of one off-frame light across an unseen room, until every forty-five seconds they align and the spots merge into a single field. Drag to stir them.

title: RGBCMYKinetic
note: Joachim Sauter's RGBCMYKinetic: five mirror disks drift in a black void while red, green and blue spotlights throw pools of light at their feet, the colors mixing only where the pools overlap. Drag a disk and play the mixer.

title: Terravision
note: Joachim Sauter's Terravision, the globe from 1994: a seeded planet tilted at twenty-three and a half degrees, mottled continents on deep ocean. Drag to spin it with momentum; scroll to dive from orbit to terrain to the warm grid of the cities.

title: Kinetic Rain
note: Joachim Sauter's kinetic rain: two fields of bronze droplets on invisible wires ripple through a twenty-five-second choreography of swells, peaks and spirals, brighter the higher they ride. Drag across the field to disturb it and watch the drops settle back.

title: Scroll Story
note: Markus Kison's scroll story: eight hundred particles on warm paper read an essay in four movements, stream, bars, scatter, rings, morphing as you scroll and retracing exactly when you scroll back, a one-line caption under each. Scroll, or let it read itself.

title: Scanlines
note: Markus Kison's scanlines: an abstract lathe-turned vessel turns slowly in the dark while a red laser line sweeps its height every twenty seconds, the surface resolved above the line and dissolving into drifting points below it. Drag to turn it yourself.

title: Finder of Wonders
note: Markus Kison's finder of wonders: the piece is a finder window, sidebar folders named DOTS, LINES, FIELDS and CURRENTS, each opening a live little world in the pane, with subfolders that vary it. Tap through the folders; the chrome is the frame, the worlds are real.

title: Point Cloud Country
note: Markus Kison's country of points: fifteen thousand dots make a terrain, green valleys, ochre slopes, snow on the high massif, a cyan river winding through, no lines anywhere. It turns once a minute; drag to orbit it, double-tap for a new country.

title: Sweet Spot
note: Markus Kison's sweet spot: a motif smeared across twenty paper prisms, abstract from everywhere except one viewpoint. Drag to hunt it; a thin arc tells you how close you are, and when the slices align the prisms flash once and deal you a new hiding place.

title: The Chosen Watcher
note: Markus Kison's chosen watcher: twelve hundred particles drift in the dark until a soft beam sweeps down, picks one, and rings it in gold, and the whole field's depth quietly re-centers on the watched one. Your pointer can only nudge the watching.

title: Durchsehen Cube
note: Markus Kison's Durchsehen cube over open country: patchwork fields and a river drift past, and the concrete cube's faces re-render the landscape from your angle instead of hiding it, seams showing. Drag to orbit the cube and the country together.

title: Live Miniature
note: Markus Kison's live miniature: a city block on a dark table whose faces carry tiny living feeds, people as dots inside lit windows, blinds sweeping, all slightly mis-registered at the corners, while a forty-second day turns gold to dusk to night. Drag to walk around it.

title: Four Particles Lost
note: Daniel Franke's four particles lost in honey: four plain bright particles drift a dark tank on a seventy-five-second loop, and their long teal ribbons, folded and layered, are the piece. Drag to stir the fluid and your wake will linger; double-tap to still the tank.

title: Deep Time Archive
note: Daniel Franke's deep time archive: generated strata in rust, ash, teal and bone, their upper bands honestly corrupted with slice offsets, banding and gold glitch ticks that thin as you go deeper. Drag down to scrub the years; tap to lift a core sample.

title: Gedankenscherz
note: Daniel Franke and Martin Backes' guessing jest: a black cabinet of five worlds, star points, rotating gold solids, a fluid ink field, a storm of letterforms, a point-cloud menagerie, bleeding into each other at the seams. Drag to travel the cabinet; tap to dwell in the world in front of you.

title: Machine Dreams
note: Daniel Franke's machine dreams: dark stone masses webbed with glowing teal crystals dissolve every thirty seconds into a new chimera, while three specimen frames along the bottom keep the recent dreams. Tap a specimen to curate it into the main view; drag across the mass to stir the dream.

title: Strata
note: Daniel Franke's ice core of a smartphone: labeled mineral strata, gold, lithium, cobalt, silicon, grow from the bottom on paper-white, melt into shimmer at the top and re-ice below in a ninety-second loop that never ends. Drag across it to add heat; tap a band for its story.

title: One Sculpture Per Viewer
note: Daniel Franke's spatial soundsculpture: a dark room of faint marker glyphs, and through a small pale portal, one luminous crystalline sculpture that exists only inside the frame and changes with where the frame points. Drag to carry the portal; tap to freeze a specimen for ten seconds.

title: Durchsehen
note: Daniel Franke and Markus Kison's Durchsehen: a concrete cube sits in a dark gallery, and from the selected viewer's position its front face renders the room behind it, so the cube nearly vanishes, seams showing. Drag to become the viewer it tracks; tap a wall to re-hang the room.

title: The Point Body
note: Daniel Franke's point body: fourteen thousand white points make a dancer in the black, depth-shaded and never still, while a closed-form sound score drives the camera, close and slow in the quiet passages, wide and fast in the loud ones. Tap to reseed, drag to take the camera, double-tap for a new dancer.

title: The Emotional Machine
note: onformative's doctrine as a machine: a shy blue particle nebula fills a dark room, and where the small bright visitor lingers, the field warms to violet and teal and gathers into slow spirals. Drag to be the visitor; leave, and it cools and forgets.

title: Zephyr's App
note: onformative's Zephyr app, the instrument itself: sixty warm-white steel blades sweep across the dark as a ceiling ribbon, reshaping through a weather loop of calm, gust and storm, with faint cyan control ghosts still hovering at six segments. Drag to set the wind yourself.

title: Meandering River
note: onformative's Meandering River: braided cyan-teal channels run diagonally over dark terrain, migrating and re-carving in a sixty-second loop, gold sediment gathering at the bends and plumes blooming on a slow pulse. Drag to stir the flow and bend the river around your hand.

title: True/False Machines
note: onformative's true/false machines: twelve tall columns run their endless procedure, shutter-waves covering and exposing warm light tubes in unison, with holds of darkness and brightness between, and now and then one column covering alone. Watch only.

title: Watson's Halo
note: onformative's Watson identity: a dotted coral halo floats in a sterile white corridor while a swarm of coral, teal and peach dots drifts around it. Drag and the swarm gathers to your attention; let go and it relaxes back into itself.

title: Sound Sculpture
note: onformative and Daniel Franke's soundsculpture: a dancer made of some two thousand white points turns in the black while the camera orbits, one continuous take. Tap to reseed the same dancer into a new composition.

title: The Inside-Out Sun
note: onformative's Anima Iki: a glowing sphere wrapped in green-violet liquid metal hangs in a purple-washed dark room, the only light there is. Drag near it and the fluid quickens and brightens toward you, the way it answered movement in the gallery.

title: Immaterial Terrain
note: onformative's Immaterials as a living contour map: a terrain of dense blue-white iso-lines breathes on black, ridges rising and collapsing as the noise field evolves, while every fifteen seconds a bright scan band sweeps across and redraws the lines it crosses. Watch only.

title: The Robot's Cue Sheet
note: Marco Tempest's robot cue sheet: a gray block-headed machine works through its poses, GREET to PRESENT to POINT, as a playhead sweeps six amber cues on the timeline below, its cyan face panel swapping patterns at each mark. Watch only.

title: Three Lit Drones
note: Marco Tempest's mind-read, done with lighting: fifteen drones ring a small figure under fog while a dial sweeps to a number, and exactly that many drones fade red and sink a little. Drag to set the number yourself; the next cycle reveals yours.

title: Card Cosmos
note: Marco Tempest's card cosmos: a 52-card deck dealt one tap at a time into a calendar arc, each card an instrument with a season ring for its suit and a moon disc for its number, the active card floating large under cyan AR reticles. Tap to deal the next week.

title: Hand Dust
note: Marco Tempest's hand dust in three acts: gold dust drifts through a soft silhouette's depth-field, bright emitters trail from the figure's moving hands, and cued bursts punctuate the finale. Drag to conduct with the right hand; the dust follows.

title: Pop-Up 1895
note: Marco Tempest's Tesla pop-up: a white paper spread breathes open and closed against black, its cloud, trees, house and fence rising on V-folds under a monochrome projection skin of turning gears, with 1895 on the house. Drag vertically to open or close the book yourself.

title: White Room
note: Marco Tempest's workshop before the show: eight black quadcopters sit on a white floor and power up one by one, status dots blinking, orbs warming to a glow, then power down in reverse, while two engineers watch from the edges. The machine's own ritual. Watch only.

title: Illusion of Interactivity
note: Marco Tempest's reveal, drawn from above: twelve drones run glowing cyan routes on a carpet while the tiny conductor gestures on his own separate cue clock, ignored completely. Drag a route's waypoint to re-author the lines and the drones re-fit; the gestures never cause anything.

title: The Conductor
note: Marco Tempest's master image: a lone conductor stands arms-raised in a white void while twelve black drones above him cycle through stack, ring and spiral on their own prearranged clock, orbs pulsing on one shared heartbeat. He commands nothing; the illusion is the piece. Watch only.

title: The Third Rail
note: Tatsuya Ishii's backstage rail: a small dark wall hangs from catenary cables under a ceiling rail, inching along at freight speed beside a grooved winch drum, while the motor drive unit blinks its one green LED. The machine before the performance. Watch only.

title: PolyNodes
note: Tatsuya Ishii's node network with a conductor: faceted polyhedra drift and re-knit in the dark while a magenta center node fires a pulse every six seconds, the wavefront reaching each node only after its per-edge delay. Watch only.

title: Post-Choreography
note: Tatsuya Ishii's 3D Edit as the piece itself: a drone flock holds formation in two tinted stereo channels while below, the edit timeline runs its REAL and DELUSION tracks through a cut, a morph and a slow push. Drag on the timeline to scrub the edit; the footage stays calm.

title: Motion Edit
note: Tatsuya Ishii's motion-editor desktop: a CAD-dark viewport where the wall, the triangle and the monolith replay their glowing cyan paths at constant spec speed, lit segment by lit segment, while the magenta playhead sweeps the timeline and the test counter climbs. Watch only.

title: Winch Ballet
note: Tatsuya Ishii's winch ballet: three white truss triangles hang from wires that leave the top of the frame, dipping and tilting in canon as slow cyan and magenta washes alternate. Drag a triangle to re-target its wires and watch the winches pull it there.

title: The Monolith Flock
note: Tatsuya Ishii's monolith flock on its preprogrammed route: eight tall white monoliths walk a slow S-curve across a paper-white gallery in follow-the-leader formation, re-forming from column to arc to stagger every twenty seconds. Replay, not simulation. Watch only.

title: Two Time Continuums
note: Tatsuya Ishii's split-timeline wall: the same drifting figures rendered twice in one frame, the left half now and the right half six seconds ago, divided by a wall with a single bright portal cut through it. The divider slides slowly; through the portal each timeline shows the other. Watch only.

title: Six Hundred Kilos
note: Tatsuya Ishii's Syn wall at freight speed: a vast dark face glides toward the viewer for forty-five seconds at one constant pace, holds, and retracts, its blue sphere pulsing on a four-second heartbeat above a cyan wireframe grid, tiny audience silhouettes below. Watch only.

title: REC / PLAY
note: Momoko Nishimoto's test range, where every gesture is a recording: drag and the readout flips to REC while your path draws; release and it flips to PLAY and the cam-drone flies your take back. Three takes stack in teal, amber and violet; double-tap wipes the slate.

title: Six Hundred Kilos
note: Momoko Nishimoto's six hundred kilos: a projection wall the size of a room hangs from a ceiling rail, glowing with slow light-forms, its shadow-field dragging beneath. It never moves faster than its amber spec, five hundred millimetres a second; drag to push it and feel the glide outlast your hand.

title: Worn by the Tracker
note: Momoko Nishimoto's tracking seat as the whole piece: a dancer who is never drawn, only twelve white Vicon markers, teal joint-lines and tiny ID tags on black, with the red camera reticle riding the torso. Drag to move the body and the markers lag their honest twelve milliseconds behind.

title: The Stack
note: Momoko Nishimoto's stack, held: three columns of drone pairs hang in a bright gray void at their marked altitudes, micro-correcting in place. Drag a wind across them and they lean and resist without scattering; tap to collapse and restack the columns.

title: Six and Sixty-Four
note: Momoko Nishimoto's reconstruction from many witnesses: one bright orb-cluster subject at center, composited from jittered viewpoints that shimmer into a halo, six cameras at rest. Drag to add cameras up to seventy, counted on screen; tap to flash the full composite.

title: Reality / Delusion
note: Momoko Nishimoto's Cold Stares morph: one line-field rendered twice in the same frame, sharp white geometry for the real world and a warm grain-heavy double image for the delusion, crossfading with no cut. Drag sideways to hold the mix yourself; tap to rest at the shimmer midpoint.

title: Fly the Camera Move
note: Momoko Nishimoto's cam-drone flying a move the hand authored: it accelerates, holds and decelerates along a glowing teal path over a sparse set of orbs and light-bars, camera cone sweeping. Draw a path and it flies your move twice; tap to fly it again.

title: Well-Trained Birds
note: Momoko Nishimoto's flock at rest in a bright studio void: twenty-four skeletal drones hold three stacked-pair columns, each carrying a pale-blue orb, moving almost not at all. Drag the small performer below and the whole flock re-forms around the new anchor; tap for the scatter call.

title: The Chair
note: Yoichi Sakamoto's border ride from the chair itself: a cold landscape of pale light-structures banks past fog banks on a fifty-five second loop, the dark chair silhouette and its warm seat glow holding the bottom of the frame. Drag to lean into the bends; tap for the next waypoint.

title: Audience, in Reverse
note: Yoichi Sakamoto's audience seat run backwards: the stage stays honestly empty until you perform. Drag to record up to thirty seconds of strokes; the piece then plays your act in reverse, pink echoes lagging, ghost figures standing where you lingered. Double-tap clears and reseeds.

title: The Fabrication Inventory
note: Yoichi Sakamoto's border inventory parading as the performance itself: ten WHILL mobilities, five white omni cubes and ten stereo headsets cross the dark stage in machined formation, no dancers anywhere. Drag one out of line and it works its way back; tap one for its spec.

title: The Figure Eight
note: Particles, remembered as a circuit: a thin figure-eight rail, drawn like hardware with twin rails and sleeper ties, fills the dark. Sixteen LED balls roll it at one constant machined speed, but a ball’s color belongs to the segment it is crossing: reds down one lobe, greens on the crossing, ambers and blues elsewhere, and each checkpoint diamond flashes white as a ball passes. The rail glows only where its traffic is. Drag across a segment to command the next balls’ color there. Tap a checkpoint to flip what follows it.

title: Cold Camera
note: One scene, two worlds, no cut: a sparse set of abstract figures stands in a dark space while a single recorded camera drifts through it. The same view is rendered twice at once: solid real forms and cyan CG wireframes, cross-dissolved across the whole frame. At the first frame they are exactly half and half, the floor grid showing through the real ground and a pale pool of camera light under the figures. Drag sideways to pull the morph toward either world. Tap to change which space leads.

title: The Orb Fleet
note: A recorded flight, flown again: ten skeletal drones cross a dark stage in a diamond formation, dark arms and boards, red wiring marks, and a pale glowing orb riding on each. Their whole recorded paths stay faintly drawn behind them, a web of where the choreography has been and will go. The flock holds formations, breaks them, and forms again. Drag through them and nearby drones swerve away, then return to the recording. Tap an orb to flash it.

title: The Slit Scanner
note: Timing made visible: three spinners, one large and two smaller, turn in black under a sweeping strobe. The big rotor is caught at a lock: its sampled bars coincide into a still amber star while the smaller assemblies step and crawl in white. The patterns are not drawn; they are what sampling does to honest rotation. Drag near a rotor to take its motor in hand and make it freeze, crawl, or reverse. Tap to snap the strobe to the nearest lock.

title: Doors of Light
note: Architecture made of light: seven thin white rectangular frames hang in a black, misty room, nested like doorways and each turned a few degrees from the last. Small lens discs on fine wires are their sources. The frames breathe and swing slowly, never quite aligning. Drag near a frame to tilt its light plane around the lens. Tap to open one door in a brief bright flash.

title: Echo Vest
note: A haptic cloth rendered as the sensation, not the garment: on a near-black field, an unseen wearer drifts slowly, and rings of violet light radiate from them every second or so, thin and numerous, warming near the body and cooling to violet as they expand. A faint circle marks the edge of perception; when a ring crosses it, the ring brightens: the cloth sensing the room. Every so often the wearer stops and the rings tighten into a brief bright pulse, then release. One body listening to a dark room. Drag to become the wearer; hold still and the rings gather.

title: Sixty-Seven Boards
note: A self-portrait in prototypes: a dark gallery wall of twenty-four circuit boards, every one drawn procedurally and different: green and black solder masks, copper traces running from pads, tiny silkscreen labels from his real domains (OSC-01, ARTNET-REV-C, SYNC-TEST-7). Each board is a small light instrument with its own private blink grammar: one pulses like a heartbeat, one sweeps its row, one blinks in morse-like bursts, one breathes, one strobes sparsely. The wall is alive but unhurried, a museum of trial-and-error, and nothing blinks in sync. The view pans slowly. Drag to lean in and inspect.

title: Layered Sequences
note: The mix is the composition: sixteen horizontal LED bars on black, and three light scripts running on them at once, additively. A cyan pulse train marches left to right; a magenta wave travels slowly; an amber swell breathes across the whole field. Where they overlap, the light whitens, and white happens nowhere else: no single script, and no pair, can reach it. The scripts never talk to each other; the beauty is accidental. Every thirty seconds the oldest script is swapped for a new behaviour and the piece keeps going. Double-tap to swap one now.

title: Omni Chorus
note: A fleet in formation, honestly: twelve small omni-wheeled movers on a dark stage, each carrying one sodium-yellow light, tracing slow synchronized formations: a rosette, a spiral, a grid folding into a circle. Each mover chases its place with lag and drift, and whenever one strays too far its light flashes magenta for a split second as it corrects: the feedback loop made visible, about three corrections a second across the fleet. Their green tire tracks persist beneath them, proof of precise control. The formation is never perfect, and the trying is the piece. Drag to grab a mover and feel its corrections strain.

title: The Suit Remembers
note: The wearable as instrument: a field of haptic-light cells on near-black, and an unseen wearer drifting through them. Where the wearer passes, cells flare white-hot, then cool slowly through warm cream and ember red, taking some thirteen seconds to go dark: the field holds a fading map of where the body has been. When the wearer pauses, a bright bloom forms. The wearer is never drawn; you read the path in the cooling cells. Drag and you are the wearer: move slowly and the bloom follows, move fast and you leave a streak.

title: Lightsaber Study
note: One beam, an invisible dancer: on pure black, a long beam of light, white core, pale blue halo, carves choreographed arcs through the dark. It moves the way a dancer moves: sharp cuts, slow sweeps, held poses where the beam vibrates faintly like a held breath and warms for a moment. Its trail is the memory of the choreography, each path fading over six seconds, so the frame holds the last several gestures as ghost writing. No figure is ever shown. A new phrase of gestures begins each loop. Double-tap for new choreography.

title: Rolling Shutter Parade
note: An illusion built from strict math: three rotors of thin bars spin at fixed speeds on black while a single strobe fires at a slowly sweeping frequency. Sampling the spin, the strobe freezes the bars into impossible standing patterns: a twenty-spoke star that holds still, spokes that cluster and crawl backwards. The physical truth and the perceived truth never agree. Every so often the illusion breaks and the bars show their true motion in red, then the strobe captures them again. Watch it; the spell needs passive eyes. Double-tap for a new illusion set.

title: Sync Drift
note: Never lock, always chase: some two hundred small light nodes on a dark field, each running its own clock, wirelessly synced to one master beacon. Every twelve seconds the beacon fires and an alignment wave sweeps outward: nodes flare warm amber as it passes and snap toward the beacon phase, then drift takes them again, some lagging gray, a few lost entirely, packet loss and all. Alignment is a bright wave moving through a sea of stragglers. Drag to become radio interference and scramble the field locally. Double-tap to fire the beacon now.

title: The Carts Drive Themselves
note: The first night anything drove itself for art: a dark temple courtyard from above, and through it, glowing carts drive themselves, no operators, no remote controls. Each follows its own route with the particular patience of the self-driven: at crossings one cart slows, stops, and yields to another, its own decision, then resumes. Around them, a hundred small audience lights wander. The carts thread the crowd without touching anyone. Drag and you become a pedestrian: the nearest cart yields and reroutes around you. Tap a cart to see its whole route.

title: One Centimetre
note: Precision as composition: a huge dark stage ruled by a fine measurement grid, major lines every ten units, and on it four small machines moving along exact paths. Around each machine’s intended position rides a small cyan circle, exactly one centimetre in the stage’s scale, and the machine never leaves it: the sampled worst deviation across the whole loop is 0.607 centimetres. The beauty is in how little deviates. Drag to push a machine off its path: its circle flashes warm and it visibly works its way back inside the promise. Tap to read its live deviation.

title: Whatever Moves, Light Rides
note: The constant across a whole body of work: whatever moves, the light rides. On a dark field, three kinds of movers go about their schedules, small flying drones, rolling carts, gliding platforms, each drawn dark and plain, each carrying a light: cool orbs, warm lamps, pale screens. The movers are the means; the lights are the cargo, the only brightness in the frame, mingling where their paths cross and trailing behind them. One fleet, one grammar. Drag to pass a shadow over the nearest lights. Tap a mover to announce its passenger.

title: Position Is Wire Length
note: Position as wire length: in a dark stage volume, ten warm glowing cubes hang from thin wires descending from the ceiling, two wires per cube, and the wires are drawn, because the rig is the composition. As the cubes glide to new positions, the wires lengthen, shorten and angle, re-triangulating overhead. Every so often a cube is handed off: one of its wires slides along the ceiling rail to a new anchor while the cube hangs nearly still. The piece is the rig thinking. Drag to swing the cubes on their wires. Tap one to trace its wires.

title: As If Well-Trained Birds
note: A flock’s devotion to raised arms: in a dark studio void, a small figure stands center-low with both arms raised and never moves. Around it, twenty-four drones fly in flocking formation, each carrying a glowing white-blue orb, the most luminous thing in the frame. The flock has a score, marks it wheels toward, splits around and regroups, but the local rules of birds keep pulling against the choreography, and the tension is the performance. The figure is the anchor; the flock is the weather. Drag to bend the flight like wind. Tap to hold the flock still, orbs glowing.

title: Measure, Correct, Move
note: Precision as beauty: across a dark field, glowing nodes travel toward their waypoints, and the piece draws both the intended path, a faint ghost, and the actual traced path, a bright line. Between correction ticks the nodes drift and err; at each tick a warm pulse fires, the node snaps toward its ghost, and the bright line kinks. The composition is the accumulation of those kinks: a field of plans and truths, and the small bright moments where the machine admitted error and fixed it. Drag to inject noise and watch the corrections multiply. Tap to reveal the plan.

title: The Camera Move, Flown
note: A camera path, authored and then survived: in one register, a calm editor’s view, a thin glowing spline with keyframe nodes, exactly like a motion path in a 3D application. In the other, three small drones fly that path carrying glowing cameras, with weight and lag: they overshoot the bends, cut the corners, sag on the climbs, and faint red connectors draw the gap between the authored point and the real one. The gap is the content: reality renders the camera path, honestly. Drag to re-author the spline and watch the drones chase your version. Tap to switch registers.

title: Five White Cubes
note: The origin of a motion grammar: five identical white cubes on a dark floor, moving the way no car can. They strafe sideways while slowly rotating, translate without turning, stop dead, spin in place, then set off laterally again: holonomic motion, forward optional. Each leaves a faint trail, and the trails are the composition: long straight records crossed by cubes whose headings refuse to match their travel. The cubes are identical; the motion is the identity. Drag to bend their paths like a current. Tap a cube to hold it mid-strafe.

title: The Fastest Leaves the Longest
note: The hardware’s thesis in one frame: on a black field, identical white nodes travel their own paths, straight lines, orbits, figure-eights, and the rule is absolute: the faster a node moves, the longer and brighter its trail. A slow node leaves a gray stub; a fast one leaves a ribbon that crosses the field; and when a node suddenly lunges, its trail flares long and hot before settling. Motion and the record of motion are the same thing. Speed is the only identity a node has. Drag to accelerate the nodes under your finger. Tap one to hold its record at full brightness.

title: A Thousand Devices, One Score
note: A temple courtyard at night, from above: a thousand small glowing devices drift in slow currents through the crowd, gathering and dispersing. The courtyard is scored into zones, and each device glows with its zone’s color, warm, cool, rose, green, changing as it crosses a boundary: the map is the music. Through the crowd, three bright autonomous carts drive their own routes, and drones cross overhead with short streaks. A thousand players who do not know they are playing. Drag to become a current in the crowd. Tap a zone to hear it alone.

title: After the Bow
note: The venue after the performance: the audience gone, the dancers gone, the seats dark at the edges. But the machines keep their schedules: the light carts run their waypoint circuits across the empty floor, dimmer than showtime; the translucent screens glide on their platforms, projections still running to an empty house; the figure-eight conveyor blinks its balls for no one. The motion is identical to the show, patient, faithful, a little lonely. Drag and the nearest machines brighten, remembering the audience. Tap for a bow: everything pauses, then resumes.

title: The Screens, Unsynced
note: The phase relationship as composition: on a dark stage, five translucent screens ride on wheeled platforms, gliding with machined precision, abstract light shifting inside each. They share a master clock, but each carries a sync offset, and the offsets drift: sometimes all five move together, bright and locked, sometimes each wanders, dim and free, and the piece breathes between the states. Small dancer-blobs move between them as guests; the canvas itself has an itinerary. Drag to conduct the nearby screens toward sync. Tap a screen to flip it between locked and free.

title: The Piste, Watched
note: The too-fast made legible: a dark piste seen from above, two fencers reduced to shadows moving at speed, lunges, retreats, an exchange too fast to follow. But behind each sword tip a glowing ribbon unspools, tracing every feint and wrist flick, and the fastest motion leaves the longest glow. Along both sides, twenty-four cameras stand in two rows, each covering its eight meters, their zones pulsing softly as the fencers pass through: the handoff, camera to camera, down the line. No scores, no crowd: the bout and the machines alone. Drag across the piste to slow the bout under your finger.

title: The Rigid Body
note: What you see is not what the machines see: a dark stage split in two. On the left, plain aluminum frames stand in a row, matte gray bars with small white domes, calm, almost boring, while a cart ferries one frame slowly across. On the right, the same scene in the same instant: every infra-red dome burns white-hot, joined by red wireframe lines, the rigid bodies the motion-capture system reads, tracked to the millimeter, the cart a burning constellation in transit. One scene, two audiences. Drag across the machine view to hide domes and watch a wireframe wobble.

title: The Balls Know the Route
note: Light as dispatched units: on a black field, a figure-eight rail runs nearly invisible, and sixteen glowing balls travel it, each at its own speed, each blinking on its own timer, some fast, some slow, some holding. Where they pass, afterimages hang as discrete dying stamps, and the eight fills with a cloud of fading light: a three-dimensional space made of timing. The balls are the only light; the rail is a rumor. Drag along the rail to surge the nearest balls. Tap one to hold its blink steady.

title: Light, Ferried
note: The show as logistics: top-down on a dark venue, twelve small carts with glowing domes, half warm, half cool, drive their own waypoint circuits with machined precision, translating without turning, the way omni wheels move. Each leaves a fading trail, and the trails weave into a glowing route-map of the whole floor. At the center, a small temple drawn in dark lines: every circuit routes around it with respect. The carts pass, queue and cross, and never collide: the choreography of autonomous things. Drag to roadblock a cart off its route. Tap one to flash its dome.

title: The Other Audience
note: The truth of the craft: a dark stage split in two. On the left, the human view: white objects, cubes, mobilities, a frame, plain and calm, moving with machined precision. On the right, the camera view: the same scene in the same instant, but every marker burns, retroreflective dots, infra-red constellations, the wireframes the motion-capture system reads. Occasionally a constellation flares as the cameras lock on, while the human view stays indifferent. The object’s real audience is the machine. Drag across the camera view to occlude a marker and watch its wireframe wobble.

title: What the Stage Props Do at Night
note: The props’ own performance: on a dark stage, white cubes with faint underglow slide in formation, split around the dancer, and rejoin in new patterns. The cubes do not accompany the dance; they are the dance, moving at constant velocity with hard stops, their underglow pulsing once each time a cube reaches its mark. The dancer moves through them small and dark, a guest in the furniture’s choreography. The furniture has better discipline than the body. Drag to cue the nearest cubes toward your finger. Tap a cube to note its arrival.

title: The Eyes, Issued
note: Vision as issued equipment: a pair of headset-eyes floats on black, two large dark lenses with a stereo-camera rig between them, behind them the world they see, rendered as a faint fisheye field warped at the edges. The eyes look: the lenses track an invisible point, converging and diverging, never quite agreeing, because each pair is calibrated and the calibration hunts. Periodically the rig snaps to a test pattern, a brief red crosshair, then resumes looking. The fisheye field warps with the gaze: the distortion is the seeing. Drag and the lenses converge on your finger.

title: The Shelf, Loaded
note: A still life that breathes: on a dark workbench, a row of identical black devices lies in inventory, chunky knurled bezels, domed lenses, ribbed bodies, visible screws, some resting on bubble wrap. They are unlit, except one. The lit unit throws a warm flood onto the bench, holds it, and hands the light to the next: unit by unit the row tests itself, deliberately, with pauses. One unit stays dark when its turn comes; the row waits a breath, then the pass continues past it, honest, not broken. Drag across the units to test them under your finger. Tap one to hold its light.

title: Enter the White
note: The furniture of apparition: in a dark teal gallery stand white curved pods, large and quiet, each with a tall opening glowing softly at the mouth. Inside each opening a translucent cyan figure hovers, drifting and turning, never leaving: the image the pod carries. The pods rotate a few degrees each way on their bases, machined and deliberate, and the figures turn with them. Beside the pods, three glowing cyan cylinders with lit ring tops pulse softly: the booth line. White objects that hold light-people. Drag to turn a pod. Tap one to dissolve and reform its figure.

title: The Room, Moved
note: The room as a machine: in a dark gallery, tall white monolithic walls glide along invisible rails with machined precision, constant velocity, hard stops, no wobble. Blue and violet light washes move with the walls, locked to the slabs. Between them, narrow gaps open and close, and through the gaps a single dancer’s silhouette passes, small, the only body in the room, dwarfed by the architecture. The walls ferry; the room performs. Drag along a wall to command its heading. Tap a gap to hold the room still for a breath.

title: Three Hundred and Ten
note: Scale as the piece: above a dark rooftop, a field of identical lighting modules hangs in the air, small domed shades glowing from within, receding in perspective until the count reads as endless: three hundred and ten of them, one light. The shades breathe in slow waves that travel across the field, warm and diffused, no beams, no spots. Occasionally one shade dims out of sequence, a faulty unit, honest, and re-syncs. Drag across the field to push a swell of brightness through it, a wind. Tap a shade to extinguish it until it re-syncs.

title: Ridden by Nobody
note: The dance of the ridden, riderless: top-down on a dark stage, ten white personal mobilities glide on precise curved paths, radio-controlled, no riders aboard, performing for each other. Each carries a cluster of bright marker dots, the machine-vision truth the invisible cameras read, and their paths cross and weave in strict choreography: they never collide, never hesitate. Five white cubes on omni-wheel bases drift through the gaps as counterpoint, glowing faintly from beneath. The audience is the camera; the absence is the piece. Drag to divert a vehicle. Tap one to flare its markers.

title: Time Is the Instrument
note: A sequencer you watch: twelve small clocks tick across a black field, each at its own interval, some in simple ratios, some irrational, each with a thin ring that fills and empties with its period. Below them, twelve horizontal tracks of light play the composition the clocks conduct, brightening each time their clock ticks. When three or more clocks land together, their tracks flare as one: a downbeat, earned by the near-misses around it. The intervals are strange on purpose, a gamelan, not a scale. Drag across the clocks to bend their tempo. Tap a clock to slip its tick earlier.

title: The Flock, Wired
note: A white void, paper-white and total. In it, a flock of small skeletal drones flies, thin dark frames with faint rotor discs, each carrying a glowing white ball on top. The flock moves as one mind: wheeling, banking, splitting and rejoining, the balls brightening as a drone climbs and dimming as it dives. Every so often the flock gathers itself into a shape, a ring, a wave, a vertical column, holds it for a breath, and dissolves back into the wheel. No sky, no ground: the performance is the only event. Drag through the flock to scatter it. Tap to command the next shape.

title: The Inside, Honored
note: The autopsy as portrait: on a dark workbench, a device lies taken apart, its components laid out in a careful grid: control boards with amber traces and tiny glowing nodes, cylindrical capacitors, a coiled ribbon cable. The traces are alive: pulses of light travel the copper paths, each board keeping its own rhythm, and the rhythms phase-lock in waves across the grid, led by the microcontroller board at the center with its red status light. The machine is not dead: it is still thinking, honored by being opened. Drag across the boards to inject a pulse. Tap a board to hear it alone.

title: The Machine, Placed
note: A meditation on a machine: in a warm-white gallery, a matte black cube sits on a white plinth, seamless, no lights, no ports, no branding. It is not dead: it breathes, a faint pulse of brightness traveling across its faces like a sleeping animal. Above it, the wall carries its dreams: large quiet fields of ink-blue wash and drifting contours that evolve continuously, and change each time the cube’s breath peaks. A tiny black cube sits beside the big one in attendance. Drag across the cube to wake it slightly. Tap the wall for a new dream.

title: Left Eye, Right Eye
note: Stereo light, honestly rendered: two floodlight cones cross in a dark gallery, pulsing in strict alternation, warm for the left eye, cool for the right, always as a smooth crossfade, never a strobe. The frame is split down the middle into the two views, and a small matte white sphere floats at the crossing, drawn twice with a slight offset between the halves: stare at the seam and it lifts off the screen. Sometimes the rhythm stutters, a pulse drops, and the depth wobbles before re-locking. Drag to detune the sync and watch it slip.

title: What the Frame Carries
note: A prop that performs alone: a tall glass frame stands in a dark theater, carried and turned slowly by invisible hands. Projection mapping plays across it, flowing contour lines, drifting point fields, slow color washes, and the imagery is locked to the frame: when the frame turns, the light turns with it, exactly. Sometimes the mapping breathes past the frame’s edges into the dark and is pulled back in. The prop is dumb glass; the light makes it a screen. Drag to turn the frame yourself. Tap for a new mapping.

title: The Body the Lights Agree On
note: Seven points of infra-red light hang in a black stage, small and dim: the markers. Between them a faint frame is implied, and the seven points drift and rotate as one rigid body, never deforming, because the motion-capture system recognizes them as a single solid thing. Light plays across the frame, cool sweeps and amber pools conforming to its transform. Halfway through the loop the markers fade to almost nothing, the tracking you must never see, and the light keeps dancing on the ghost of the body. Drag to grasp and turn the body.

title: What the Blink Leaves
note: Dozens of small warm-white balls drift through a black void on invisible tracks, each blinking on its own private interval. The composition is not where the balls are but what their blinks leave behind: afterimage ghosts that draw ephemeral shapes in the dark, a dense bright knot where short intervals cluster, a faint ghost-arc behind one slow ball. Occasionally the intervals align and the whole field flares once, warm and bright, then falls back to its private rhythms. Candlelight, not signage. Drag to disturb the intervals.

title: The Blade, Sensed
note: The bout as data: on a dark piste floating in black, two white wireframe fencers duel while the hardware watches. Every blade tip leaves a thin cyan sensor trail studded with data ticks, white detection brackets ride the tips a fraction behind, and on each touch a burst of macroblocks digitizes the hit and an amber score bar at the top grows by one segment. No numbers, no commentary: the score is a bar and the fight is instrumented. Faint sensor rigs blink at the strip’s ends. Drag across the piste to glitch the trails.

title: Sit Down, Move Through
note: Software that terminates in your body: you are strapped into a VR chair gliding slowly through a surrounding field of data: point clouds streaming past at true parallax speeds, cyan wireframe rings passing overhead, red detection-box constellations, deep blue washes behind. The viewpoint banks, rises, and dives on a slow heavy arc, and a faint chair outline at the bottom of the frame tilts with it: the machine you ride. The motion is a glide, never a thrill. Drag to steer the chair. Tap to commit to a dive or a rise.

title: Where Ads Belong
note: A gallery of lies, properly hung: a dark concrete wall with a fire escape carries a loose grid of empty ad slots. One by one, counterfeit posters composite into them with a brief inpaint shimmer and a macroblock flicker: neon marks, halftone fields, confident shapes, no words, no brands, placed exactly where ads belong, flush and lit. They hang a while, fade, and the slot waits for the next forgery. Tap a slot to forge one yourself. Drag across a poster to tear it down.

title: 170,000 Dreams, One Cube
note: The inside of a diffusion model, exhibited: a black room bordered by a dense wall of tiny data strips, the 170,000 training images as texture that never resolves. Above, attention maps drift as glowing white constellations, connecting and dissolving. At the center, two latent image-fields morph into each other endlessly and never arrive, muted blue, rose, and green, around a small dark wireframe cube: the machine that holds the model, subordinate to its own inside. Below, thin white loss curves keep falling. Drag to walk through the latent space.

title: Detect, Segment, Erase, Rebuild
note: A machine-vision pipeline played as an instrument: five horizontal stages show the same night street five ways. Detect: the scene with cyan boxes hunting two walking figures. Segment: the street reduced to flat coded masks, white people, magenta buildings, green road. Inpaint: the figures erased, the background visibly healing behind amber fronts. Depth: the scene as flat grays, near bright, far dark. Composite: the finished frame, counterfeit posters in the slots and glitch confined to the figures. A bright wave sweeps the stack, pulsing each stage as it passes.

title: Nine Buffers
note: A glitch composer as a playable artwork: a three-by-three grid of live buffers on black, each cell doing real work. Detection boxes hunt drifting targets; grayscale silhouettes wander; ad-slot masks appear and dissolve; a halftone field pulses; RGB noise chews a hidden figure; a depth wash shifts; flat segmentation blocks rearrange; a surface heals itself; and in the corner, the master cell composites them all. No labels, no numbers: the cells are the interface. Tap a cell to study it alone. Drag inside one to tune it.

title: Mask Law
note: Corruption with a jurisdiction: on a perfect black field, a dancer moves inside a white outline, and the glitch, datamosh blocks, channel splits, quantization, lives only inside that silhouette, like a law of physics. Not one corrupted pixel ever crosses the boundary; the black around the body stays untouched and silent. The body writes and the glitch reads: when the dancer holds still, the corruption keeps living inside the paused mask. Drag to move the jurisdiction. Tap to hold the body and watch the inside keep burning.

title: The City, Edited
note: A night street that refuses to advertise: drawn buildings pan slowly past, their windows mostly dark, while every advertising surface is edited in real time. Billboards blank to flat white slabs, brutal and total, each erasure flaring with a burst of cyan and red macroblocks; other slots fill with counterfeit generative posters, neon marks and halftone fields with no words at all. Each pass, a different set of surfaces is erased or replaced. Drag across a poster to erase it yourself. Tap a blank slab to forge a new one.

title: The Body, Between Poses
note: A body that exists only in transition: a large white wireframe figure on black continuously morphs between dance poses, crouch, reach, twist, fall, and never once rests in any of them, because the next transition always begins before the last one lands. You can watch the mesh work: short gray vectors at the joints show where each vertex is traveling, and the fastest joints glow cyan. Every few seconds the figure hard-cuts to a new phrase with a single felt frame of white. Tap to slow time and study the between.

title: What the Sound Casts
note: The artwork is the shadow of a sound: in a gray-black gallery, huge soft projections sprawl across the wall, tree-branch forms slowly rotating, growing, and shedding limbs. The objects casting them exist only inside the sound software and are never shown; you see only what their shadows do. When the generative audio swells, the branches grow; when it recedes, they shed. A small console glows faintly at the bottom: the machine that makes the sound that makes the shadows. Drag to move the light and swing the shadows across the wall.

title: Eight Ways to Dream
note: A diffusion model’s learning, made legible: eight horizontal lanes each show the same latent composition at a different noise level, the top lanes nearly resolved into soft colored forms, the lower ones dissolving into gray static. A denoising wave cascades through the stack continuously: each lane clarifies, holds, re-noises, and clarifies again, offset from its neighbors, with a thin white loss curve falling along its bottom edge. No metrics, no percentages: eight dreams clarifying in parallel. Drag across a lane to knock it back into noise.

title: Your Pose, Drawn
note: The body-to-mesh mechanism, turned on you: a large blue wireframe figure stands in a black void, every joint driven by springs with real weight, lag, and overshoot. Drag near a hand or foot and that limb follows your finger, the whole body leaning in; move sharply and the limb tips emit white scribbles, loose hand-drawn strokes that are the true paths the tips traveled, fading over twelve seconds. Fast joints brighten where the mesh deforms. When you stop, the figure settles into a slow idle phrase of its own. Tap to cue a gesture.

title: The Wall Hums
note: An LED wall as a pure piece: a deep blue-black field of dense white diagonal scanlines, thousands of them, slightly irregular, breathing as slow waves of spacing and brightness roll through the hatching. A single small figure stands silhouetted at the bottom, nearly still: one person against the light. Now and then a starburst flare blooms somewhere in the field, magenta or green, brief and precise. The wall is the subject and it hums at a pitch set by its own line spacing. Drag to bend the lines gently around your finger.

title: A Face, In Dashes
note: Photographic content reduced to marks: on a black field, a giant face assembles from thousands of short white dashes, each one’s length set by the brightness of a generated portrait and its angle set by the portrait’s own contours. From a distance it is a face; up close it is only marks. It holds for a breath, dissolves back into scatter, and reassembles as a different face: frontal, three-quarter, profile, never the same twice. Thin green data columns scroll at the thirds behind it. Drag across it to scatter the assembly under your finger.

title: The Stage Explodes, Quietly
note: Performers inside a box-storm: on a black stage, three small blue wireframe figures dance a slow phrase while hundreds of hard white rectangles and triangles radiate outward from their bodies, tumbling and shrinking as they fly. The figures emit the storm: every sharp movement, an arm snap, a turn, detonates a burst of boxes from that limb. Above and below them, a stack of white wireframe ellipse rings rotates and breathes. It is a detonation in slow motion, in black, white, and one blue. Drag across the stage to detonate it yourself.

title: The Bout, Drawn
note: Officiating-grade broadcast graphics, as the artwork: a live arena feed fills the frame, two dim figures dueling on a piste under grain, the camera breathing slightly. Over the picture, every blade tip leaves a luminous ribbon, red for one side, cyan for the other, white at the core, each one a true history of where that blade has been for the last eight seconds. Thin crosshair reticles ride the ribbon heads, and where the ribbons cross they flash. There are no score bugs and no commentary: the drawing over reality is the whole broadcast. Drag sideways to scrub the replay.

title: System, Not Picture
note: His signature, made visible: on the left, four small live feeds: a camera, a tracking grid, a data stream, a waveform. In the center, the system itself: a tall stack of chunky processing blocks, sense, detect, render, output, each lighting up as mint data packets travel the flow lines into it. On the right, the image those packets build: a small figure moving through light, deliberately not the biggest thing on screen. A credit line along the bottom assigns the honors: system, Hanai; image, someone else. Tap a block to open it. Drag a feed to rewire the machine.

title: No Markers. Just Seeing.
note: Machine vision, honestly imperfect: a dark, grainy camera feed fills the frame, and fast white streaks cross it with no markers at all. The system watches: a thin amber box snaps around each streak, always two frames late, and the detected path draws itself as a glowing cyan line over the feed. Sometimes the box loses its object, freezes red while the streak escapes, then re-acquires; the trajectory keeps the gap where the track was lost. A tiny readout reports the confidence, and it dips when the system does. Drag to throw it something new to see.

title: On Cue, Every Night
note: A live system that must work: six channels run in parallel lanes, camera, projection, tracking, light, sound, network, each with its own live signal. Below them, a small stage window combines all six into one performing figure. Every minute the show cues on a countdown and performs; when a lane faults, and they do, the figure visibly simplifies, losing that signal, but the show never misses its cue. A status line along the bottom keeps the record, and it only ever counts up. Drag a lane to stress it, and watch the show adapt anyway.

title: The Input Is a Whisper
note: The quietest input, amplified into the largest image: at the center of a dark field, a tiny circle holds a whisper: a trembling line, a slow breath, a few micro-jitters, all simulated, never a real microphone. The room reads it fifty times larger three ways: the tremor becomes a cyan seismic waveform, the breath becomes a magenta radial pulse, the sideways jitter becomes a mint particle current filling the frame. A small label states the exchange: input whisper, output room. Double-tap for five seconds of silence, and watch the room empty.

title: A Light That Does Not Exist
note: A virtual illuminant casts a real shadow: a white figure dances slowly at the left of a dark stage, lit by nothing. On the back wall stretches its shadow, huge, soft, and wrong: it shows the pose from half a second ago, stretched tall, and sometimes it detaches entirely and wanders off on its own for a few seconds before rejoining. A pale pool on the floor is the only trace of the light that isn’t there. Occasionally a second impossible light flickers on and crosses a second shadow over the first. Drag to move the lamp that doesn’t exist.

title: Grows With the Audience
note: A model that only learns what you give it: on the left, a wall of small generative marks grows by one a second, all of them gray and untrained. On the right, a small machine renders its attempts, and it trains only on the marks somebody opted in: tap a mark and it glows green and joins the dataset; the attempts, which begin as noise, start echoing the contributed strokes. Nothing ever trains on a gray mark, even if the model is starving. A counter along the bottom reports the whole truth: trained on N marks, all opted in.

title: The Stage Is a Medium
note: Dancers inside a visible medium: two or three white figures move slowly through a dark blue-gray room that is filled, floor to ceiling, with hundreds of translucent pale-cyan boxes tumbling at every depth. The bodies displace the medium: boxes deflect around the dancers and a disturbed wake follows each figure through the field. A few boxes glow from within. Every so often the whole field exhales, drifting outward, cooling, then settles back. There is no floor and no wall: the boxes are the architecture. Tap a figure to follow it. Drag to pour the field.

title: Draw What the Blade Does
note: Things too fast to see, made visible by drawing their path: invisible movers duel across a black piste, each carrying one bright retroreflective marker dot, and the system samples the markers into long tapering ribbons, red, cyan, and white for the fastest, that persist for seconds and braid where the movers cross. The movers themselves are nearly invisible; the trail is the artwork, and if they vanished the drawing would still be complete. This is the lane’s thousandth piece. Tap a ribbon to study one blade’s handwriting. Drag to stir the air.

title: Phenomena
note: Rhythm and motion culled from minuscule phenomena, amplified: at the center of a dark field sits a tiny framed patch, 24 pixels of dust drift, tremor, and pulse, barely visible. The room reads it three ways at forty times scale: its sideways drift becomes a sweeping cyan current of particles, its trembling becomes a yellow seismic waveform, its pulsing brightness becomes a magenta breathing sun. Along the bottom, three faders mix the amplification live. The smallest thing in the room makes the largest image. Tap the patch for a new phenomenon.

title: The Model Watches
note: A model learns in public, honestly: on the left, an archive wall of small generative scribbles grows by one a second. On the right, a little stack of layer bars trains on them and keeps attempting the archive: early generations are noisy magenta blobs, later ones are structured mint echoes of the very same strokes, because each attempt is drawn from real archive scribbles with less and less noise as the loss falls. Every thirty seconds the best attempt is pinned to a gallery strip below. No magic, just a falling curve. Drag in the archive to curate what it learns from.

title: No Extant Tools
note: A hand-written render pipeline, shown instead of hidden: four stages stacked on a dark console. INPUT, a jittery cyan signal. RULES, where the signal visibly bends through three hand-drawn blocks: quantize makes it step, delay shifts it, fold mirrors it back on itself. GEOMETRY, where the ruled signal becomes a small yellow polyline creature. FEEDBACK, where the creature’s past returns as magenta echoes inside the signal itself. You watch code become image, and sometimes glitch. Tap a stage to solo it. Drag across a rule block to rewrite it.

title: Hold the Light
note: The audience moves a luminous ball, and beam lights build geometry from where it has been: eight projectors at the edges of a dark room fire thin beams at a glowing white ball as it drifts, and its recent positions become the vertices of a slowly rotating mint wireframe volume, a constellation built from its own path. The volume grows, holds, then exhales, its oldest points releasing. Three small dancers drift through; when a beam crosses one, it flares. Drag to hold the ball: it has weight, it lags, it hums. Tap to pulse the room.

title: Rules for a Body
note: One phrase, two outputs: on the left of a split stage a small dancer performs a seeded phrase; on the right, the same phrase is decomposed live by a rule. FRAGMENT shatters its trail into two dozen orbiting shards. MIRROR reflects it into a counter-phrase. QUANTIZE snaps it to a coarse grid, stepping like a low-resolution ghost. SPIRAL winds its trail into a growing helix. A strip of glyphs along the bottom names the active rule without a word. Tap a glyph to switch rules. Drag to decompose deeper.

title: The Invisible Blade
note: A fencing tip moves too fast for the eye, so the machine draws it: a fencer-dot lunges across a dark arena, and its blade’s trajectory synthesizes a beat behind the motion, because detection has latency and the lag is honest. The trail is velocity made geometry: brightness is speed, width is acceleration, color turns magenta where the path bends. At each lunge’s end the trail freezes into a gray engraving, and the arena keeps the last twelve as a score. A small amber reticle rides the detected tip, always a little behind the truth. Tap to thrust.

title: Chains
note: Live trading data rendered as a river: pulses of buying and selling flow along three dark threads, and every six events compress into a block, cyan for buys, magenta for sells, its height their volume, its level the price. The blocks chain and scroll, and a thin white trace through their midpoints draws the market’s contour. Occasionally a whale arrives, an oversized pulse whose block sends a yellow shockwave through its neighbors. No numbers, no axes: the river is the data. Tap to inject your own trade. Drag to stretch or compress time.

title: Fork This
note: The artwork is a platform: at the left, a big white dancer glyph performs its loop. Tap it and it forks: a smaller child appears beside it, mutated: a new color by generation, a shifted pose, a sparser or doubled line, running its own live loop and linked to its parent by a hairline of lineage. Children fork children; the family tree spreads right across the frame, a forest of variations all descended from one pose, every one of them still dancing. Drag across a branch to prune it. The piece never ends: it only forks.

title: Palm-Sized Dancers
note: Five palm-sized microdrones fly a tight ballet at the center of a dark stage, but the drones are not the system: four motion-capture cameras sweep scan lines from the corners, position-lock rings snap to each drone a beat late, faint dashed infrared frames hover around them, visible to the cameras and almost to no one else, and along the top a 2.4 GHz band ripples with every command burst. In the corner, a small panel shows the stage as the cameras see it: five white dots on black. Tiny dancers, enormous infrastructure. Tap to command a reform.

title: Backstage, Lit
note: The unglamorous layer, shown as the spectacle: a huge circuit board fills the frame, its traces carrying real packets, tiny white squares that light each trace segment as they pass, bound for the eight devices ringed around the edges: a drone, a spotlight, a wheelchair, an LED ball, a cube, a costume patch, a projector, a truck, each pulsing only when a packet actually arrives. At the right hangs a technical costume, its twelve sensor nodes firing in sequence down the limbs. Every light has a packet behind it. Tap a trace to probe it.

title: Ride the Stage
note: The audience rides through the dance: from above, six dancer-dots weave their phrases across a dark stage while four rider platforms glide among them on omniwheels, strafing sideways and spinning in place, never turning like cars. Each platform carries a small viewport showing the mixed feed: the real dancers near it plus virtual ghost dancers in cyan, dancing other phrases. When a viewport crosses a real dancer, a ghost syncs to it for a moment in a warm flash: the virtual and the real touch. Tap a platform to board it and ride.

title: Thread the Feed
note: The network becomes textile: a feed of short abstract messages rises from the bottom of a dark frame, and mid-frame an embroidery hoop catches them one by one and stitches them in, letter by letter, in slow glowing thread, each character landing with a tiny stitch dot. Inside the hoop the finished messages accumulate into a dense neon patchwork; when it fills, the whole cloth section slides down and folds away along the bottom, and the hoop starts again. Input in, cloth out. Tap to send a message of your own into the feed.

title: Gravity Is the Score
note: Flight derived from physical laws, not animation: twelve light-drones orbit three dancer-dots on a night field, but every drone is pulled down by gravity, lagged by inertia, damped by air, so the paths sag, wobble, and overshoot: you can feel the air. Each drone carries a small diamond with a projection mapped onto it, its stripes and grids shifting with the diamond’s tilt as a faint beam tracks it from off-frame. The physics is the choreography. Tap for a gust of wind. Drag upward to raise a thermal and watch them ride it.

title: They Have No Sense of Time
note: A dance class for the time-blind: three small dancer-dots perform phrases on a dark stage while three safety-orange robot arms try to learn them, replaying each phrase with a fixed lag, at constant joint velocity, with no anticipation and no flourish. A beat grid ticks along the bottom; every time a claw lands on the count, a tick locks into the robot’s ledger, and every miss stays an empty gap: the failure is the data. When two robots lock together, an amber cube changes hands. Tap to count in another robot. Drag across the grid to stretch the tempo.

title: Can a Spotlight Fly?
note: Ishibashi’s own question: a dark void, one small drone, and a miniature spotlight bolted underneath. The drone hunts in slow searching curves, pausing, tilting, while its warm cone sweeps the dark below, revealing dust motes that exist only inside the light. Where the cone lands, a warm pool blooms on the invisible floor and a slow ripple spreads: the light has weight, it presses. When it finds a drifting dust cluster, it holds, and the pool warms to full. One drone, one light, the question. Tap to aim it. Drag to fly it yourself.

title: Ball Track
