note: The machinery is the piece: dozens of full-color LED balls roll forever along a thin figure-8 spiral rail, and at each of seventeen infrared control points a ball’s color switches to its next programmed state, so ripples of color travel around the track. Along the bottom, visitor terminals blink: a tiny white command packet flies up to a control point and forces the next ball through it to change. Every effect shows its cause. Tap a control point to send your own command. Drag along the rail to speed or slow the segment under your hand.

title: The Wood Sings
note: Timber, timbre: a wooden electronic instrument floats on black, part cello, part circuit board, its grain flowing in long lines around a few knots. Eight strings cross it, studded with brass nodes; idle, a faint sap-glow travels the grain and every half minute the wood tunes itself with a slow arpeggio. The wood is the interface: no knobs, no screens. Tap a node to pluck it: the grain lights outward from your touch and its tone rings. Drag across the strings to bow a chord that brightens with your speed.

title: Signal Field
note: A black field of RGB particle static: thousands of tiny red, green, and yellow points drift in slow swirling clusters while white wireframe polyhedra travel through them, bending the particles around their edges. A deep pulse breathes under everything at fifty beats a minute, and the field brightens on each beat. Every forty seconds or so, a word slices across in huge glitch-cut type, RESONANCE, then dissolves back into points. Clinical, not festive. Tap to detonate the field. Drag to stir it.

title: Lobby Feed
note: The audience feeds the stage: the performance frame at the right stands ready, but the cast comes from the lobby. Small visitor-dots drift in from the doors at the top corners; as each crosses the capture line it is scanned in a warm mint sweep, a welcome, not a checkpoint, and projected into the frame at human scale as a dancing stick figure, keeping its own muted color. When the frame holds eight, the longest-resident bows in a warm glow and drifts home. Tap a door to admit your guest. Drag a dancer into the spotlight.

title: Before You Move
note: The signal arrives before the movement: a dozen braided pairs of lines flow across a dark field, a thin cyan signal line and a thicker white movement line tracing the same spikes and dives, the white always 120 milliseconds behind: you can see the future arriving. Where a signal spikes hard, a muscle-node flares and sounds: light and tone are triggered by the cause, never the effect. A tiny readout in the corner is proud of the head start. Tap to flex. Drag to draw a signal for the movement to chase.

title: The Flock Obeys
note: Machines as dancers: a warm-white dancer performs seeded phrases at center stage, lunges, spins, freezes, while eight cyan drones answer with readable rules: they orbit when it spins, scatter when it lunges, hover in a ring when it freezes, trail when it glides. At the right stands a tall frame where the dancer’s mathematical doppelganger, a mint stick figure, snaps every half second to the nearest archived pose, no interpolation, always a beat behind and never smooth. Tap to launch another drone. Drag to steal the flock for ten seconds.

title: Mirror, Dreaming
note: A mirror that dreams instead of reflecting: a dark humanoid silhouette stands at its center, nobody in particular, swaying gently, while around it a re-imagined scene blooms and shimmers at the edges: tonight an astronaut tableau, station panels, floating tools, the Earth glowing below. Across the top the current prompt types itself out, deletes, and types the next dream: a reef, a neon forest. The pose is always preserved; the dream is the weather. Tap for the next dream. Drag to blend two dreams yourself.

title: The Erased Crossing
note: Diminished reality at a night crossing: pedestrians cross the zebra as dark silhouettes, but the system erases them: a flickering mint outline, a dissolve, and the figure continues as the machine’s guess at a person: a ghost filled with wavy amber and teal striations. One figure is never erased: a warm-coated person at center, solid, breathing, occasionally adjusting their glasses, looking at the camera. The crowd is there, but only as hallucination. Tap a silhouette to spare it for thirty seconds.

title: Played
note: A face played like an instrument: a large wireframe face fills the frame, threaded with electrode leads to its muscle regions. A seeded etude runs: bright sparks travel the wires, and on arrival, always a beat behind the spark, the muscle contracts: the contour lines scrunch, an amber flash answers, a tone fires, brow high, jaw low. A small sensor dot in the corner twitches with each command: the hand commands, the face obeys. Clinical and musical, never cruel. Tap a muscle to fire it. Drag across the face to play your own phrase.

title: Emergency Level
note: An oracle that only reports a number: on a dark radar scope, amber jets fly their historical routes, drawn as faint arcs, and the system watches for deviation. When a jet strays from its baseline, its trail flares red and a tick joins the ledger beside the gauge: a tall one-to-five meter at the right edge whose amber needle climbs with clustered deviations and relaxes as traffic normalizes. At five, the scope’s rim pulses red. No headlines, no explanations: the gauge is the message. Tap a jet to file a report. Drag along a route to move the goalposts.

title: The Sound Is the Light
note: The sound is controlled by the light: in a dark chamber, a pile of mirror spheres sits on a platform, ringed by swirling binary dust. A soft greenish beam rakes across the pile, and wherever it touches a sphere, that sphere flares and sings: a shimmering note pitched by its place in the pile, its ripple ring expanding. Every flare is caused by the light; nothing twinkles on its own. Tap to cue the beam through a point. Hold a drag to pin it and sustain a chord.

title: The Screens Are Watching
note: The reversal: a wall of twelve laptop screens glows in a dark gallery, but they show no content: each shows a face drawn in its own light, two eyes, a nose tick, a mouth arc, staring out. All twelve pairs of pupils track the same unseen point as it wanders; occasionally one face blinks, never all at once. A red recording dot migrates from screen to screen: someone is always being recorded, and the dot moves. Tap a screen and the whole wall looks at you. Drag, and you are the thing being watched.

title: Siphon
note: The invisible made visible, quietly: twelve serene figures sit in a dark room, each periodically beaconing a faint ring into the air: their devices, calling out. A hollow red circle with an ear roams between them, and when it passes a ring it siphons it: the ring spirals into the listener, and the figure’s data leaks upward as a drift of small amber glyphs. Nobody reacts. The leak is ambient, like weather. Tap a figure to make it call out. Drag to do the listening yourself.

title: Panoptic Perceptron
note: Query by example, played as a mosaic: sixty-four abstract satellite tiles, each a tiny seeded miniature of blobs, lines and grids, each also an eight-number description the machine computed. One tile is the query, outlined in mint; every twenty seconds the perceptron re-ranks the city by similarity and the twelve nearest tiles slide in to assemble around it at full brightness while the rest recede into dimness. Then a winner becomes the new query, and the city is seen again. Tap any tile to aim the panopticon.

title: Follow Everyone
note: A plaza from above, annotated by everyone: forty walkers cross a dark paving grid in seeded streams, and over them float thought-bubbles written by the crowd: one to three invented glyphs each, dialogues and noises no one can read. Tags attach, drift, detach, and sink into a fading ticker along the bottom: the poem of the plaza. An amber bus periodically arrives and empties eight more walkers into the poem. Tap a walker to tag it yourself. Drag from one to follow it.

title: Eyes Shut
note: A self-portrait drawn by a hand that is not allowed to see: under a warm ring light, a white hand-dot draws one continuous line, wandering toward the landmarks of a face and missing them, the classic blind-contour wobble, while a mint eye floats above, closed. The rule is absolute: if the eye opens, the hand freezes mid-line. Finished portraits peel off and join a tagged wall of previous attempts. Tap to peek for two seconds, and watch the line stop dead. Drag to cheat the blindness, briefly.

title: The Shortest Stack
note: Counting, knitted: a counter runs upward in binary, each number drawn as a strip of black and white stitches, and every strip is placed on whichever row of the field is currently shortest. The rows fill their valleys first and a striated cliff grows; when the count tops out, a new season starts on top and the old ones compress below. Two yarns only: the complexity is in the counting. Press and hold to stop the machine mid-strip. Tap for a new sweater.

title: Seeing Voices
note: The voice in your head, drawn as rings: a white dot walks a dark maze toward its center, steered by a pulsing violet voice-ring three times its size: every three seconds the rings pulse and the dot obeys. A cyan thread remembers the route. Sometimes the voice disagrees with itself: the rings split into two red-edged sets, the dot hesitates and jitters, then the voice re-converges and the walk goes on. No words, ever: the moment it speaks it stops being a voice. Tap to whisper a suggestion. Drag to sow doubt.

title: Saliva Exchange
note: A bar where strangers trade DNA like drinks: patrons queue along a dark counter, and at the attendant’s station, pairs exchange strands: two dotted helices rise, cross mid-air, and trade colors as they cross, cyan becoming magenta, magenta cyan, then sink into the other patron, tinting them a little toward what they received. The queue shuffles forward forever; the bar fills with tinted regulars: a portrait of circulation. Tap a patron to inspect its strand. Drag one to the front of the line.

title: Social Turkers
note: Thirty first dates, directed by gig workers: a grid of thirty small arenas, in each a white dot orbits a magenta dot while tiny cyan vote-ticks along the edges steer the orbit, the invisible hands of paid strangers refreshing their votes every two seconds. Every twenty seconds or so an arena resolves: a tight orbit becomes a mint ring, a loose one a red cross, and the glyph stays as the season’s ledger while a new date begins. Tap an arena to rig its vote. Drag between arenas to swap the dates.

title: 24 HOUR HOST
note: A party run by an invisible host: eight guests drift in a dark circular room while an unseen AI periodically scans them with a thin cyan sweep, then whispers pairings through the host’s earpiece: white arrows arc out, and the guests converge into constellations, hold, and disperse, in ninety-second cycles of choreography nobody chose. The AI is never drawn: only its orders are. Tap to call a pairing round. Drag to hold the earpiece yourself.

title: LAUREN
note: A human playing a smart home, drawn as a floor plan: an attention-eye tours a schematic house of seven rooms, and the house anticipates it: before the eye arrives, the next room’s lights warm amber, its door swings open, its speakers pulse. A fading mint trail records where attention has been; the rooms it just left stay warm a few seconds, like a held glance. The eye never blinks and is never late. Tap a room to request a visit. Hold to see the house’s whole memory of being watched.

title: Follower
note: Surveillance as a service, drawn as its trace: on an abstract night grid, a white dot wanders the streets all day, and fourteen seconds behind it a red ribbon follows its exact route, fading as it ages: the follower, who is never a body, only the record. When the followed looks back, the trace vanishes for five seconds and a gap stays in the record forever. At day’s end the scene freezes under a flash and a white border: the single photograph the followed takes home. Drag to redirect the wanderer; the tail never breaks.

title: Crowdpilot
note: A blind date steered by a crowd: a white dot walks a faint corridor toward a magenta target while three advisors, a friend, a stranger and a hired assistant, flash direction chevrons from the frame’s edges. Every two seconds the votes tally and the dater turns by majority, and its trail takes the winner’s color: a barcode of who was driving. No words anywhere: the vote is the conversation. Tap an advisor to weight its voice. Drag the target to change the subject.

title: Happiness Hat
note: A diagram of discipline: forty-eight wearers, pale circles with a single arc for a smile, sit in eight rows under a mint line: the required smile. Smiles slacken. A sensor makes its rounds; when a smile falls short, a red spike fires from behind the wearer and the arc snaps back to the line with a twitch. Mint is the law, red is the punishment, and the grid breathes corrections forever. Tap to move the law to a new height. Drag across the wearers to commit the crime yourself.

title: An Empty Room
note: The quietest piece in the gallery: a square of deep dark, and inside it a room drawn in barely lighter tones, breathing: its edges swell and settle two percent over a ninety-second cycle. Forty dust motes drift inside, brightening as they cross an invisible diagonal beam of light, dimming after. Every few minutes a pale ghost shape crosses the room at a whisper and dissolves. Built to hang on a wall for hours and ask nothing. Tap for a breath. Drag to stir the dust.

title: Still Life (HSB D, After)
note: The five Platonic solids as translucent ghosts: tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron and icosahedron orbiting a common center on near-black, each washed in its own hue, faces at a third opacity, edges bright, overlaps flaring where the colors add. Every motion is tuned so the whole configuration returns exactly to itself every sixty seconds: a perfect loop, the craft of the piece. Tap a solid to hold its orbit; it catches up and the loop still closes. Drag to tilt the heavens.

title: Simulacrum (After)
note: A plotter drawing that never touches paper: one continuous line at a constant Micron weight wanders the sheet, then resolves, over four minutes, into the wireframe ghosts of the five Platonic solids, overlapping, corners overshot by a hair the way a real machine overshoots. One ink per sheet: black, then sepia, then indigo, then a fresh sheet. No taper, no wobble: the steadiness is the beauty. Tap to lift the pen. Drag to sketch in pencil what the pen will ink next.

title: Today's Ideology (After)
note: A day’s paper, abstracted past recognition: twelve synthetic photographs, hard-edged geometries in newsprint tones, distorted the mechanical way: horizontal slice bands slide at their own speeds, color channels split red and cyan in alternating bands, and every forty-five seconds the grid re-cuts itself with a stutter. The dateline in the corner advances a day every three minutes and the paper regenerates. No faces, no words: the news, remembered only as a grid.

title: Every Combination
note: Every possible combination, walked in order: a grid of colorform tiles, bars, circles and quarter-arcs in seeded arrangements, stepping one tile every twenty seconds through the full combinatorial space: 1,280 forms, no repeats, counted honestly in the corner. Every two minutes the city changes and the tiles re-tint: Tokyo neon on black, Berlin concrete, London fog and red, New York taxi, Mexico City, LA pastels. Tap a tile to step it. Drag to scan the space.

title: Omnia
note: A small watercolor, translated into a score: seeded blooms in sage, umber, slate and rose pool dark at their edges, and two hundred agents hatch from those pools to read the painting. The wash is their terrain: dark pigment slows them like syrup, pale wash lets them run, and every step drops an ink dot in the color of the wash beneath. Over minutes a second image accretes over the first: a dotted cartography of the watercolor. Tap for rain. Drag to stir the painting itself.

title: 100 Agents, Straight Lines
note: The score, performed: one hundred agents walk in straight lines and nothing else. When two paths cross, both turn, left if the other is younger, right if older, and a white bloom marks the crossing. Their fading trails build a city: dense intersections downtown, long boulevards where nobody was interrupted. Every three minutes the score advances: the turn changes, the palette warms, the agents learn to avoid each other’s trails. Tap to freeze three agents mid-step. Drag to raise a temporary wall.

title: Nine Fields, Moving
note: Max Bill’s nine fields, reimagined as a software sketch: a 3 by 3 grid where every field is split between two hues along a seeded edge, in Bill’s own palette of cobalt, vermilion, ochre, viridian, carbon and cadmium. Every eight seconds one field resolves: its edge sweeps to a new angle, its hues step to a neighboring pair, and its neighbors drift in sympathy. One field at a time: a quiet perpetual argument. Tap a field to make it resolve now.

title: Sixteen Forests, One Canopy
note: Sixteen tropical forests distilled into one canopy that runs on its own sensor weather: humidity clumps the leaves, light gilds them, temperature speeds their drift, thermal columns lift them, and every few minutes a storm rolls through, darkening and churning the canopy before it clears. A strip at the bottom reads the forest’s instruments live. Tap for a clearing of sun. Drag for wind. Double-tap for a different forest entirely.

title: Facade, Dreaming
note: The building as a dreaming canvas: a perspective facade in indigo and steel, its bays converging to an off-center vanishing point, and over it three thousand particles of data-paint stream, pool and eddy, slowing in the curved bays, shying from the darkest ones, surging across the whole building every ninety seconds. The architecture never changes; only the dream does. Tap a bay to wake it. Double-tap for a new dream on the same building.

title: Seventy Heartbeats, One Painting
note: A living painting grown from heartbeats: seventeen simulated visitors, each an oscillator between 58 and 92 beats a minute with a living jitter, send rings out through a dark field of embers, and where rings cross the particles ignite warm. The hearts slowly drift toward unison, flare, and drift apart again; the strip at the bottom tells the truth about it. Tap your own rhythm four times and your heart joins the painting. Drag to hold a breath.

title: A Reef That Never Stops Growing
note: A reef that grows and hallucinates forever: recursive walker-tips extend, fork and die back across six colonies on a black seabed, new tips glowing white, old growth fading over a minute into shadow. Now and then a bleach wave passes over one colony and it re-grows in a new hue through its own pale skeleton: stress and recovery, the reef’s memory. Tap a tip and a polyp blooms. Drag for current. Nothing ever resets: death is fade, birth is growth.

title: Weather Inside the Machine
note: The room responds: a latent-walk dreamscape whose weather is real. The hour sets its hue temperature (amber dawn, cyan noon, magenta dusk, deep blue night), the day of the year sets its turbulence, and a slow room-noise gives each day its own character. A thin strip at the bottom reads the room: the time, the drift, the calm. Open it at 6am and at 11pm and it is a different piece. Drag for a gust. No microphone: the room it reads is the clock’s.

title: A Thousand Dimensions, Flattened
note: A thousand dimensions flattened into a sculpture: twenty-five hundred points from a twelve-dimensional dataset, projected and force-settled into four brain-coral clusters that turn slowly in pseudo-3D, breathing out of phase, storming now and then as one cluster pulls tight. Tap a cluster and it answers with three heartbeats. Drag to spin it. Double-tap and a new dataset re-grows the sculpture, every point traveling to its new home.

title: A Memory, Plotted
note: Data is not just numbers, data is a memory: six hundred of them, each with a year, an intensity and a name, embedded as four glowing archipelagos, ember, gold, ice, violet, ringed by contour ribbons. The constellation breathes; every so often a memory migrates, walking across the dark to another family and changing color as it goes. Tap one to read its record: 1979, the summer of the storm, intensity 0.83.

title: Dreams Without Cuts
note: Anadol’s latent walk, the dream that never cuts: three thousand particles ride a flow field with four poles, a magenta vortex, cyan rivers, an amber bloom, a deep blue storm, and the walk melts from pole to pole over minutes, different regions changing at different rates, colors shifting as it goes. Nothing ever jumps: tap and it leans toward the nearest pole, drag and it stirs, double-tap and even the new dream arrives by interpolation.

title: Measured Like a Body
note: Sewing patterns as a way of knowing someone: the cutting table lays out a subject the way her grandmothers measured a body, dotted red cutting lines, grain arrows, notches, drill holes, gold pins. The pieces are the subject’s parts: for a relationship, the first year, the argument, the repair, the long summer. The annotations measure the unmeasurable: patience 14, trust, in cm: all of it. Tap to measure something else: an AI, a painting, a week. Drag a pin and the pattern re-grades around it.

title: Fifty-Two Characters, One City
note: Fifty-two channels of installation become one schematic city: ten train lines as characters, their personalities read off their data. Old lines shudder, long lines trail far behind themselves, social lines pause at transfer stations, and when two characters meet at a station they trade a small spark: the connections made, and sometimes missed. Tap a line to meet it. Drag for rush hour. Double-tap for night service: only the 7, the A and the L keep running.

title: Written, Then Unread
note: A diary that keeps the ritual and burns the evidence: the hand writes real journal pages, timelines, letters, lists, then free entries down the page, but the letterforms are stripped to minimum strokes: the rhythm of writing, the word-shapes and line-breaks and flourishes, with nothing legible anywhere. Tap and the same page rewrites in a new mood: calm, restless, tender. Drag to guide the hand. Double-tap to turn the page.

title: Giochi: The Studio Takes Itself Apart
note: Her studio, taken apart and playing: flat rooms in sage, clay, dusty blue, ochre and plum, and the objects wander: a plant chasing a chair, a lamp chasing a stack of books, nobody ever quite caught. Each trails its path-line behind it, in the color of the room it started in, until the line gets tired of its color and puts on a different one halfway, with a knot to mark the change. Tap an object to follow it. Drag for wind. Double-tap to rearrange the studio.

title: Modelli Circolari: A Model of a Model
note: A painting that is a model of a model: one obsession, one color family, whole square. At the center an inner focus circle hosts the diagram she is building to understand it: symbols, connections, single words, memory, signal, the self. Threads stitch across the gridded paper. Every minute the color drains and a new theme takes the square: identity in blue, musical notation in gold, choreography in green. Tap a symbol to read it: a synapse, a seam, a downbeat.

title: Incroci: Five Dates Each
note: Ninety-nine strangers, five significant dates each, painted in black between three rails: the day on the left, the month across the middle, the year on the right. Every line is one date; where strangers share a day, a month, a year, the crossing glows faintly gold. Tap any line and it will tell you whose it is: born 14.03.1988, first word 1990, the wedding, the storm. All black on paper: the discipline, and the overlaps are the beauty.

title: A Life, Stitched
note: Fourteen thousand four hundred ninety-six days, stitched: an accordion book where a life is sewn in white thread on paper, so faint you must lean in, while the events glow over it in the legend’s colors: yellow for achievement, blue for travel, red for love, a red cross for a break-up, a black cross for a loss. The needle takes ninety seconds to sew one life. Tap an event to learn its name: a first word, the year of the storm.

title: Dear Someone: A Weekly Correspondence
note: Dear Data as a ritual engine: every week the postcard asks one small question (times I checked the clock; smiles at strangers; texts I did not send) and invents a code that has never existed before to answer it. Spiral-wrapped stems, circle clusters, looped threads, day arcs, one grammar per week, never reused. The legend is part of the artwork, hand-lettered in the same wobble as the data. Tap to flip it over: the legend writ large. Drag to tilt it in the light.

title: Four Inks, One Poster
note: A poster printed the slow way, in the open: four halftone plates, cyan for temperature, magenta for visitors, yellow for words, black for time, each dot’s size a data value, each plate slightly misregistered, inks multiplying where they overlap. DATA IS A HUMAN MATERIAL, set big across the top. Tap to isolate one ink and read its stream alone, drag to push the registration out, double-tap for fresh data.

title: Fifteen Years of Branching
note: Her signature diagram, growing: a tree of decisions with wobbling pencil branches, every split named, leaves as colored data-dots at the twig tips. Fifteen years of projects roots at the bottom: work, data, drawing, books. It grows for a minute, holds in full leaf, sheds, and regrows. Tap for another tree: a Dear Data week, then a word-tree that branches into twiglets and leaflets. Drag for wind. Double-tap for winter.

title: My Teacher Is Three
note: Two agents, one page: a three-year-old scatters a dozen bright fridge magnets wherever she likes, and the designer may only draw around them in pencil, never move one. Her modes are the adult’s three answers: trace their contours, hatch the gaps, or connect their centers. Tap to swap teachers, drag to be the child and drop more magnets, double-tap for a fresh scatter. The caption is hers: she added a few bits to make it better. she was right.

title: What the Biobank Sees
note: One person, about 300 labelled data points: blood pressure, ECG trace, consent form, urine sample. Every two minutes the biobank’s formatting explodes her, points drifting along dotted chains of custody into structured grids, unstructured wanderings and stored rows, then gathers her again. Tap to change whose eyes you see through, eight perspectives. Double-tap for the unstructured data alone, the part that is there but not formatted for research.

title: What Ship Would You Be?
note: A badge engine in the grammar of Royal Navy crests: every visitor gets a ship’s badge where the sky’s crosshatch is their nerves, the sea’s waves their conscientiousness, the token their warmth, the ring’s weight their openness, and the size the popularity of their word. The legend runs along the bottom in the same hand. Tap a badge to read it, swipe to shuffle the fleet, double-tap for a new crew.

title: The Hidden Beauty of Long Multiplication
note: Schoolbook arithmetic as ornament: a real long multiplication worked in full on paper, 452823 by 983, every digit a hand-stroked glyph, partial products cascading in blue, the carries arcing violet above the addition, the product boxed in gold at the bottom. It works itself over ninety seconds, forever. Tap for new factors, drag to smudge the digits, double-tap to see the carries alone.

title: I Am a Piece. Ask Me Anything.
note: The companion narrator, and this one does not wait: it advances its own pages every seven seconds, measuring itself as it goes. Strips exactly as long as it claims, a width it can prove, a count of the babies born while you have been looking (it counted none of them). Drag it upward and it will tell you your altitude in anteater-tongues. Double-tap to slam it shut and hear something new.

title: A Week of Checking the Time
note: Dear Data, Week 01: a postcard that draws its own week, seven columns of wobbly pencil arrows, length for the hour, direction for the reason (up for appointments, right for boredom, down-left for running late), color for the device. Tap to flip it over: the legend in the same pencil hand, squeezed next to the stamp, the postmark and a coffee ring. Double-tap for a new week.

title: Eleven Years of Invoices
note: Eleven years of UK invoices in two layers: above, a string quartet of four gold ribbons whose note lengths are the average payment speeds, slow quarters stretched long and taut; below, a cyan pulse grid ticking at 120 BPM, the uninterrupted metronome of global trade. No artistic license was applied to the underlying metrics. Tap to hear each layer alone, drag to lean into a slow quarter, double-tap for the pulse by itself.

title: Forwards Is Growth
note: The US economy as a breakbeat ring: 232 quarters since 1968 in neon on black, pink spinning forwards for growth, cyan reversed for recession, so the financial crisis is a seven-quarter backwards run at the bottom of the loop. The legend is printed at the top. Tap a segment to isolate its quarter, drag to scratch the loop like a record, double-tap to hold the long recession.

title: I Am a Piece. I Am a Portal to the Data.
note: A book that narrates itself, strictly 1:1: it tells you its width in pixels and means it, keeps a water drop of exactly six pixels because a mouse drinks less than six millilitres a day, counts its own loop seconds while you stand inside them. No charts anywhere; the object is the data. Tap to turn its pages, drag to drop it and watch it splash exactly as wide as it is, double-tap to slam it shut and reopen it somewhere new.

title: Bonfire Nightmare
note: A year of Bristol air as weather: amber haze drifting over a night skyline, its density the particulate reading, thickest on bonfire night; below, the drone waveform that sings the same curve, and ripples where the dub echo throws the peaks back. The legend is printed at the top, the data gathered by citizen scientists. Drag to clear the air with your hand, tap for the echo.

142,036 EU laws drawn as a fugue: the number of laws each year from 1952 to 2019 is the number of gold voices weaving the score, one ribbon in the quiet years, eight at the legislative peaks, each entering with its Ode to Joy notation strip. One encoding, stated at the bottom. Tap a year to hear its voices enter, drag to scrub the decades, double-tap for the single voice of 1952.

title: Zippo Season
note: The 2023 Canadian fire season as 6,600 ember marks on one band: sharp orange flames for human fires, the Zippo ting; low brown embers for natural ones, the wood crackle; igniting at two and a half seconds a day. Tap to strike a match and add your own fires to the count, drag for wind, double-tap to stop on a day and read its number.

title: On Standby
note: A piece designed to be slept to: seven lanes of overnight devices, fridge, router, phone charger, TV, console, laptop, speaker, each pulse of mint light a draw of power, brightness for wattage, width for duration. Ten minutes stand in for ten hours, and the piece says so. Drag toward a lane to listen closer, tap a lane to leave it a trickle.

title: Nenana
note: A century of Nenana ice breakups as a thermometer staff: 109 bands, each placed at its true date, higher for an earlier melt, blue for late years and amber for early ones, with 2019, the earliest on record, in gold near the top. The century plays at a year a second. Tap a band to hear its chord and see its date, drag to scrub the century, double-tap for the ten earliest breakups burning alone.

title: Atlantis
note: Plato’s city as a machine diagram: three concentric land rings turning at three different speeds under four fixed bridges, housing blocks riding their rings, watchtowers breathing around the rim, a temple at the still center. Tap to send the signal out from the temple, bell by bell. Drag to turn the orrery yourself. Double-tap for the black-on-white inversion.

title: Scorched Earth
note: The piece opens as its own legend: six quiet lines of type on paper. Then a flame catches at the center of the text and a burning ring grows outward at the rate the land burnt, week by week, until the year is a set of tree rings on charred paper. Tap to ignite it yourself, drag to give the burn a wind, double-tap for the whole year in eight seconds.

title: The End of the Road
note: Danish windshield counts as a requiem: twenty years of insects on near-black, each year a column of fluttering ticks, amber for the big ones, pale for the small, dense in the first year and thinning year by year until the last columns are nearly empty. A bell tolls at every year’s turn. Drag to lean in and slow time, tap a year to hear it alone, double-tap to return to the abundance of the first year.

title: Fused Grid
note: Four diamond quadrants of a circuit-board city, each tiled with random rectilinear street modules folded on themselves, hatched blocks scattered, two double-weight avenues crossing the whole. The plotter draws it quadrant by quadrant and the finished board stays. Drag to trace the streets with a fading current, tap to re-fuse a new city, double-tap for the black-on-white inversion.

title: UFO
note: The International Space Station as an oscillator: a bright dot circling a small dark Earth on a 92 second orbit, its altitude breathing the waveform in the readout below between 40 and 90 hertz, the telemetry printed honestly in the corner. Tap for a sonar ping, drag to bend the orbit like gravity, double-tap for one fast lap of the Earth.

title: The Future
note: A disc of nearly a thousand tiny ink trees, 954 in this planting: canopy circles and grass tufts packed edge to edge, with two clearings, a propeller hub above and a city-block hub below. The forest plants itself in a spiral and replants forever. Drag for wind through the glyphs, tap for a new forest, double-tap for the survey: the hubs turn the one green and the census prints.

title: Hold the Line
note: Canada’s 2023 wildfire season as a visible instrument: a timeline of ticks, yellow for human fires, orange for natural, grey for unknown, a dark rumble band of burnt land thickening beneath, and a stack of notes rising above as the area accumulates. Tap a day to live inside it, drag to scrub the season, double-tap for the 226-fire day.

title: Sforzinda
note: Filarete’s ideal city in plotter ink: a star plan drawn live, radial streets running from a ring of gates out to tower points, a moat circle, tiny buildings stamping in one by one where the streets converge. Every city is a new throw within strict limits. Drag to turn the plan on its drafting table, tap for a fresh city, double-tap for eight seconds of the white-on-black inversion.

title: spherical inversion and trigonometry
note: The workbench as artwork: one black curve bent through spherical inversion on white paper, and beside it the tool’s own parameter panel in monospace, values live, star meters and all. Drag to turn the zoom and radius knobs, tap to step the highlighted parameter, double-tap for the zero state.

title: inky skies
note: Paper marbling as weather: dark and dark-red ink ribbons looping and folding through milky grey, thinner where they stretch, pooling where they cross. Drag to stir the water, tap to drop fresh ink, double-tap to freeze the perfect print for six seconds.

title: Hilbert goes for a walk
note: A 16 by 16 grid walked by the Hilbert curve: squares bloom large and pale where the walk has just passed, settle through orange to red behind it, and wait ahead as small hollow outlines. Tap to re-roll the warm palette, drag to pull the walker to your finger, double-tap to subdivide into 32 by 32.

title: silly dither
note: A billowing volume made of nothing but white dots on black: ordered dithering, dense where the smoke is bright, dissolving at the edges. Drag to thicken the dots under your finger, tap to flip the dither pattern, double-tap to scatter it into static and watch it re-gather.

title: checkerboard fbm
note: A checkerboard warped by fbm noise into dark rolling terrain, lit like a storm: a bright blue-white front breaks in from one edge. Drag to move the light across the relief, tap to send the storm surging across the field, double-tap to flatten it to a perfect checkerboard for six seconds.

title: little flowfeilds
note: One tiny weather system: a small disc of indigo, mustard, and maroon flow streaks circulating like a fingerprint on a vast cream emptiness. Tap to reseed its weather, drag to nudge it (it settles shyly back), double-tap for a second smaller field beside it.

title: flow fields
note: A full-bleed river of metallic streaks: thousands of fine lines flowing through a curl field into a bright vortex off-center. Drag to plant a second vortex under your finger, tap for a surge, double-tap to drain the field to a ghost and watch it rebuild.

title: noise on top of noise
note: A pale pink wireframe torus, warped by noise on top of noise, tumbling slowly in a black void, small and alone. Drag to lean its spin, tap to reseed the warp, double-tap to freeze the noise away and see the perfect torus for six seconds.

title: Em_p/t.'y
note: Ink rivers seen from the air: thick black ribbons slithering across a pale blue-grey marbled terrain, re-contouring as they flow. Drag to carve a valley they pool into, tap to spring a new river, double-tap for the drought: six seconds of empty terrain before the waters return.

title: m_is.'s/u
note: A specimen, not a performance: a fibrous monochrome vortex of torn concentric rings around a black void, breathing almost imperceptibly. Tap to turn the page to the next vortex in the series, double-tap for a slow close-up into the void.

title: R_u.'n
note: Two panels: above, a black screen where a single white line redraws itself forever, knot to coil to knot; below, the strip of the sequencer that drives it, one amber step light walking its row. Drag to take the line’s head in your hand, tap to reseed its start, double-tap to force its densest knot.

title: Suspension of d_is/b[e]l/ie.'f
note: His one landscape: a monochrome hillside, a hooded figure seated in the corner, and a single shocking magenta orb hovering above the slope, the only color allowed. Drag to tear glitch corrosion across the terrain and the orb drifts to feed on it; tap to churn the orb, double-tap to detonate it.

title: Phy/s[a]/ru.'m
note: A pale slime mold thinking in veins: a reticulated grey network grows from seed points across a pale ground and melts back into soft puffs when unfed. Drag to lay a nutrient trail it grows toward, tap to drop a seed, double-tap to starve it into full dissolution.

title: Coll/[i]s/io.'n
note: A white urchin crystal on deep black, hundreds of jittered spikes pulsing between a dark spore state and a blazing bluish-white expansion. Drag to make it flinch, tap for a polarity punch, double-tap to hold it at full blaze.

title: F_o.'r y[o]u, m_us.'e
note: A black fractal fern on clean white, hundreds of feathery fronds blooming from a dense core, then contracting into a pinwheel eye medallion and blooming again on a long breath. Watch only; tap to snap the eye shut for an instant, double-tap to hold the medallion.

title: A_n.'d gh[o]st.'s
note: Sakr’s polarity strobe: a black inkblot sunburst on paper white, hairline filaments radiating like cracked glass, the whole frame flipping black to white on a slow flicker clock that quickens as the blot contracts. Watch it breathe; tap for one instant flip, double-tap to hold the current polarity for five seconds.

title: Cyan Eddy
note: A grey smoke field with one lit current: the fastest particles render as cyan-white filaments threading through the murk and curling into a slow central eddy. Stir in circles to spin the eddy up, drag straight to tear it, tap for a gust, double-tap for five seconds of perfect spiral.

title: Bliss Seed
note: A dim starburst seed at exact center that grows only with patience: hold your touch near it and over half a minute the blades lengthen into a full cross flare with violet at the tips; starve it and it sighs back down, never quite dying. Tap for one drop of light, double-tap to command rest.

title: Low End Brightness
note: Klsr’s own statement of the method: one dim line that thickens into filaments, blooms, and saturates into noise over about three minutes, then exhales back, the low end driving brightness the whole way, a thin arc marking the progression. Drag to conduct it forward or back, tap for a snare bloom, double-tap to hold it mid-breath.

title: No Star Is Lost
note: An ink creature on clean off-white, magenta and purple with teal accents and black smoke rising through it, growing, blooming, and going spent unless fed. Drag through it to feed it, tap to drop a new seed, double-tap to wash the page clean.

title: Lit Bottle
note: Lightning in a bottle: a violet discharge column in smoke that must be charged by hand. Press and hold to charge it, release for the strike, tap for a fork, double-tap to ground it into darkness.

title: Slipstream
note: An aurora field of filaments curling through a slow current, each ribbon shifting teal to green to violet along its length. Drag to raise the wind, tap to bloom a knot, double-tap to freeze the sky into a still.

title: Chasing
note: A cross flare floating in the dark, blade crossed by beam at a hot white center, breathing slowly. Drag to steer it and stretch its blades, tap to strike the center, double-tap to switch between GOLD and BLUE.

title: Every Tiny Grain
note: A column of refracted light: a violet blade with a hot white core and pink fringing at its edges, breathing on a slow swell of low end, dissolving into brightness and rebuilding. Drag to bend the blade, tap to strike a bloom, double-tap to hold the bloom at its peak.

title: The Board Is Listening
note: His statement as an instrument: systems that turn signals, joysticks, EEG, audio, into light and motion. Below, a dark panel with three labeled inputs, STICK, BRAIN, SOUND, each drawing its own live trace; above, one particle field, the light those signals become. Tap STICK and the field steers smoothly where the control points, with inertia. Tap BRAIN and the field stutters and blooms in erratic bursts, as if thinking. Tap SOUND and it pulses radially on a beat. Switching morphs the field's character over two seconds: one field, three nervous systems. Drag to feed the active input; draw wild zigzags into BRAIN for wilder bursts, circle steadily into SOUND for a steady pulse. Double-tap the field and all three argue at once. The traces never lie: they draw the actual control signals driving the light above them.

title: Until Observed
note: His first sketch, superposition: a particle in all its states at once until observed. A field of particles drifts in the void, each one rendered as a smear of four ghost positions, everywhere it could be, shimmering, never settling. Touch it and you become the observer: a collapse wavefront spreads outward from your finger at a visible speed, and particles it passes snap into single sharp white points, the field crystallizing into hard certainty around your hand. A tiny readout at the bottom names the state. Lift your finger and the certainty dissolves over a few seconds, the points smearing back into their ghost-clouds. Tap collapses one pinpoint star in the fog. Double-tap observes everything at once, two seconds of total sharpness, then full release into maybe. The collapse is beautiful, and it is also a loss: the sharp points are lonelier than the clouds.

title: How the Music Looks
note: The KLSR method: audio first, then visuals that look how the music sounds, with fixed coupling rules, the low end driving brightness, the snare controlling feedback, every piece progressing from quiet to a culmination of noise. This one performs that arc live. It opens on a single dim line breathing in the black. Over about ninety seconds the line thickens into filaments, the filaments bloom into a pale-violet field, and the field saturates into beautiful noise, then exhales back to the line. Drag sideways to conduct it: rightward rushes the build, leftward pulls it back to a whisper, and a flick carries momentum. Tap strikes the snare, one sharp feedback bloom. Double-tap holds the progression frozen mid-breath for six seconds. A thin arc at the bottom marks where you are between quiet and noise. Hold it at the edge of noise as long as you like; the quiet line is as beautiful as the climax, and the arc needs both ends.

title: 001 to 108
note: His spring discipline: 108 numbered daily sketches, and this is the sketchbook itself. One sketch fills the frame at a time, a small running system in the same monochrome hand, waveform, burst, matrix, osc, flock, pulse, and every twenty seconds the book advances: 001, 002, 003. The number and title sit at the top in amber, the only color, because the counting is the work; a thin rail along the bottom marks your place in the 108. Drag sideways to scrub through the book, the sketches playing live under your finger; tap to hold one and study it; double-tap to leap somewhere random. Every number is stable: sketch 015 always looks like sketch 015. Some are strong and some are duds, sparse little pixel and dot studies that barely move. The duds stay in. The lab keeps its failures, and that is its honesty.

title: Noisy Nebula
note: His Full System, the entire patch exposed: four layers compose one finished image, an indigo particle nebula with a pale-violet core, an ice-blue filament web, magenta feedback smears, and a faint grain finish, and every layer has its own voice. Along the left edge, four thin labeled faders, NEBULA, WEB, SMEAR, GRAIN, plus a MASTER strip along the bottom: drag a fader to ride that layer in and out of the composite and the mix, live. Drag on the field itself to scrub the nebula's rotation and bend the smear. Tap a strip to solo its layer for five seconds. Double-tap the field to hold the whole mix frozen for a breath. The finished piece is never finished: it is a system you conduct, and muting all but one layer shows you the skeleton it blooms from.

title: Oscilloscope Music
note: The oscilloscope-music tradition, Fenderson's n-spheres: seven white spheres orbit a common center, their positions driven by two detuned oscillators, left channel as X, right channel as Y, so the sound is the picture. Their trails persist like phosphor, weaving rosettes, knots and near-circles that never quite repeat as the frequency ratio drifts in and out of phase near simple harmonics. The readout at the bottom tells you the ratio, because the number is the honesty. Drag horizontally to bend the ratio and warp the choreography, the drone you hear bending with it; drag vertically to offset the phase and knot the rosettes. Release and the ratio relaxes home toward a harmonic. Tap strikes a new shared phase; double-tap locks the ratio for a perfect ten-second loop. Ear and eye stay locked because there is only one signal.

title: Hairball
note: His neuroscience, drawn by itself: a hundred nodes drift on slow orbits inside a slowly rotating tangled ball, edges forming and dissolving between whichever nodes drift within reach. At rest it is dim and quiet, grey on black, a brain thinking almost nothing. Touch it and you become the electrode: nodes near your finger fire hot white, and the firing propagates along the edges like a seizure wave before settling back to rest over a few seconds. Slow drags raise gentle local waves; fast drags raise cascades. Tap strikes a single node and its neighbors answer. Double-tap silences the whole network for a breath, then it wakes node by node. A small readout counts the firing; most of the time it reads almost zero, and that quiet is what makes a cascade matter.

title: Murmuration
note: His boids, live: a few hundred white arrowheads on pure black, moving through three breathing phases on a slow loop. First they scatter into loose drifting streams; then they converge into a dense vertical vortex swirling at center; then the vortex loosens into a compact horizontal flock streaming like starlings. A small readout at the bottom names the phase. Drag and your finger becomes a gravity well: the flock streams in and orbits it, tighter the faster you move. Release and the well dissolves while the cycle resumes where it left off. Tap fires a shockwave through the flock; double-tap locks the current phase until you release it. Pure monochrome, one flock, no color anywhere: every bit of the beauty is the flock's own motion, and the sound, if you enable it, only narrates the phase, never leads it.

title: 9,500 Kilometers
note: Her telematic loop, Taipei and Switzerland answering each other. One square, two stages split by a faint seam: on the left, Taipei, warm dark and dense with amber particle weather; on the right, Switzerland, cold dark and sparse with ice-blue filaments. A signal loop runs between them: a bright pulse leaves one side, takes four real seconds to cross the seam, and arrives transformed, cooled and thinned into Switzerland, warmed and densified into Taipei, and the far side answers in its own time. Drag on either stage to play that city's voice into the loop; tap for one struck pulse; double-tap holds both stages silent for a breath before the answering resumes. The delay is never shortened: the distance is the instrument, and neither city wins. There is no map and no readout; the seam and the four seconds carry all the geography there is.

title: Deep Inside the Board
note: "Listen to the whispers of ghosts deep inside my no-input mixing board." The screen is near-black: a faint hand-drawn circuit of deep-green feedback traces, and along them, tiny dim motes, the ghosts, drifting. You cannot quite see them until you touch, and the touch they want is the quietest one: drag slowly near a trace and its ghosts wake, brightening toward phosphor green, their whisper-tones rising to the edge of hearing. Move fast and you scare them: the trace goes dark and silent for a while. Tap gently and the nearest ghost answers alone. Double-tap and they all converge toward your point and glow together, a quiet choir, then disperse. Haste is punished and stillness rewarded; the discovery of this is the tutorial, and the tone is tenderness, not haunting.

title: Lockdown Mixer
note: Her lockdown-era circuit-bent video mixers, playable. The screen shows a slow abstract feed, phosphor green and amber bands and a pulsing circle, that is constantly being bent: scanlines crawl, chroma smears magenta at the edges, horizontal hold slips in slice groups, sync tears and re-locks. Drag sideways to bend the hold under your finger; drag vertically to roll the sync; tap for a chroma slap. Double-tap loses sync entirely: the picture rolls free for five seconds, then crashes back to lock with a low thump. Let go and the mixer re-locks for a moment, then starts dirtying itself again on its own, because clean is the exception and dirty is its nature. The sound is the machine's electrical voice: a faint CRT whine and mains buzz under filtered noise. Analog breakage only; there is no footage and nothing to watch but the bending.

title: Tape That Has Since Been Lost
note: "The roughness, haze, and subtle instability of the tape became an essential part of the sound." An amber tape-line unspools across the black, carrying its white recording marks, and a playhead rides it. Every pass wears the tape: marks smear, the line wobbles with wow and flutter, dropouts eat holes, hiss blooms at the edges. Drag to scrub, and scrubbing wears it faster, slow hands gentle, fast hands cruel. Tap drops the needle for one clean play. Double-tap flips the tape and plays it backwards at double cost. Wear is one-way; nothing heals. When the recording is gone, only hiss remains, and then, quietly, a new tape loads while the counter keeps counting: PLAYS and WEAR, printed small at the corner, because the counting is the honesty. The decay is not a failure. The decay is the voice of every lost tape.

title: ROOTS
note: Her ROOTS duo with Vir Torres: butoh and flamenco meeting a no-input mixing board, a process of mutual listening. Two fields share the square and cannot be separated. The body, an ember mass grounded in the lower frame, is yours: slow drags move it like butoh, heavy and deep; fast drags strike it like flamenco heels, red flashes the machine catches and recirculates as green ripples. The machine, phosphor feedback filaments over the whole frame, never stops, not even when you do. They modulate each other continuously: the machine's flares sharpen the body's strikes, the body's strikes push the machine toward a howl, the filaments bend around the body's mass like water around a stone. Double-tap releases the body to stillness, corpse-quiet, while the machine plays on alone: the loneliest state, and the most beautiful. Neither leads. The coupling is the piece.

title: Somewhere in Taipei
note: Her Outer Pulsation series: guerrilla noise gigs in Taipei's underpasses, the concrete as the hall. This is an underpass you can play: a perspective vault of fourteen pillars marching to a vanishing point, sodium pools dim on the concrete, the ghosts of editions past glowing faintly green on their pillars. Drag across the vault to strike it: each pillar answers with its own low resonance, bright and short for fast hands, deep and dwelling for slow ones. Cross all fourteen in one pass and the gig is complete: a new edition glyph is archived on the left wall, permanent for the session. Tap tests one pillar. Double-tap starts a fresh edition. Play continuously for about three minutes and the police-tolerance clock ends the gig for you, fading the vault quiet before the next edition reboots. No score, no targets: it is a gig, not a test.

title: Held Back
note: Her arc from Berserk to ghost-whispers, held in one mass. A dense coil of red filaments sits at the center of the black, a system entirely capable of violence, played at whisper volume. Drag and you build pressure: the coil tightens, brightens, begins to tremble, amber highlights sparking at the highest strain, the sound climbing toward a howl that is hard-capped and never arrives. Release, and the pressure bleeds off over a long exhale, the mass loosening into grey ghost shimmer that drifts outward and fades. Tap strikes one point of the coil, a brief red flare. Double-tap bleeds it to near-black and it slowly re-coils over twenty seconds, because the coil always re-forms. The explosion never happens. The restraint is the composition, and it is beautiful precisely because of what it refuses.

title: No Input
note: Her instrument: a mixing desk with its outputs patched into its inputs, nothing else connected. This field is the same: rivers of phosphor-green signal stream across desk black, depositing energy into the very field that steers them, feeding on themselves and nothing else. Sometimes the loop finds a stable tone, a slow breathing band of light; sometimes it howls, a burst of feedback red the system takes seconds, or half a minute, to tame. You never command it; you accompany it. Drag and your amber fader-line bends the loop for a moment, gaining up locally, late and in the system's own way, before the loop swallows your touch. Tap for one clean pulse and watch it recirculate for many seconds. Double-tap drains the loop toward silence, and it re-boots itself from its own noise floor. Nothing enters from outside, ever.

title: Paper Through the Machine
note: From The Assassin's score: paper talismans in a period world, heard through electronics. Three flat paper-cut figures, a person, a horse, a bird, folk silhouettes with punched pattern holes, drift at different depths in blackness, small in the void. Periodically an electronic scan passes through: inside its pale teal band the paper turns translucent, its edges fray into static, and its cut-out holes bloom gold; then the band moves on and the paper restores itself, whole. The scan is not destruction; it is the machine reading the paper, and the restore always comes. Drag and the scan follows your hand, reading whatever you cross. Tap and a new figure cuts itself into being and joins the drift. Double-tap reseeds. Tradition and machine take turns occupying the same body, and neither wins.

title: Whose Space-Time
note: His scoring method as a place: "I try to enter the psychological state of the characters, or the imagination of the space-time environment of any story." Three characters live here, not as figures but as worlds. The Prisoner: cold iron marks in slow heavy currents, dense and low. The Drifter: temple gold, sparse, quick, darting. The Dreamer: dusk violet, faint, dissolving as it drifts. Three quiet sigils rest along the bottom edge, a bar, a zigzag, a circle. Tap one and the whole piece cross-dissolves into that space-time over four seconds, palette, viscosity, density and sound register together; entering is a dissolve, never a cut. Dragging feels different inside each: heavy lag, skittish scatter, a wake that dissolves behind you. Double-tap releases you back to the dark to choose again. You are always inside exactly one of them, and it colors everything.

title: No Computer in the Mix
note: His discipline, kept literally: "I try to use a synthesizer to compose music directly without using a computer to mix it." An empty black field; the first gesture is the first mark. Drag and your path is drawn as both form and sound in the same instant: the line's curvature is the pitch contour, its speed the brightness, its weight the body of the tone. Fast is bright, thin and high; slow is dark, heavy and low. Lift your finger and the line sustains, dimming from temple gold to umber as it decays over twenty seconds; draw again and the new line harmonizes or clashes with the fading ones, and where two lines cross, a small steel-blue shimmer marks their beating. One line at a time, the loudest, burns crimson. Tap strikes a gong-dot. Double-tap clears the field for a fresh take. There is no grid, no scale, no correction anywhere: wobble stays wobble, and dissonance is allowed to be beautiful.

title: Remake This
note: Bioerosion's gesture: the stems, released for anyone to remake. The piece ships as four independent layers, a deep teal drone-terrain, a warm murmur thread, a silver grain field, a cold pulse grid, composited in that order, each running on its own clock, none syncing to another. The composition is whatever you arrange. Four thin colored strips edge the frame, one per stem. Tap a strip to mute its stem, sound and image together. Drag from a strip to scrub that stem's phase and speed; leave it running backwards while the others run forward. Double-tap a strip to freeze the stem mid-frame, a chop that stays until you release it. There is no save, no share, no canonical form: the remake exists in your session, and when you close the page it is gone, like a mix played once in a room.

title: Kind, Ordinary, Happy, Pure
note: Millennium Mambo's signature, abstracted: he murmurs "kind, ordinary, happy, pure people" over fine regular beats, the whispered human scale inside the machine scale. Here the machine is a rigid grid of vertical beat-lines pulsing at a strict 120 beats per minute, cold steel blue, relentless, never glitching. Through it wanders one soft warm trace, the murmur: a breathing bone-colored blob with a fading trail, never synced to the grid, never on the beat, never absorbed. Drag and you become the murmur, your path drawn free and unquantized. Tap and the grid flares at your column while the murmur shivers. Double-tap reseeds the wander. With sound on, the pulses are cold and regular and the breath tone follows your path's curvature, carefully never landing on the beat. The tension between them is the entire piece.

title: Recorded From Somewhere
note: The xianchang poetics: a documentary of where the piece is running. Six hundred small marks fill the frame edge to edge, dots and dashes whose density, warmth and drift come from the place itself: its ambient swell and lull, its slow day turning warm to cool and back. A loud bright hour and a quiet dark one look like different places, because they are. Nothing is labeled; there are no meters and no clocks, the place reads in the marks, and everything changes like weather, never like a switch. Watch it record. Drag to stir the recording into a slow swirl that settles. Tap for a collision, the Three Gorges boats translated to light. Double-tap reseeds the place. The shipped piece listens to a simulated room, because a gallery page asks for no microphone; the place it documents is the one it imagines, completely.

title: The DJ Replaces the Orchestra
note: Lim Giong's Live Movies: silent archival footage re-scored live, except there is no footage. A letterboxed band carries drawn silhouettes, a boat, figures, a rooftop, a bicycle, drifting like found film under grain, scratches and flicker. You are the DJ: drag and your gesture re-scores the archive, faster hands pushing the grain coarser, the tint warmer, the flicker harder, the drift quicker. Stop, and the archive goes cold and quiet, blue-grey, near-frozen mid-frame. Tap for a hard cut to a new arrangement, with a soft thump. Double-tap reseeds the archive into another era. Nothing here is beat-synced; the cuts follow your hands, not a tempo. It must read as worn, anonymous, found, because that is the music's memory.

title: Sound Is the Image
note: Lim Giong's stereo picture, sound standing AS the image: a dark field whose only contents are a sound made visible. A low drone draws a terrain of slow teal ridges across the lower frame; a gong strike throws concentric gold rings; a whispered thread of bone white wanders the upper third, brightening with the sound's high energy; deep down, a crimson sub-bass bloom you feel more than see. There is no scenery and no decoration: the visuals have no independent existence, they are the audio's body. Drag horizontally to play the terrain like a record, scrubbing the drone's pitch while the ridges redraw from it. Tap for a gong whose pitch is set by the tap's height. Double-tap reseeds the base tone. What you hear is what you see, because they are the same signal.

title: Silence Remembers
note: The Ekholux end-state: "A world unraveled by language. A space where sound takes shape, and silence remembers." A wireframe tower stands in blackness, three hundred vertices of thin pale lines, one of them crimson: the keystone. The tower is held together by a hum, and the hum is you: move, and your motion sustains it, lines warming amber, vertices holding home. Stop, and within seconds the drone decays; the vertices let go and drift apart like slow snow into a point-cloud, the keystone drifting last. Tap the keystone and it pulses, briefly re-gathering its neighbors. There is no repair button and no integrity meter; attention is the structure, and the state reads in the geometry. Double-tap raises a new tower. The deluge is not failure. The deluge is the piece.

title: Folded From Pixels
note: Huang's A Thousand Cranes: "Each crane in this digital sky is folded not from paper, but from pixels, carrying the same hope: for peace, for healing." A night sky, one pale moon, and a murmuration of origami cranes, each a flat dark polygon bird whose crease pattern glows neon teal; one in twenty carries a gold wing-tip. The flock banks and turns as one body over the empty lower sky. Every forty seconds or so a fold-pulse ripples through them: a crane folds itself flat and unfolds again, the heartbeat of the flock. Tap to release a new crane at your fingertip, folding into being and joining the turn; drag a wind gust through them and watch the body bend and settle. Double-tap reseeds the flock. They never land. The sky is their element, and the fold is their pulse.

title: Gritty and Drippy
note: The Chalkroom again, but under the no-text rule: Huang and Anderson's hand-drawn universe with the words taken out, leaving the handwriting itself. A black void fills with chalk glyph-strokes, procedural scribbles that cluster like lines on a page at three depths, suggesting writing everywhere and resolving into letters nowhere. Drag and you fly: the field parallaxes against your hand, near marks sweeping past. Fly fast and the strokes near your path cannot hold their form: they shed chalk drips, tears that fall and fade, the signature of paint at speed. Tap and a pressure wave trembles the nearby marks into a burst of grit. Double-tap reseeds the field. With sound on, the flight is an airy rush that rises with your speed. Gritty and drippy, never brittle and bright, and not one letter in it.

title: One Platform
note: The Ekholux track builder's promise, kept small: "BUILD. RIDE. ENJOY. Start with a single platform. Build it into your own insane route." A black void, one neon platform, one small yellow rider rolling on it under gravity. That is all you get, and it is enough to start. Tap to place more platforms, snapped to a loose grid with a slight tilt; drag and your hand becomes a gravity well, bending the rider's arc as it launches off edges and lands, hopefully, on your architecture. Its trail fades behind it; complete a circuit and the route's ghost stays in the dark. If the rider falls out of the world, it loops back to the last platform it touched: the route is a closed world and nothing is lost. Double-tap clears back to one platform. Yours is the only light in the void, so build it well.

title: Angle. Reflect. Release.
note: Ekholux's puzzle mechanic in Huang's own words: "In Ekholux, you shape reality with resonance. Angle. Reflect. Release. Every echo leads you closer to the truth." A dark void, a few concrete rails in an open triangle, and sound made visible: flick to launch an amber sound sphere from the bottom edge; it bounces off the rails, and every bounce sheds an expanding resonance ring. Where two rings overlap, the overlap glows teal, resonance made visible. Tap a rail to rotate it fifteen degrees and change the acoustics of the whole space; spheres that wander into the dark portal fade out of the world. Double-tap reseeds the rails. No score, no timer, no levels: the geometry is the instrument, and the truth it leads to is just the shape of the room, heard.

title: Final Ten Seconds
note: The Ekholux Ekho: creatures that repeat their final ten seconds, trapped in time's last breath. On a black field above a grief-blue floor-line, five pale figures trace their own ten-second paths forever: one pacing, one reaching up, one kneeling, their trails lingering as fading chalk. A small deep-red marker pulses each time a loop closes. You can walk among them but never interrupt them; the loops are monuments, not obstacles. Drag a closed loop of your own, finished within ten seconds, and the piece keeps it: your gesture becomes a sixth ekho, replayed alongside the others for as long as the page is open. Tap for a closure marker; double-tap releases everyone and reseeds. With sound on, each ekho hums its own low tone. It is a memorial you can join, briefly, on its terms.

title: The Measurement Breaks In
note: Huang's Bodyless mechanism without the photorealism: a calm slate field with a pale moon, progressively invaded by crystalline facets, the mechanical order compressing the world into computable forms. The shatter starts at one seed point in the lower-left and spreads like frost across four hundred cells, each turning to a flat facet shade with a bright neon edge; somewhere inside it, always, one crimson cell, the donor thread. Drag and the measurement accelerates around your hand. Tap a facet to hold it still, a pause in the decay. But the spread is capped: it decelerates and stops at the edge of almost, the moon never quite consumed. Double-tap reseeds the frost. With sound on, every breaking facet ticks, quietly, like the world being counted.

title: A Stranger's Cornea
note: From Huang's Samsara: "Perhaps we are only borrowing each other's eyes for a brief passage through this world." A flat generative landscape, sage hills, a few tree forms, a low amber sun, drifts on a near-black field, and you never see it raw: two translucent corneal lenses float through it on slow orbits, bending everything seen through them, each with its own warp. A thin ring around each lens thins as the ten-minute loan runs down; when it ends, the lens dissolves. Drag to move a borrowed eye and feel the hills refract; tap and the lenses blink-swap places, the world suddenly bent by the other cornea. Double-tap begins a new loan. No eyeballs, no horror: this is a gift economy of vision, and the tenderness is the technology.

title: Six Feet of Granulation
note: The talking stick: a six-foot baton wired to granular synthesis, built with Interval Research for the Moby Dick tour, where the motion of the stick is the instrument and there are no buttons and no keys. A long amber baton lies diagonal across a dark stage in a field of about 120 chalk grains. Drag to wield it: move slowly and the grains gather toward you into loose clusters that almost form words, then think better of it; move fast and they scatter into noise, reddening at the peak of the swing. Tap for one clear struck tone at the tip; double-tap reseeds the field. With sound on (first touch), the granulation is real: dozens of tiny grains of tone whose density and brightness follow your hand's velocity. It is a controller, not a wand. Nothing sparkles. Things just barely, almost, gather.

title: Ventriloquist's Violin
note: The self-playing violin, 1975: a violin with a loudspeaker inside it, playing prerecorded music while she played live, a duet with herself. She called it a ventriloquist's dummy. Two violins face each other on a black stage: at left the machine, wood-toned, a speaker cone pulsing where its heart should be, playing its fixed looping phrase forever and shifting key every sixteen passes; at right yours, in chalk. Drag across it to bow: stroke speed is volume, position is pitch, politely quantized to the machine's key unless you bow hard, and then it detunes and you are clashing on purpose. Tap and the dummy answers, quoting your last phrase back transposed. Double-tap reseeds its loop. It never stops playing itself. That, she would tell you, is exactly what makes it a partner and not an accompaniment.

title: Until the Ice Gives
note: Duets on Ice, 1974: Anderson performed standing in ice skates frozen into blocks of ice, playing violin against a self-playing machine violin, telling stories until the ice melted. This piece keeps her clock. Two ice blocks with blades frozen into them sit under a looping machine staff; drag to play the second violin, your white line against the amber machine phrase, and tap for a deadpan story fragment. But the melt runs from the first second and never pauses: over four minutes the blocks shrink, the drips quicken, the pool spreads. When the last ice is gone the machine stops mid-phrase and the stage goes black except the meltwater line. No outro, no replay button. The ending is not a failure state. The ending is the piece. Double-tap afterwards, if you want another performance, and bring new ice.

title: Cover Your Ears to Hear
note: The Handphone Table, 1978: a long wooden table, sound conducted through bone. Put your elbows on the worn spots, cover your ears, and the sound enters your skull; the body is the speaker. Here the table waits in the dark, two elbow-rests glowing on their pale worn patches, and above it, nothing: the piece is silent until you perform the listening gesture. Two touch points, one on each rest, held: then whisper-blue sound glyphs bloom in the darkness and a close, lowpassed murmur starts, as if inside your head. Lean by shifting your hands and the sound leans with you. Lift one hand and everything cuts instantly, mid-bloom. One finger alone only brightens a rest. The table refuses to perform without the gesture, because the intimacy is not a feature. It is the whole instrument.

title: Flying Through the Lists
note: The Chalkroom, Anderson and Hsin-Chien Huang's VR of hand-drawn words: a black universe of chalk lettering, gritty and drippy, never brittle and bright. You fly forward through it and the flight never stops. The words drift at every depth, ANGELS OF ARTIFICE, SAY TO MYSELF, OCEAN, SUGAR CANDY BABY, MONO TASKING, each drawn the way chalk actually behaves, doubled edges, uneven weight, drips hanging off the letters. Steer with a drag to choose your line; fly through a word and it is collected, flashing ember and joining a litany list down the right edge, with a soft pluck if you have tapped for sound. Tap near a word and it bursts into chalk dust. Double-tap reseeds the field. No neon, no sparkle: her particles are dust and snow, and the list you gather is the level.

title: Fenway Speaks
note: Fenway Bergamot, Anderson's audio drag: her voice dropped eight semitones into a pompous male alter ego who footnotes everything she says. The screen splits in two: above, her lines in thin white type, flat observations about the late ferry and the six-o'clock dog; below, a beat later, his replies in heavier grey type, correcting her. Fog is not weather. Fog is the harbor declining to comment. Between the registers sits his mark, a moustache on a paper chip, and it twitches whenever he speaks. The script is original, six exchanges, and the two voices never agree; by the last pairs his pomposity thins into something sadder. Drag to scrub the conversation, tap and he interrupts with an aside, double-tap reshuffles the script. Played straight, the way she always played him.

title: Greek Chorus
note: The "O Superman" mechanism, kept in strict black and white: one syllable, "Ha", looped on a Harmonizer 1,246 times across the record, a Greek chorus of one voice made many. At center, a single large Ha pulses on a rock-steady 84 BPM metronome, and every pulse sheds a faint echo-ghost that drifts outward and fades, the chorus accumulating around its own floor. The background tint alternates between two near-blacks, chord to chord. Across the lower third, a deadpan litany advances one phrase every sixteen pulses, written new in her register: say it once and it is a joke, say it forever and it is a law. Drag to pull the ghosts into tighter or looser orbits; tap to advance the litany; double-tap to reshuffle it. The Ha never varies. Tap once for sound and it never will.

title: Gesture Scrubs the Buffer
note: Anderson's tape-bow violin, 1977: horsehair replaced by a strip of prerecorded tape, the strings replaced by a playback head, so that bowing is not expression, it is playback control. A graphite tape strip crosses a dark stage carrying one recorded sentence as a chalk waveform: "I want to tell you a story about a story." Drag the bow-handle along the strip and you scrub the sentence: fast drags stretch the waveform thin, reverse drags compress and mirror it, and dragging across the strip bends its pitch, the whole phrase warping under your hand while the amber contact point glows. Tap loads the second recorded sentence; double-tap reseeds a new deadpan line from the pool. You will never change what it says. You only ever change how it is said. That distinction is the instrument.

title: The Static Stare
note: Warhol's Screen Test, 1966: four minutes, one shot, a face that does not blink. An original portrait fills the frame in high-contrast black and white, half of it fallen into shadow, eyes open and looking straight out at you. Almost nothing happens, and the almost is everything: a breath at half a percent, the shadow edge creeping a few pixels over minutes, a jaw that shifts once. Blinks are scheduled every twenty to forty seconds, and every time, the eyelids tense, tremble, and do not close. The eyes never close. Watching is the interaction; the discipline is the piece. Stay for the whole take. It can tell whether you did.

title: The Doot-Doot Choir
note: The Transformer treatment: overexposed white, a gold banner, and the most famous walk in rock and roll drawn as a stepped bassline crossing the frame at its own unhurried pace, forever. Beneath it, street tableaux in Reed's flat register, written new for this piece: a man selling umbrellas who does not look up, a dog waiting outside a closed theater, two men losing an argument to a cup of coffee. Along the banner, little doot-doot-doot glyphs repeat like a candy stripe, the sweetest chorus ever committed to tape. Drag up or down to walk to a different stretch of street: the tableau changes, the doots thicken or thin, and the bassline never, ever hurries. A thin rainbow strip seals the bottom edge, exactly where Warhol's factory would have put it.

title: Multiply-Exposed
note: The Magic and Loss reliquary, rebuilt as a breathing portrait. The words MAGIC AND LOSS repeat along all four edges like a border on a shrine, alchemical glyphs burn red in the corners, and at center an original portrait, no photograph, no likeness, exists in four exposures at once: sunglasses band, hand resting on the heart, paint-stripped ruin behind the head. Each exposure's opacity breathes on its own slow period, so the lead keeps passing from one registration to another and the face never resolves into a single image; grief does not sit still for its portrait. Tap and the lead shifts, slowly, the way attention actually moves. Nothing jumps, nothing reveals. It just keeps almost becoming someone.

title: The Locked Groove
note: The last side of Metal Machine Music ends in a locked groove: a 1.8-second loop cut so the needle can never leave, the record's ending chosen as an eternity. This piece does the same. For twelve seconds a form gathers out of near-black, the White Light/White Heat ghost treatment: a faint effigy, crown, sockets, jaw, drawn just above black, with one highlight edge arriving last; you have to look twice to be sure it is there. Then it locks. The final gesture, a slow 1.8-second breath through the form's tones, repeats forever: no outro, no fade, no resolution, ever. A small infinity sign sits in the corner like the side-4 label. Watch-only. The piece is not stuck. It chose this.

title: Peel Slowly and See
note: Warhol's instruction for the Velvet Underground & Nico sleeve, rebuilt as a mechanism on an original form: a bold screen-printed composition in yellow and black on white, a peel tab at its corner, and the order set small in the corner: PEEL SLOWLY AND SEE. So peel: drag across the form and the top layer tears back along your path with a jagged edge, and underneath is not a gag but a second finished artwork in pink and black, a starburst, a ring field, a scallop sea; there are three hidden works, and they are real. The peel stays peeled; there is no reset button. Press and hold to lay a fresh sheet down and move to the next hidden piece. The banana is not here. The instruction was always the artwork.

title: The Feedback Machine
note: Metal Machine Music as a machine that plays itself: two wave systems face each other across a black field like Reed's guitars leaned against their amplifiers in a garment-district loft at 5 a.m. The left and right families run different patterns, the famous stereo split, and where they collide at center, new harmonics bloom in bright chrome knots, computed from the actual sum.
